<h4><strong>Upcoming Chrome Enterprise Core updates</strong></h4>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome client certificate support on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Built-in client certificate support in Chrome for iOS enables managed users to securely authenticate to corporate resources using mutual TLS (<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/mtls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>mTLS</u></a>). Historically, iOS isolated certificates within the system store accessible only to built-in Apple apps, but this launch allows Chrome to provision and manage its own hardware-backed certificates independently. By integrating with the iOS Secure Enclave for non-exportable private key storage, Chrome provides a high-assurance identity signal specifically for Zero Trust environments using Microsoft Entra ID and Conditional Access. These credentials are provisioned within the work-managed Chrome profile and are inaccessible to other applications or personal profiles on the device.</p>

    <p>To implement this feature, admins must enable the <strong>Apply supported user settings to Chrome on iOS toggle</strong> in the Google Admin console and configure the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ProvisionManagedClientCertificateForBrowser" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ProvisionManagedClientCertificateForBrowser</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ProvisionManagedClientCertificateForUser" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ProvisionManagedClientCertificateForUser</u></a> policies to initiate issuance and rotation. Finally, the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AutoSelectCertificateForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AutoSelectCertificateForUrls</u></a> policy should be used to automate certificate selection for designated corporate domains to ensure a seamless authentication flow.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 148 on iOS - Feature rolls out gradually</strong>.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Managed profile reporting support&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise Core is launching cloud profile reporting support for the <strong>Apps &amp; extension usage</strong> report and the <strong>Versions</strong> report in the Google Admin console.</p>

    <p>On the <strong>Apps &amp; extension usage</strong> report, admins will be able to see a new total install count for managed profiles (work profiles). They will be able to see which extensions have the most installs across all managed profiles.</p>

    <p>On the <strong>Versions</strong> report, admins will be able to see the total number of managed profiles running each version of Chrome. For example, they will be able to see if managed profiles are using older versions of Chrome.</p>

    <p>To enable cloud profile reporting for both of these reports, admins have to enable the existing <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CloudProfileReportingEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CloudProfileReportingEnabled</u></a> policy. If you have already turned on Managed profile reporting, the reports will automatically start reporting the data.</p>

    <p>How to find these reports? In the Admin console, navigate to <strong>Chrome browser &gt; Reports &gt; Apps &amp; extensions usage</strong> or <strong>Chrome browser &gt; Reports &gt; Versions</strong>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 148 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>: The profile reporting on the Versions report will be available to Chrome Enterprise Trusted Testers.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><p>&nbsp;</p>

<h4><strong>Upcoming Chrome Enterprise Premium updates</strong></h4>

<p><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Enterprise Connectors API&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise will soon expand programmatic management for <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/12166576" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise Connectors</u></a>. This update will introduce resources to define and assign connector configurations, complementing the existing connector policies to allow administrators to manage the full life-cycle of these integrations at scale.</p>

    <p>Previously, configuring Service Providers was a manual process in the Google Admin console. This update enables automation, which helps reduce manual errors and improve the efficiency of managing integrations with third-party security solutions.</p>

    <p>Administrators can now use the Chrome Management API to manage ConnectorConfiguration resources (defining the provider). Connector Selection is managed via the Chrome Policy API, enabling the assignment of these configurations to Organizational Units or Groups. This works in tandem with existing Policy API settings for event reporting and content analysis, including policies such as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnSecurityEventEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnSecurityEventEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnPrintEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnPrintEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseRealTimeUrlCheckMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseRealTimeUrlCheckMode</u></a>. For technical details, developers should refer to the <a href="https://developers.google.com/chrome/management/reference/rest" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Management API</u></a> and <a href="https://developers.google.com/chrome/policy/reference/rest" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Policy API documentation</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 143 on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: This rollout adds support for programmatic management of Chrome Enterprise Connectors via a new API</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 148&nbsp;on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>: This rollout introduces the ConnectorConfiguration and ConnectorSelection resources, enabling the creation of service provider instances and their assignment to organizational units.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><strong>&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Drag support for data controls&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome will enhance&nbsp;the Data Controls framework by extending security enforcement to drag-and-drop operations across Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, and Android to ensure consistency with existing clipboard policies. Admins will be able to&nbsp;manage this behavior through the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DataControlsRules" rel="noopener" target="_blank">DataControlsRules</a> policy, though any WARN verdict will automatically escalate to a BLOCK to prevent a warning dialog from interrupting the interactive drag loop.</p>

    <p>When an action is restricted, users will see the new <strong>ClipboardDragBlock</strong> dialog or an Android blocking modal stating that dragging content is not allowed on the site. This update will close&nbsp;a critical data exfiltration gap using local evaluation to maintain performance and privacy. Organizations should test these rules using the <strong>DataControlsDragEnforcement</strong> feature flag and the <code>chrome://policy/test</code> page.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 148&nbsp;on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows - Feature rolls out gradually</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Enterprise extension DOM activity telemetry&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This enterprise-only feature provides security auditing for Chrome Extensions by creating a high-fidelity pipeline that monitors risky behavior. It specifically focuses on identifying Code Injection (execution risks) and Data Access (theft risks) occurring between web pages and extensions. Verified signals are filtered to ensure browser performance is not impacted, and they are ultimately transmitted using the Chrome real-time reporting pipeline for Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system analysis.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 148 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows - Early preview available to Chrome Enterprise Trusted Tester</strong>.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New policy setting for DataControlRules&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome is enhancing the existing <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DataControlsRules" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DataControlsRules</u></a> policy by introducing a new setting labeled <strong>Pasting restrictions across management boundaries</strong>. This update provides admins with a context-based mechanism to block against sensitive web content being pasted into or from managed Chrome profiles without requiring specific source or destination URLs.</p>

    <p>As of Chrome 148, admins could use a simple checkboxes in the Google Admin Console to establish data boundaries for Incognito mode, other Chrome profiles, and applications other than Chrome. This enhancement is designed to strengthen data loss prevention for Chrome Enterprise Premium customers by preventing corporate data exfiltration into unmanaged environments. Users will receive immediate on-browser notifications if a paste action is restricted, ensuring real-time awareness of organizational security policies.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>
        <p><strong>Chrome 148 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, macOS, Windows - Feature rolls out gradually</strong>.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><strong>&nbsp; &nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Hardening against local policy tampering&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Local settings on bring-your-own-device (BYOD) devices can sometimes conflict with corporate policy settings. To address this potential security gap, policy conflict signals in Chrome now detect and report whenever corporate policies are being overridden by local policy. Chrome 145 integrates these new policy conflict signals from the managed Chrome profile into existing security reports, controlled by the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UserSecuritySignalsReporting" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UserSecuritySignalsReporting</u></a> policy.</p>

    <p>For more information on device reporting, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1698333#zippy=%2Creporting-policies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>View ChromeOS device list and details - Chrome Enterprise and Education Help</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 144 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Detection and reporting of policy conflict metadata begins.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 145 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>: Visibility into Chrome policy hardening signals via the Devices API becomes available.</li>
      <li>Chrome 150 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Admin console UI is updated to display conflict signals and policy values begin reporting.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Current ChromeOS updates</h4>

<p><a id="chromeOSA147" name="chromeOSA147"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Class Tools activity logs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>For improved administrative oversight, Class Tools now generates activity logs. This feature provides administrators with a record of specific in-product actions, such as a teacher connecting to a student, sending content, or viewing a student's screen. The logs are designed to align with existing ChromeOS audit standards, creating a detailed event trail that can be used for troubleshooting and monitoring user activity within the domain.</p>

    <p>For more detail, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16982533"><u>Class Tools log events&nbsp; - Chrome Enterprise and Education Help</u></a>.</p>
  </li>

    <p>By the end of 2026, Admins will need to migrate from the legacy certificate enrollment solution to the new one leveraging the Certificate Provisioning API, which was launched back in ChromeOS M142 by the end of 2026.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For instructions, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11338941"><u>Configuring Certificate Provisioning for ChromeOS via SCEP - Chrome Enterprise and Education Help</u></a>.</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA147" name="upChromeOSA147"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Troubleshoot connectivity with ChromeOS Diagnostics&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS has a built-in <strong>Diagnostics</strong> app, which allows users to troubleshoot their issues. To open the Diagnostics app, use this key sequence:</p>

    <p><strong>&nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;[Ctrl] + Search Key + Esc</strong>&nbsp;</p>

    <p>ChromeOS 149 will add a <strong>Connectivity</strong> troubleshooting function to the <a href="https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/10566784" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Diagnostics app</a>, to help users diagnose connectivity problems to a pre-defined list of Google Services. This tool helps troubleshoot customer networking-related problems, such as the inability to access specific Google services.</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/px6lTT1LHSEqHuDw4QXKIkwmdEUsmua9O0_N3hVZPY3a1s-j6qE76HE1U3O0xEQ1YDmo=w895" width="2036" height="1688" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/px6lTT1LHSEqHuDw4QXKIkwmdEUsmua9O0_N3hVZPY3a1s-j6qE76HE1U3O0xEQ1YDmo"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB147" name="upChromeOSB147"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Updates blocked for certain ChromeOS Flex devices&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>From ChromeOS 150 onwards, we will begin blocking updates for devices unable to meet the minimum requirements for the Chrome Browser. This will affect devices using the following:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Intel and AMD graphics from 2010 and older&nbsp;</li>
      <li>Nvidia graphics from 2014 and older&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>This does not affect any <a href="https://support.google.com/chromeosflex/answer/11513094" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>certified devices</u></a>. If unexpected devices are affected, reach out to Google <a href="https://support.google.com/chromeosflex/answer/4594885" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS Flex support</u></a>.</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes &nbsp;</h2>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA146" name="chromeBrsrA146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>AI Mode and Lens enhancements&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Previously, in Chrome 143 on macOS and Windows, new AI Mode capabilities were integrated into Chrome browser. Users can access AI Mode directly from the <strong>New tab</strong> page and the address bar, allowing users to ask complex questions directly from where they start browsing. Admins can turn off these features (value 1) using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AIModeSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AIModeSettings</u></a> policy or by using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> (value 2). For more details, see this article in the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14443058#zippy=%2Cgemini-enterprise%2Cgoogle-lens%2Cai-mode:~:text=Google%20generative%20AI%20features%20available%20through%20Chrome" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center</u></a>.</p>

    <p>In Chrome 145, we rolled out the multi-tab context feature on AI Mode and Lens. Users can choose to share the contents of one or more of their open tabs, helping them ask questions, compare, summarize, and find information more efficiently. Admins can turn off these features (value 1) using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SearchContentSharingSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SearchContentSharingSettings</u></a> policy or by using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> (value 2). Also in Chrome 145 on Android and iOS, new AI Mode capabilities were integrated into Chrome browser.</p>

    <p>In Chrome 146, Google Drive files become available as context. Admins can turn off these features (value 1) using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SearchContentSharingSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SearchContentSharingSettings</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 143 on macOS, Windows: New AI Mode capabilities will be integrated into Chrome and can be controlled using <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AIModeSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AIModeSettings</u></a> policy or the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> policy.</li>
      <li>Chrome 145 on macOS, Windows: The multi-tab context feature will be available and can be controlled using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SearchContentSharingSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SearchContentSharingSettings</u></a> policy or <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> policy.</li>
      <li>Chrome 145 on Android, iOS: New AI Mode capabilities will gradually become available on Android and iOS.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on macOS, Windows</strong>: Google Drive files become available as context. Admins can turn off these features (value 1) using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SearchContentSharingSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SearchContentSharingSettings</u></a> policy.</li>
      <li>Chrome 147 on macOS, Windows: The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensDesktopNTPSearchEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensDesktopNTPSearchEnabled</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensRegionSearchEnabled"><u>LensRegionSearchEnabled</u></a> policies will be deprecated. Admins can use <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SearchContentSharingSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SearchContentSharingSettings</u></a> to control these features.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB146" name="chromeBrsrB146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Extended Autofill experience</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 146, some users can save and autofill additional types of data previously only available to users with <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/142893#zippy=%2Cturn-on-enhanced-autofill" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Enhanced autofill</u></a> enabled. Admins can control the feature using the existing <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AutofillAddressEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AutofillAddressEnabled</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AutofillPredictionSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AutofillPredictionSettings</u></a> policies.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong> - Feature rolls out gradually</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC146" name="chromeBrsrC146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Local network access restrictions</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 142 restricted the ability to make requests to the user's local network, gated behind a permission prompt. A local network request is any request from a public website to a local IP address or loopback, or from a local website (for example, intranet) to loopback.</p>

    <p>Gating the ability for websites to perform these requests behind a permission mitigates the risk of cross-site request forgery attacks against local network devices such as routers, and reduces the ability of sites to use these requests to fingerprint the user's local network.</p>

    <p>This permission is restricted to secure contexts. If granted, the permissions additionally relaxes mixed content blocking for local network requests (since many local devices are not able to obtain publicly trusted TLS certificates for various reasons).</p>

    <p>This work supersedes a prior effort called <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5737414355058688" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Private Network Access</u></a>, which used preflight requests to have local devices opt-in. For more information on this feature, see <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QQkqehw8umtAgz5z0um7THx-aoU251p705FbIQjDuGs/edit?usp=sharing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Adapting your website for new Local Network Access restrictions in Chrome</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Chrome 145 introduced more granular permissions for websites requesting access to a user's local network. The previous single local-network-access permission is being split into two distinct permissions:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>
        <p>local-network: Grants access to IP addresses in the local network space (for example, intranets, internal devices).</p>
      </li>
      <li>loopback-network: Grants access to loopback IP addresses (for example, localhost, 127.0.0.1).</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>The old local-network permission will remain as an alias, ensuring existing configurations and Permissions Policies continue to function as expected. This change provided both users and Admins with more precise control over how websites interact with internal network resources. Current enterprise policies managing local network access will not be affected by this change.</p>

    <p>Chrome 146 introduces two new enterprise policies for managing local network access restrictions: <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalNetworkAccessIpAddressSpaceOverrides" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalNetworkAccessIpAddressSpaceOverrides</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalNetworkAccessPermissionsPolicyDefaultEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalNetworkAccessPermissionsPolicyDefaultEnable</u></a>.&nbsp;These policies can be set using <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14749672" rel="noopener" target="_blank">custom configurations</a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 145 on Android, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia: The permission split is rolled out.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong>: Two new enterprise policies will be available for managing local network access restrictions:
        <ul>
          <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalNetworkAccessIpAddressSpaceOverrides" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalNetworkAccessIpAddressSpaceOverrides</u></a> could be used to mark IPv4 and IPv6 address blocks as public or private. IP ranges that are treated as public will not cause permission prompts when accessed by other pages. For example, CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10 can be marked as public. This is useful for certain VPN and proxy setups. Marking 0.0.0.0/0&nbsp; and ::/0 as public is equivalent to disabling the local network access restrictions.</li>
          <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalNetworkAccessPermissionsPolicyDefaultEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalNetworkAccessPermissionsPolicyDefaultEnabled</u></a> can be used to cause the LNA permission to be automatically delegated to iframes by the parent frame, without requiring explicit annotation of the child iframes. This is useful in situations where local network access is performed by an embedded SaaS tool inside of a different SaaS tool. This includes certain locally hosted documentation and knowledgebase softwares.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong> - Feature rolls out gradually</li>
      <li>Chrome 147 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Local Network Access restrictions expanded to include WebSocket and WebTransport connections.</li>
      <li>Chrome 152 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalNetworkAccessRestrictionsTemporaryOptOut" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalNetworkAccessRestrictionsTemporaryOptOut</u></a> policy will be removed.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrCC146" name="chromeBrsrCC146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Selective permission intervention</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 146 introduces <strong>Selective permission intervention</strong> that prevents advertising-related JavaScript on pages from accessing certain privacy sensitive permissions, such as geolocation, microphone, clipboard, bluetooth, usb, and display capture, for&nbsp;increased user privacy.</p>

    <p>Even if policies such as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DefaultGeolocationSetting" rel="noopener" target="_blank">DefaultGeolocationSetting</a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#VideoCaptureAllowedUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank">VideoCaptureAllowedUrls</a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AudioCaptureAllowedUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank">AudioCaptureAllowedUrls</a>, or <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ClipboardAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank">ClipboardAllowedForUrls</a> are used, those sites can still have permissions denied for ad script.</p>

    <p>Admins can&nbsp;disable this intervention using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AdsSettingForIntrusiveAdsSites" rel="noopener" target="_blank">AdsSettingForIntrusiveAdsSites</a> enterprise policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia - Feature rolls out gradually</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD146" name="chromeBrsrD146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Bundled security settings</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature provides users with bundled security options to configure security settings based on their desired level of protection while using Chrome. Users can choose between <em>Enhanced</em> for the highest level of security and <em>Standard</em> for the default balanced protection. Users can still set custom values for the settings, as they can today. This simplifies the user experience and makes it easier for users to get the level of protection they want without needing to understand advanced configuration options. Existing enterprise policies take precedence over end-user bundle selections. If an existing policy is configured for security settings, the values will not be overridden by a user's choice of security bundle.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>
        <p><strong>Chrome 146 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></p>
      </li>
    </ul>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/rOjYTnw6WvE99D9DxEhOhicp7JJVfmmI4txz8ZjRrflAoiH_xqEhpJMjp2vOGQw-jNAP=w895" width="1080" height="563" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/rOjYTnw6WvE99D9DxEhOhicp7JJVfmmI4txz8ZjRrflAoiH_xqEhpJMjp2vOGQw-jNAP"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE146" name="chromeBrsrE146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove third-party storage partitioning policies</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Third-party storage partitioning became the default in Chrome 115. Chrome 128 removed the <code>chrome://flag</code> that allowed users to disable this feature, and the deprecation trial ended with Chrome 139. In Chrome 146, we remove the enterprise policies <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DefaultThirdPartyStoragePartitioningSetting" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DefaultThirdPartyStoragePartitioningSetting</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyStoragePartitioningBlockedForOrigins" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ThirdPartyStoragePartitioningBlockedForOrigins</u></a>. We advise users to transition to alternative storage solutions, either by adapting to third-party storage partitioning or by using <code>document.requestStorageAccess({...})</code>, where needed.</p>

    <p>If you have any feedback, you can add it <a href="https://g-issues.chromium.org/issues/425248669" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here in the Chromium bug</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong>: Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DefaultThirdPartyStoragePartitioningSetting" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DefaultThirdPartyStoragePartitioningSetting</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyStoragePartitioningBlockedForOrigins" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ThirdPartyStoragePartitioningBlockedForOrigins</u></a> Policies</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2>Chrome Enterprise Core changes</h2>

<p><a id="chromeECA146" name="chromeECA146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Spin.AI Risk score update in the Admin console&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As early as Chrome 146, the risk assessment scores for Spin.AI in the <strong>Admin console </strong>will reflect <a href="https://spin.ai/help/gworkspace-security/risk-assessment-scoring-scale-update/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>recent changes made by Spin.AI</u></a>. The scoring still follows the 0 to 100 scale, however, a score of 0 will reflect low risk, while a score of 100 will reflect a high risk.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeECB146" name="chromeECB146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Experimental cryptographic compliance policies&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p><strong>PreferSlowKEXAlgorithms</strong> and <strong>PreferSlowCiphers</strong> are two new, experimental enterprise policies that configure Chrome to order its preferred key agreement algorithms (supported groups) and encryption cipher algorithms, in <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8446" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TLS 1.3</u></a>, to reflect a preference for algorithms that have been approved by a specific compliance regime. Currently, the only compliance regime is <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-becker-cnsa2-ssh-profile/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CNSA2</u></a>. This does not guarantee that any specific algorithms will be negotiated. It allows server operators who want to support clients with and without compliance requirements to differentiate between clients, and only use certain non-default algorithms with increased cryptographic strength for those explicitly configured to prefer them. This policy is not required for security. The default cryptography used by Chrome is strong enough to withstand a brute force attack using the entire power of the sun. Setting this policy will cause Chrome to be slower when accessing websites. This policy only affects TLS 1.3 and <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9000/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>QUIC</u></a>, it does not affect earlier versions of TLS.</p>

    <p>These policies are temporarily available as a single combined flag, <code>chrome://#cryptography-compliance-cnsa</code>.</p>
  </li>
  <li>Chrome 143 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia: The policies are available but marked as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/intl/en_ca/policies/#EnableExperimentalPolicies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>experimental</u></a> for Chrome browser</li>
  <li>Chrome 144 on ChromeOS: The additional policies that apply to the ChromeOS device login screen are available but marked as experimental.</li>
  <li><strong>Chrome 146 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>: Around Chrome 146, the TLS servers for Google properties will be updated to negotiate ML-KEM-1024 when this flag is set. At that point, the policy will no longer be marked as experimental.</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeECC146" name="chromeECC146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Seamless Okta Single Sign-On on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome on macOS now provides an enhanced Single Sign-On (SSO) experience for organizations using <a href="https://www.okta.com/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Okta</u></a>. When a macOS device is managed and configured with the appropriate Extensible Enterprise SSO Mobile and Device Management (MDM) profile for Okta, users will benefit from a seamless authentication flow.</p>

    <p>Specifically, prompts that previously asked for user permission to open the Okta Verify application or to allow local network communications during Okta FastPass authentication will no longer appear. Chrome will use Apple's built-in Extensible SSO mechanism to handle these authentications.</p>

    <p>Requirements:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Enable SSO support as an&nbsp;<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow ugc" href="https://help.okta.com/oie/en-us/content/topics/identity-engine/devices/config-credential-sso-ext-macos.htm?cshid=csh-sso-ext-macos">Okta Self-Service Early Access feature</a>.</li>
      <li>The device must be running macOS.</li>
      <li>The device must be managed and have the correct ExtensibleEnterpriseSSO MDM profile configured by an administrator.</li>
      <li>The organization's Okta environment must be set up to support this flow.</li>
      <li>The Okta Verify application must be installed on the device.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>Admins can manage this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensibleEnterpriseSSOBlocklist" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensibleEnterpriseSSOBlocklist</u></a> policy. To prevent Chrome from using the built-in Okta SSO integration, add <code>okta</code> to the policy's list of strings. To disable this built-in integration for all supported identity providers, add the value <code>all</code>.</p>

    <p>This update aims to reduce user interruption and streamline access to Okta-protected resources.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on macOS</strong> - Feature rolls out gradually</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome Enterprise Premium changes</h2>

<p>Read more about the differences between <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/products/chrome-enterprise-premium" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise Core and Chrome Enterprise Premium</u></a>.</p>

<p><a id="chromeEPA146" name="chromeEPA146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Enterprise cache encryption&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>Chrome Enterprise Premium offers enterprise cache encryption, a feature designed to mitigate data exfiltration risks by encrypting browser data stored at rest, specifically the HTTP cache. Using OS-level APIs for key storage through App-Bound encryption, this functionality renders locally-stored data inaccessible to malware if a device is compromised.</p>

    <p>This feature operates transparently in the background, though it may impact performance due to real-time encryption. Administrators can manage this via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CacheEncryptionEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CacheEncryptionEnabled</u></a> policy. Note that enabling or disabling this policy will automatically clear the existing cache to ensure data consistency.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>: Cache encryption becomes available on desktop platforms.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeEPB146" name="chromeEPB146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Hardening against local policy tampering&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>Policy conflict detection signals for <a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/9275380" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Context-Aware Access (CAA)</u></a>, closes a significant security gap by enabling the detection of corporate policies being overridden by conflicting local settings on BYOD devices.</p>

    <p>This is achieved by integrating new policy conflict signals from the managed Chrome profile into the existing security reporting pipeline, controlled by the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UserSecuritySignalsReporting" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UserSecuritySignalsReporting</u></a> policy.</p>

    <p>This visibility allows Admins to set CAA rules in Chrome Enterprise Premium's (CEP) Data and Threat Protection tools or Security Gateway to automatically block access to corporate applications if critical policies, such as DLP controls, Safe Browsing, or Extension blocklists, are found to be non-compliant.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 144 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Detection and reporting of policy conflict metadata begins.</li>
      <li>Chrome 145 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Enables the Context-Aware Access (CAA) evaluation flow to allow Admins to write enforcement rules based on the existence of a conflict.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Admin console UI is updated to display conflict signals and policy values begin reporting.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome browser changes</h4>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrA146" name="upChromeBrsrA146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>CSS update: decoupling of Width and Style properties&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><span aria-label="gkms:snippet widget"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"><span><img width="15" height="15" title="Click and drag to move"></span></span></a>

    <p>Chrome will soon align with updated <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/css-2025/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSS specifications</u></a> regarding the behavior of <code>border-width</code>, <code>outline-width</code>, and <code>column-rule-width</code> properties. Previously, if the corresponding <code>border-style</code>, <code>outline-style</code>, or <code>column-rule-style</code> was set to none or hidden, the computed width of these properties would be forced to <code>0px</code>, regardless of the specified value.</p>

    <p>With this change, the computed values of <code>border-widt</code>h, <code>outline-width</code>, and <code>column-rule-width</code> will always reflect the author-specified values, independent of the *-style property. Additionally, the resolved values (as returned by <code>getComputedStyle()</code>) for <code>outline-width</code> and <code>column-rule-width</code> also will reflect the specified values.</p>

    <p>The change aligns Chrome with Firefox and WebKit, which have already implemented this behavior.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147&nbsp;on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong>: No rollout step&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrB146" name="upChromeBrsrB146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Device Bound Session Credentials&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To enhance user security and combat session cookie theft, Chrome is introducing <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/device-bound-session-credentials" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)</u></a>. This feature allows websites to bind a user's session to their specific device, making it significantly harder for stolen session cookies to be used on other machines.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 145 on Windows - Feature rolls out gradually</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147 on macOS</strong> - Feature rolls out gradually&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrE146" name="upChromeBrsrE146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 126 began to directly support accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Administrators can use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy starting in Chrome 125 to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider.</p>

    <p>This policy will be supported through Chrome 147 and will be removed in Chrome 148. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that administrators can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise administrators may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt-in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt-out through Chrome 146.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 148 on Windows</strong>: The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrF146" name="upChromeBrsrF146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>X25519Kyber768 key encapsulation for TLS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 124 enabled by default on all desktop platforms a new post-quantum secure TLS key encapsulation mechanism <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-124-beta#x25519kyber768_key_encapsulation_for_tls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>X25519Kyber768</u></a>, based on a NIST standard (ML-KEM). This protects network traffic from Chrome with servers that also support ML-KEM from decryption by a future quantum computer. This change should be transparent to server operators. This cipher will be used for both <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8446" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TLS 1.3</u></a> and <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9000/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>QUIC</u></a> connections.<br>
      However, some TLS middleboxes might be unprepared for the size of a Kyber (ML-KEM) key encapsulation, or a new TLS ClientHello cipher code point, leading to dropped or hanging connections. This can be resolved by updating your middlebox, or disabling the key encapsulation mechanism via the temporary <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, which will be available through Chrome 145. However, long term, post-quantum secure ciphers will be required in TLS and the enterprise policy will be removed as of Chrome 146. Post-quantum cryptography is required for CSNA 2.0. To learn more, see <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2023/08/protecting-chrome-traffic-with-hybrid.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Protect Chrome Traffic with Hybrid Kyper KEM</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 131 on Linux, MacOS, Windows: Chrome will switch the key encapsulation mechanism to the final standard version of ML-KEM</li>
      <li><strong><strong>Chrome 147&nbsp;on Linux, MacOS, Windows:</strong> </strong>Enterprise policy will be removed.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

  <li><strong>Deprecation and removal of Privacy Sandbox APIs&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <ul>
      <li>Topics</li>
      <li>Protected Audience</li>
      <li>Shared Storage</li>
      <li>Attribution Reporting</li>
      <li>Private Aggregation</li>
      <li>Related Web Sites</li>
      <li>requestStorageAccessFor</li>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivacySandboxSiteEnabledAdsEnabled"><u>PrivacySandboxSiteEnabledAdsEnabled</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivacySandboxAdTopicsEnabled"><u>PrivacySandboxAdTopicsEnabled</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivacySandboxAdMeasurementEnabled"><u>PrivacySandboxAdMeasurementEnabled</u></a></li>
      <li>RelatedWebsiteSetsOverrides</li>
      <li>RelatedWebsiteSetsEnabled</li>

However, some users who rely on server-side integrations (such as k-anonymity server, or coordinators) will see a break in the services. We have proactively reached out to users of the APIs with our deprecation plans. At the time of removal, Chrome 150, all the policies associated with these APIs will also be removed.</p>

    <p>None of the APIs are enabled by default to enterprise users. Enterprise teams may want to review the status for any managed profile in their Admin console.</p>

  <li><strong>Enable "Always Use Secure Connections" by default&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 150 will enable the <strong>Always Use Secure Connections</strong> setting in the "public sites only" mode by default. This means Chrome will ask for the user's permission before the first access to any public site without HTTPS. Public sites are defined as sites that have a globally unique name, and excludes direct navigation to RFC 1918 addresses (192.168.0.1, 10.0.0.0/8, etc), as well as shortnames such as go/.</p>

    <p>Prior to enabling it by default for all users, Chrome will enable <strong>Always Use Secure Connections</strong> for the users who have opted in to <a href="https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/11577602" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Enhanced Safe Browsing protections in Chrome</u></a>.</p>

    <p>If you are a website developer or IT professional, and you have users who may be impacted by this feature, we very strongly recommend enabling the "Always Use Secure Connections" setting today to help identify sites that you may need to work to migrate. Admins can use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HttpAllowlist" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HttpAllowlist</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HttpsOnlyMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HttpsOnlyMode</u></a> policies to override this behavior.</p>

    <p>For more information, see our <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/security/ask-before-http/ask-before-http-adoption-guide.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>adoption guide</u></a> and <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2025/10/https-by-default.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>announcement blog post</u></a>.</p>

  <li><strong>Isolated Web Apps&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p><a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/tutorials/getting-started-with-isolated-web-apps" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Isolated Web Apps</u></a> (IWAs) are an extension of existing work on PWA installation and Web Packaging that provide stronger protections against server compromise and other tampering that is necessary for developers of security-sensitive applications. Rather than being hosted on live web servers and fetched over HTTPS, these applications are packaged into Web Bundles, signed by their developer, and distributed to end-users through one or more of the potential methods described in the <a href="https://github.com/WICG/isolated-web-apps/blob/main/README.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>explainer</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 to v5 migration&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/reference" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>v5 API</u></a> instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5. If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4*</code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead: <code>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</code>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users. For more details, see <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/reference/Migration.From.V4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Migration From V4 - Safe Browsing</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrO146" name="upChromeBrsrO146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate and remove XSLT&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p><a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/xslt-10/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>XSLT v1.0</u></a>, which all browsers adhere to, was standardized in 1999. In the meantime, XSLT has evolved to v2.0 and v3.0, adding features, and growing apart from the old version frozen into browsers. This lack of advancement, coupled with the rise of JavaScript libraries and frameworks that offer more flexible and powerful DOM manipulation, has led to a significant decline in the use of client-side XSLT. Its role within the web browser has been largely superseded by JavaScript-based technologies, such as JSON+React.</p>

    <p>Chromium uses the libxslt library to process these transformations, and <a href="https://discourse.gnome.org/t/stepping-down-as-libxslt-maintainer/27615" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>libxslt was unmaintained</u></a> for ~6 months of 2025. Libxslt is a complex, aging C codebase of the type notoriously susceptible to memory safety vulnerabilities like buffer overflows, which can lead to arbitrary code execution. Because client-side XSLT is now a niche, rarely-used feature, these libraries receive far less maintenance and security scrutiny than core JavaScript engines, yet they represent a direct, potent attack surface for processing untrusted web content. Indeed, XSLT is the source of several recent high-profile security exploits that continue to put browser users at risk. For these reasons, Chromium (along with both other browser engines) plans to deprecate and remove XSLT from the web platform. For more details, see this article on&nbsp;<a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/deprecating-xslt" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Chrome for Developers</a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 143 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, MacOS, Windows: Deprecation (but not removal) of the APIs.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 152 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, MacOS, Windows:</strong> Origin Trial (OT) and Enterprise Policy go live for testing. These allow sites and enterprises to continue using features past the removal date.</li>
      <li>Chrome 155 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, MacOS, Windows: XSLT stops functioning on Stable releases, for all users other than Origin Trial and Enterprise Policy participants.</li>
      <li>Chrome 164 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, MacOS, Windows: Origin Trial and Enterprise Policy stop functioning. XSLT is disabled for all users.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrP146" name="upChromeBrsrP146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>PostQuantum cryptography for DTLS in WebRTC&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature will enable the use of PostQuantum Cryptography (PQC) with WebRTC connections. The motivation for PQC is to get WebRTC media traffic up to date with the latest cryptography protocols and prevent <em>Harvest Now to Crack Later</em> scenarios.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Admins will be able to control this feature using an enterprise policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#WebRtcPostQuantumKeyAgreement" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebRtcPostQuantumKeyAgreement</u></a>, to allow enterprise users to opt out of PQC. The policy will be temporary and is planned to be removed by Chrome 152.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 142 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia: Feature rolls out</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 152 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong>: Remove enterprise policy</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

  <li><strong>Moving to a 2-week release cycle&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>From September 2026 (Chrome 153) Chrome will move to a 2-week release cycle, from the current four-week cycle. The web platform is constantly advancing, and our goal at Chrome is to ensure developers and users have immediate access to the latest capabilities, fixes, and performance improvements. Building on our history of adapting our release process to match the demands of a modern web, we are announcing this significant step to further increase our development velocity and Chrome Stable is moving to a 2-week release cycle. You can find more details in the&nbsp;<a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-two-week-release" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Chrome for Developers</a>&nbsp;blog post.</p>

    <p>Extended Stable is available for customers who might have concerns about the maintenance costs. For more information about Extended Stable, see this&nbsp;<a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16942104" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Help Center</a>&nbsp;article. The 2-week Stable option remains the most secure choice and should be utilized if security is a larger concern than maintenance costs.</p>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrQ146" name="upChromeBrsrQ146">&nbsp; &nbsp;</a></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL hosts&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>According to the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL Standard specification</u></a> URL hosts cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host. This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a> and <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL focus</u></a> areas. To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows file:// URLs. For more details, see this <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github discussion</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 157 on Android, ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, MacOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><strong>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeEPA146" name="upChromeEPA146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Enterprise Connectors API&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise will soon expand programmatic management for <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/12166576" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise Connectors</u></a>. This update will introduce resources to define and assign connector configurations, complementing the existing connector policies to allow administrators to manage the full life-cycle of these integrations at scale.</p>

    <p>Previously, configuring Service Providers was a manual process in the Google Admin console. This update enables automation, which helps reduce manual errors and improve the efficiency of managing integrations with third-party security solutions.</p>

    <p>Administrators can now use the Chrome Management API to manage ConnectorConfiguration resources (defining the provider). Connector Selection is managed via the Chrome Policy API, enabling the assignment of these configurations to Organizational Units or Groups. This works in tandem with existing Policy API settings for event reporting and content analysis, including policies such as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnSecurityEventEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnSecurityEventEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnPrintEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnPrintEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseRealTimeUrlCheckMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseRealTimeUrlCheckMode</u></a>. For technical details, developers should refer to the <a href="https://developers.google.com/chrome/management/reference/rest" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Management API</u></a> and <a href="https://developers.google.com/chrome/policy/reference/rest" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Policy API documentation</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 143 on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: This rollout adds support for programmatic management of Chrome Enterprise Connectors via a new API</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147&nbsp;on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>: This rollout introduces the ConnectorConfiguration and ConnectorSelection resources, enabling the creation of service provider instances and their assignment to organizational units.</li>
    </ul>

<p><strong>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeEPAA146" name="upChromeEPAA146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Drag support for data controls&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome will enhance&nbsp;the Data Controls framework by extending security enforcement to drag-and-drop operations across Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, and Android to ensure consistency with existing clipboard policies. Admins will be able to&nbsp;manage this behavior through the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DataControlsRules" rel="noopener" target="_blank">DataControlsRules</a> policy, though any WARN verdict will automatically escalate to a BLOCK to prevent a warning dialog from interrupting the interactive drag loop.</p>

    <p>When an action is restricted, users will see the new <strong>ClipboardDragBlock</strong> dialog or an Android blocking modal stating that dragging content is not allowed on the site. This update will close&nbsp;a critical data exfiltration gap using local evaluation to maintain performance and privacy. Organizations should test these rules using the <strong>DataControlsDragEnforcement</strong> feature flag and the <code>chrome://policy/test</code> page.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows - Feature rolls out gradually</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><strong>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeEPB146" name="upChromeEPB146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Increased file size support for DLP scans&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise Premium will extend its Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and malware scanning capabilities to include large and encrypted files. Previously, files larger than 50 MB and all encrypted files were skipped during content scanning. This update will close that critical security gap. For policies configured to save evidence, files <strong>up to 2GB</strong> can now be sent to the Evidence Locker. This provides administrators with greater visibility and control, significantly reducing the risk of data exfiltration through large file transfers.</p>

    <p>No new policy is required to enable this feature. It is automatically controlled by the existing DLP rule configurations in the Google Admin console. If admins have rules that apply to file uploads, downloads, or printing, they will now also apply to large and encrypted files. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11587610" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>What are ChromeOS data controls?</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147&nbsp;on Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>This stage enables the collection of large (&gt;50 MB) and encrypted files for the Evidence Locker, closing a key DLP security gap.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><strong>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeEPC146" name="upChromeEPC146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support for AllowList and BlockList for DeveloperToolsAvailability policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome will introduce two new policies, <strong>DeveloperToolsAvailabilityAllowlist</strong> and <strong>DeveloperToolsAvailabilityBlocklist</strong>, which provide granular control over the availability of Developer Tools based on URL patterns.</p>

    <p>Previously, administrators could only allow or disallow Developer Tools globally. With these new policies, admins can now enforce a general block on Developer Tools to secure sensitive corporate data, while explicitly permitting access on specific internal URLs for development or troubleshooting purposes.</p>

    <p>These controls are available on Windows, Mac, Linux, and ChromeOS. If these new policies are not configured, the behavior of the existing <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DeveloperToolsAvailability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DeveloperToolsAvailability</u></a> policy remains unchanged.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147&nbsp;on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows -</strong> Feature rolls out gradually. Introduces the <strong>DeveloperToolsAvailabilityAllowlist</strong> and <strong>DeveloperToolsAvailabilityBlocklist</strong> policies on Desktop platforms.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><strong>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeEPD146" name="upChromeEPD146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support for AllowList and BlockList for IncognitoModeAvailability policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome will introduce two new policies, <strong>IncognitoModeUrlBlocklist</strong> and <strong>IncognitoModeUrlAllowlist</strong>, to provide administrators with more precise control over Incognito mode usage. Previously, administrators could only completely enable or disable Incognito mode via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#IncognitoModeAvailability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>IncognitoModeAvailability</u></a> policy.</p>

    <p>These new policies function similarly to the existing <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#URLBlocklist" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URLBlocklist</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#URLAllowlist" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URLAllowlist</u></a> policies but are specifically designated for Incognito sessions. This allows organizations to restrict access to specific URLs in Incognito mode to protect sensitive information while permitting legitimate usage on other sites.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147&nbsp;on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows - </strong>Feature rolls out gradually. Introduces the <strong>IncognitoModeUrlBlocklist</strong> and <strong>IncognitoModeUrlAllowlist</strong> policies.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><strong>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeEPE146" name="upChromeEPE146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Enterprise extension DOM activity telemetry&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This enterprise-only feature provides security auditing for Chrome Extensions by creating a high-fidelity pipeline that monitors risky behavior. It specifically focuses on identifying Code Injection (execution risks) and Data Access (theft risks) occurring between web pages and extensions. Verified signals are filtered to ensure browser performance is not impacted, and they are ultimately transmitted using the Chrome real-time reporting pipeline for Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system analysis. This feature can be enabled by admins using the <strong>ExtensionDOMActivityLoggingEnabled</strong> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 148 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong> - Early preview available to Chrome Enterprise Trusted&nbsp;Testers</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Current ChromeOS updates</h4>

<p><a id="chromeOSA146" name="chromeOSA146"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Local Camera folder policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Starting in ChromeOS 146, a new local Camera folder policy allows Admins to specify a location for storing Camera files when local storage is deactivated on user devices.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>When <strong>Do not allow users to store and read local data</strong> is enabled, the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalUserFilesAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalUserFilesAllowed</u></a> policy, local storage is deactivated on user devices. This new policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/camera-save-location/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CameraSaveLocation</u></a>, allows Admins to extend that setting to apply for <strong>Camera files</strong>, using the <strong>Save to local Camera folder option</strong>.</p>

</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes &nbsp;</h2>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB145" name="chromeBrsrB145"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>AI Mode and Lens enhancements&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 143 on macOS and Windows, new AI Mode capabilities were integrated into Chrome browser. Users can access AI Mode directly from the <strong>New tab</strong> page and the address bar, allowing users to ask complex questions directly from where they start browsing. Admins can turn off these features (value 1) using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AIModeSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AIModeSettings</u></a> policy or by using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> (value 2). For more details, see this article in the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14443058#zippy=%2Cgemini-enterprise%2Cgoogle-lens%2Cai-mode:~:text=Google%20generative%20AI%20features%20available%20through%20Chrome" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center</u></a>, Chrome—Generative AI features and policies.<br>
      In Chrome 144, we rolled out the multi-tab context feature on AI Mode and Lens. Users can choose to share the contents of one or more of their open tabs, helping them ask questions, compare, summarize, and find information more efficiently. Admins can turn off these features (value 1) using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SearchContentSharingSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SearchContentSharingSettings</u></a> policy or by using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> (value 2).<br>
      Starting in Chrome 145 on Android and iOS, new AI Mode capabilities are integrated into Chrome browser.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 143 on macOS, Windows:&nbsp; New AI Mode&nbsp;capabilities will be integrated into Chrome and can be controlled using <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AIModeSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AIModeSettings</u></a> policy or the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> policy</li>

  <li><strong>Disable force-installed extensions with non-malware violations&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

Such violations include general program violations, unwanted software, and potential security vulnerabilities not classified as malware. Users retain the ability to enable or disable these extensions, but will not be able to remove them.</p>

    <p>This change does not affect managed instances of Chrome that are joined to a Microsoft Active Directory domain, joined to Microsoft Azure Active Directory or enrolled in Chrome Enterprise Core. On macOS, this change does not affect instances of Chrome that are managed via MDM, joined to a domain or enrolled in Chrome Enterprise Core.</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE145" name="chromeBrsrE145"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome WebGPU toggle in AAPM&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This update disables the WebGPU Javascript API in the Chrome browser for users enrolled in Android Advanced Protection Mode (AAPM).</p>

    <p>Websites using <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/webgpu" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebGPU</u></a> for 3D rendering (for example, Google Maps) will use slower alternatives like <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebGL</u></a>. Expect decreased performance for heavy rendering (benchmarks indicated about a 5.78% latency decrease). Users are informed in AAPM settings.</p>

    <p>For developers, the <code>navigator.gpu</code> object will be undefined, requiring you to implement a fallback option.</p>

    <p>Admins retain control and may disable the feature if functional impact is prohibitive. The feature is toggled via an AAPM callback hook, requiring system/root access.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 145 on Android</strong></li>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrF145" name="chromeBrsrF145"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome removes support for obsolete virtual cameras on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As early as Chrome 145, Chrome will remove support for obsolete virtual cameras for all macOS releases that it supports.</p>

    <p>On macOS, modern virtual cameras are built using the <a href="https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coremediaio" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Core Media IO</u></a> framework, which has been available since macOS 12.3. Apple has performed outreach, and all modern virtual camera software has been migrated to use this <a href="https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2022/10022/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Core Media IO framework</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Obsolete virtual cameras, built as DAL plugins, have been blocked by macOS itself starting with macOS 14.1 (2023), and have been unsupported in Safari since 2018, if not earlier.</p>

    <p>Chrome will remove support for obsolete virtual cameras for all macOS releases that it supports. This allows Chrome to improve security by fully disallowing loading of third-party libraries into Chrome processes.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 145 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
