<p><a id="chromeBrsrI139" name="chromeBrsrI139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove risky extension flags in Google Chrome&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To enhance the security and stability of the Chrome browser for our users, official Chrome branded builds will be removing <code>--extensions-on-chrome-urls</code> and <code>--disable-extensions-except</code> command-line flags starting in Chrome 139. This change aims to mitigate the risks associated with harmful and unwanted extensions.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Developers can still use the both flags in non-branded builds such as <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium and Chrome For Testing</u></a><strong>.</strong></p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrJ139" name="chromeBrsrJ139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove SwiftShader fallback&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Allowing automatic fallback to <a href="https://get.webgl.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebGL</u></a> backed by <a href="https://github.com/google/swiftshader" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SwiftShader</u></a> is deprecated and WebGL context creation now fails instead of falling back to SwiftShader.&nbsp; This was done for two primary reasons:&nbsp;</p>

    <ol>
      <li>SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process.</li>
      <li>Users have a poor experience when falling back from a high-performance GPU-backed WebGL to a CPU-backed implementation. Users have no control over this behavior and it is difficult to describe in bug reports.</li>
    </ol>

    <p>SwiftShader is a useful tool for web developers to test their sites on systems that are headless or do not have a supported GPU. This use case will still be supported by opting in but is not intended for running untrusted content. To opt in to lower security guarantees and allow SwiftShader for WebGL, run the chrome executable with the <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> command-line switch.</p>

    <p>During the deprecation period, a warning will appear in the javascript console when a WebGL context is created and backed with SwiftShader. Passing <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader </code>will remove this warning message.</p>

    <p>Chromium and other browsers do not guarantee WebGL availability. It is important to test and handle WebGL context creation failure and fall back to other web APIs such as Canvas2D or an appropriate message to the user.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139&nbsp;</strong>

        <ul>
          <li><strong>on Linux, macOS: </strong>Swiftshader will be disabled on macOS and Linux.&nbsp; Users on machines without a GPU will not be able to use WebGL.</li>
          <li><strong>On Windows: </strong>The fallback to Swiftshader after three out-of-memory (OOM) errors will be disabled on Windows. Swiftshader usage will be limited to devices without a GPU or those with a GPU on the blocklist.&nbsp;</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrK139" name="chromeBrsrK139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Shared tab groups&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Users can now collaborate on tabs using the shared tab groups feature. With this feature, users can create and use a set of tabs on their desktop or mobile device and their collaborative partners can browse the same tabs on their devices. When one person changes a tab in the group, the changes are reflected across all users’ browsers in the group. An enterprise policy, <strong>TabGroupSharingSettings</strong>, will be available in Chrome 140 to control this feature.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout of the ability to join and use a shared tab group. Users on Stable Chrome will not be able to create a shared tab group (the entry point will not be available) - this part of the feature will only be available on Beta/Dev/Canary for this phase of rollout.&nbsp;</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on iOS:&nbsp; </strong>As early as Chrome 139, support for iOS will rollout</li>
      <li>Chrome 140 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: <strong>TabGroupSharingSettings </strong>enterprise policy will be available to the enterprise owner in the Google Admin console.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrL139" name="chromeBrsrL139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support accounts in pending state on Chrome iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Accounts whose credentials somehow became invalid are no longer automatically signed out and removed from Chrome on iOS. Instead, these accounts stay signed in to the browser, in a newly introduced <em>pending state</em> associated with a persistent error indication in the UI so users are encouraged to resolve it. This also means that local data associated with these accounts are no longer automatically deleted, but instead kept on disk. Existing policies controlling sign-in (for example, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a>) continue to work as before.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on iOS:</strong> Feature will gradually roll out&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrM139" name="chromeBrsrM139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Upcoming change for CA certificates included in the Chrome Root Store&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In response to sustained compliance failures, Chrome 139 changes how publicly-trusted TLS server authentication, that is, websites or certificates issued by Chunghwa Telecom and Netlock, are trusted by default. This applies to Chrome 139 and later on Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, and Linux; iOS policies do not allow use of the Chrome Root Store in Chrome for iOS.</p>

    <p>Specifically, TLS certificates validating to the Chunghwa Telecom or Netlock root CA certificates included in the Chrome Root Store and issued:</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- after July 31, 2025, will no longer be trusted by default.</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- on or before July 31, 2025, will be unaffected by this change.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>If a Chrome user or an enterprise explicitly trusts any of the affected Chunghwa Telecom or Netlock certificates on a platform and version of Chrome relying on the Chrome Root Store, for example, when explicit trust is conveyed through a Windows Group Policy Object, the Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT) constraints described above will be overridden and certificates will function as they do today.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For additional information and testing resources, see <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2025/05/sustaining-digital-certificate-security-chrome-root-store-changes.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Sustaining Digital Certificate Security - Upcoming Changes to the Chrome Root Store</u></a>.</p>

    <p>To learn more about the Chrome Root Store, see this <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/net/data/ssl/chrome_root_store/faq.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>FAQ</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows:</strong> All versions of Chrome 139 and higher that rely on the Chrome Root Store will honor the blocking action, but the blocking action will only begin for certificates issued after July 31, 2025.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrN139" name="chromeBrsrN139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Stop sending Purpose: prefetch header from prefetches and prerenders&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Now that prefetches and prerenders are using the Sec-Purpose header for prefetches and prerenders, this change&nbsp; removes the legacy <code>Purpose: prefetch</code> header that is still currently passed. This update is behind a feature flag or kill switch to prevent compatibility issues.</p>

    <p>The scope includes speculation rules prefetch, speculation rules prerender, <code>&lt;link rel=prefetch&gt;</code>, and Chromium's non-standard <code>&lt;link rel=prerender&gt;</code>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrO139" name="chromeBrsrO139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome to remove support for macOS 11&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 138 is the last release to support macOS 11; Chrome 139 and later will no longer support macOS 11, which is outside of its support window with Apple. Running on a supported operating system is essential to maintaining security.</p>

    <p>On Macs running macOS 11, Chrome will continue to work, showing a warning infobar, but will not update any further. If a user wishes to have their Chrome updated, they need to update their computer to a support version of macOS. For new installations of Chrome 139 and later, macOS 12 and later will be required.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrP139" name="chromeBrsrP139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Fire error event instead of throwing exception for CSP blocked worker&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>When blocked by <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Content Security Policy (CSP)</u></a>, Chromium currently throws a SecurityError from the constructor of Worker and SharedWorker. To be spec-compliant, the CSP needs to be checked as part of fetch and then fire error events asynchronously instead of throwing an exception when the script runs new Worker(url) or new SharedWorker(url).&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This update aims to make Chromium spec-conformant, which is, it no longer throws exceptions following constructor calls, and fires error events asynchronously.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrQ139" name="chromeBrsrQ139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Randomizing TCP port allocation on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature enables TCP port randomization on Windows versions 2020 H1 and later. We do not anticipate issues with rapid re-use of prior ports (which can cause rejections due to port re-use timeouts) on these versions. The rapid port re-use issue stems from <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&amp;v=m7hI2LulMxE" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>the Birthday problem</u></a>, where the probability of randomly re-picking an already used port quickly approaches 100% with each new port chosen, unlike sequential port re-use models.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows,&nbsp;macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome Enterprise Premium changes</h2>

<p>Read more about the differences between <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/products/chrome-enterprise-premium" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise Core and Chrome Enterprise Premium</u></a>.</p>

<p><a id="chromeEPA139" name="chromeEPA139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Active account detection&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>Chrome Enterprise can now detect whether an employee is using their corporate or personal Google account on Google Workspace pages like Google Drive, Docs, or Gmail. This allows administrators to create more granular Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rules to prevent sensitive data from being moved to personal accounts, addressing a critical data exfiltration risk.<strong> </strong>For instance, an administrator can now configure a policy in the Google Admin console to block a file upload to a personal Google Drive account while still allowing it to a corporate account.<strong> </strong>To use this feature, administrators should create or update their DLP rules to include the new <strong>Google Workspace Web app signed-in account</strong> condition. There is no single enterprise policy to enable or disable this feature; control is managed through the creation of these specific DLP rules.</p>
&nbsp;
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: </strong>The Chrome browser can detect the active user account on Google Workspace pages and sends this information as a new signal with Data Loss Prevention (DLP) scan requests.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeEPB139" name="chromeEPB139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Enterprise Connectors API&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>Chrome Enterprise is introducing programmatic management for Chrome Enterprise Connectors. This update exposes connector settings as new and updated policies within the existing Chrome Policy API, allowing IT administrators and technology partners to manage these configurations at scale. Previously, this was a manual process in the Google Admin console. This update enables automation, which helps reduce manual errors and improve the efficiency of managing integrations with third-party security solutions.</p>

    <p>Administrators can use the Chrome Policy API to programmatically control settings for event reporting, content analysis, and real-time URL checks. This launch includes updates to the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnSecurityEventEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnSecurityEventEnterpriseConnector</u></a> policy and adds new policies such as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileTransferEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileTransferEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/intl/en_ca/policies/#OnPrintEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnPrintEnterpriseConnector</u></a>, and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseRealTimeUrlCheckMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseRealTimeUrlCheckMode</u></a>.</p>

    <p>For technical details, developers should refer to the main <a href="https://developers.google.com/chrome/policy/reference/rest" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Policy API documentation</u></a>&nbsp;</p>
&nbsp;
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Android, iOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: </strong>This rollout adds support for programmatic management of Chrome Enterprise Connectors via a new API</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>

<p><a id="chromeEPC139" name="chromeEPC139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Copy and paste rules protection&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>To help organizations better prevent data exfiltration on mobile devices, Chrome is extending its existing desktop clipboard data controls. Administrators can now use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DataControlsRules" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DataControlsRules</u></a> policy to set rules that block or warn users when they attempt to copy or paste content that violates organizational policies. This feature allows admins to define data boundaries and prevent sensitive information from being pasted from a work context into personal apps or websites on their mobile fleet. This addresses a significant security gap and a frequently requested feature from enterprise customers who have cited the lack of mobile data controls as a concern. To use this feature, administrators can configure clipboard restrictions within the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DataControlsRules" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DataControlsRules</u></a> policy, providing a consistent management experience across desktop and mobile to strengthen their organization's overall security posture.</p>
    &nbsp;
    <ul>

<p><a id="chromeEPD139" name="chromeEPD139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Data Loss Prevention support for iFrames&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>To enhance security and prevent data exfiltration, Chrome's Data Loss Prevention (DLP) capabilities are being extended to the content within iFrames. Currently, DLP rules configured by administrators do not apply to content inside an iFrame, which allows a potential security loophole where users can bypass restrictions. This feature closes that gap. With this change, when a user performs a DLP-triggering action (such as uploading a file) from a site loaded in an iFrame, Chrome will send the entire URL hierarchy, from the source iFrame up to the top-level page, to be evaluated against all applicable DLP rules.</p>
    &nbsp;
    <p>The motivation for this change is to provide a more robust security posture and eliminate a known method for bypassing data protection policies. No new enterprise policies are required to enable this functionality; it will work with existing DLP rules configured via the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/10106035?sjid=5991552215396607268-NA" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Connector policies</u></a>. Administrators should be aware that their existing rules will now apply to iFrame contexts, which may block user actions that were previously permitted.</p>
    &nbsp;
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: </strong>Initial launch of Data Loss Prevention support for iFrames. This phase adds enforcement for file upload events originating from within an iFrame context and it will work with existing DLP rules configured via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileAttachedEnterpriseConnector</u></a> policy</li>
      <li>Chrome 140 on Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: This expanded phase combines two feature rollouts, extending DLP iFrame support to include enforcement for both file download and printing&nbsp; actions.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeEPE139" name="chromeEPE139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Enable watermarking on Single Page Applications&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>To enhance data security, Chrome Enterprise Premium’s watermarking feature now supports Single Page Applications (SPAs). This addresses a significant customer request, as watermarks previously only applied to traditional websites. This capability is controlled by your existing Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies in the Google Admin Console; no new policy configuration is required for this enhancement.</p>
    &nbsp;
    <p>IT administrators should be aware of a key technical limitation. SPAs utilize same-document navigations, which cannot be paused for a security scan like a standard page load. Consequently, there may be a brief delay before a watermark appears after navigating within an SPA. Additionally, DLP rules set to <em>Warn</em> or <em>Block</em> will not display an interstitial page for these SPA navigations; the action would only trigger on a full page reload.</p>
    &nbsp;
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: </strong>This rollout adds support for watermarking on Single Page Applications (SPAs)</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>

<ul>
  <li><strong>IP protection</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature limits availability of a user’s original IP address in third-party contexts in <strong>Incognito mode</strong>, enhancing Incognito's protections against cross-site tracking when users choose to browse in this mode. IP addresses facilitate a range of use cases, including routing traffic and preventing fraud and spam. However, they can also be used for tracking. For Chrome users who choose to browse in Incognito mode, we want to provide additional control over their IP address, without breaking essential web functionality. To strike this balance between protection and usability, this proposal focuses on limiting the use of IP addresses in a third-party context in Incognito mode. To that end, this proposal uses a list-based approach, where only domains on the <a href="https://support.google.com/privacysandbox/answer/16085975?hl=en&amp;ref_topic=16076404#:~:text=The%20Masked%20Domain%20List%20(MDL)%20is%20a%20list%20of%20domains,in%20the%20IP%20Protection%20explainer." rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Masked Domain List (MDL)</u></a> in a third-party context will be impacted. For enterprises, this feature can be controlled via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivacySandboxIpProtectionEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivacySandboxIpProtectionEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrM139" name="upChromeBrsrM139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Local network access restrictions</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 140 restricts the ability to make requests to the user's local network, gated behind a permission prompt. A local network request is any request from a public website to a local IP address or loopback, or from a local website (for example,. intranet) to loopback. Gating the ability for websites to perform these requests behind a permission mitigates the risk of cross-site request forgery attacks against local network devices such as routers, and reduces the ability of sites to use these requests to fingerprint the user's local network.</p>

    <p>This permission is restricted to secure contexts. If granted, the permissions additionally relaxes mixed content blocking for local network requests (since many local devices are not able to obtain publicly trusted TLS certificates for various reasons).</p>

    <p>This work supersedes a prior effort called <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Private Network Access</u></a>, which used preflight requests to have local devices opt-in. Enterprises that need to disable or auto-grant the permission can do so using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalNetworkAccessAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalNetworkAccessAllowedForUrls</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalNetworkAccessBlockedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalNetworkAccessBlockedForUrls</u></a> policies. The value of '*' can be used to allow local network access on all URLs, matching the behavior prior to rolling out the restrictions.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrN139" name="upChromeBrsrN139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Probabilistic Reveal Tokens</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To ensure that all businesses can continue to estimate the amount of fraud on their systems, train models to defend against fraud, and analyze emerging fraudulent behavior while still mitigating the ability to track users at scale using IP addresses, we propose to introduce a delayed IP sampling mechanism called Probabilistic Reveal Tokens (PRTs) alongside IP Protection for use in protected traffic.</p>

    <p>PRTs will be included on proxied requests in a new HTTP header added by the browser for domains that indicate they want to receive them via a signup process. Each PRT will contain a ciphertext, generated by an Issuer and re-randomized for unlinkability by the browser prior to the request, that the recipient can decrypt after a delay. Google will be the issuer for Chrome's implementation. A minority of the decrypted PRTs contain the client's pre-proxy IP address (that is, non-masked, and as observed by the token issuer), while the remaining PRTs provide no information about the client's original IP address. This results in only a small percent of PRTs containing and revealing the user's IP. Since PRTs will only be attached when IP Protection is enabled, admins can use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivacySandboxIpProtectionEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivacySandboxIpProtectionEnabled</u></a> policy to control IP Protection and PRTs.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrO139" name="upChromeBrsrO139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Propagate Viewport overscroll-behavior from Root</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature will propagate overscroll-behavior from the root instead of the body. The <a href="https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/6079#issuecomment-816307011" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSS working group resolved</u></a> on not propagating properties from the body to the viewport. Rather, properties of the viewport are to be propagated from the root element e.g. <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow/#:~:text=not%20propagated%20to%20the%20viewport" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>scroll-behavior</u></a>, <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scroll-snap/#:~:text=not%20propagated%20from%20HTML%20body" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>scroll-snap-type</u></a>, <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scroll-snap/#:~:text=padding%20values%20are%20not%20propagated%20from%20HTML%20body" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>scroll-padding</u></a>. As such, overscroll-behavior should be propagated from the root element. However, Chrome has had a longstanding issue of propagating overscroll-behavior from the body rather than the root, which deviates from the behavior of Safari(WebKit) and Firefox(Gecko). This feature intends to fix this by propagating overscroll-behavior from the root rather than the body.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrP139" name="upChromeBrsrP139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Script blocking in Incognito</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Mitigating API Misuse for Browser Re-Identification, otherwise known as Script Blocking, is a feature that will block scripts engaging in known, prevalent techniques for browser re-identification in third-party contexts. These techniques typically involve the misuse of existing browser APIs to extract additional information about the user's browser or device characteristics.</p>

    <p>This feature uses a list-based approach, where only domains marked as “Impacted by Script Blocking” on the Masked Domain List (MDL) in a third-party context will be impacted. When the feature is enabled, Chrome will check network requests against the blocklist. The Chromium's subresource_filter component will be reused, which is responsible for tagging and filtering subresource requests based on page-level activation signals, and a ruleset is used to match URLs for filtering. The enterprise policy name is <strong>PrivacySandboxFingerprintingProtectionEnabled</strong>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrQ139" name="upChromeBrsrQ139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SharedWorker script inherit controller for blob script URL</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>According to <a href="https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#control-and-use-worker-client" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Worker client case (github)</u></a>, workers should inherit controllers for the blob URL. However, existing code allows only dedicated workers to inherit the controller, and shared workers do not inherit the controller. This is the fix to make Chromium behavior adjust to the specification. An enterprise policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SharedWorkerBlobURLFixEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SharedWorkerBlobURLFixEnabled</u></a> is available to control this feature.</p>

    <p>We plan to adjust the <a href="https://privacysandbox.google.com/cookies/storage-access-api" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Storage Access API</u></a> semantics to strictly follow the Same Origin Policy, to enhance&nbsp; security. <ul>
  <li><strong>HSTS tracking prevention</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This update will mitigate user tracking by third-parties via the <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6797" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)</u></a> cache. This feature only allows HSTS upgrades for top-level navigations and blocks HSTS upgrades for sub-resource requests. Doing so makes it infeasible for third-party sites to use the HSTS cache in order to track users across the web.</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrW139" name="upChromeBrsrW139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL hosts</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>According to the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL Standard specification</u></a>, URL hosts cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host. This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a> and <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL focus</u></a> areas. To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows file:// URLs (<a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>).</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 145 on Android, ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

    <p>Third-party storage partitioning became the default in Chrome 115. Users are advised to transition to alternative storage solutions, either by adapting to third-party storage partitioning or by using&nbsp; <code>document.requestStorageAccess({...})</code> where needed.</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrY39" name="upChromeBrsrY139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 → v5 migration</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/reference" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>v5 API</u></a> instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5. If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4*, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead: safebrowsing.googleapis.com. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users. For more details, see <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/reference/Migration.From.V4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Migration From V4 - Safe Browsing</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrZ139" name="upChromeBrsrZ139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Isolated Web Apps</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Isolated Web Apps (IWAs) are an extension of existing work on PWA installation and Web Packaging that provide stronger protections against server compromise and other tampering that is necessary for developers of security-sensitive applications.</p>

    <p>Rather than being hosted on live web servers and fetched over HTTPS, these applications are packaged into Web Bundles, signed by their developer, and distributed to end-users through one or more of the potential methods described in the <a href="https://github.com/WICG/isolated-web-apps/blob/main/README.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>explainer</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>In this initial release, IWAs will only be installable through an admin policy on enterprise-managed ChromeOS devices.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 146 on Windows </strong>This rollout adds support for Isolated Web Apps in enterprise-managed browser configurations on Windows.</li>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrAA139" name="upChromeBrsrAA139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome will start directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Administrators may use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy starting in Chrome 125 to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 146, and will be removed in Chrome 147. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows: The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that administrators can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise administrators may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt out through Chrome 146.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147 on Windows:</strong> The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<h3><strong>Upcoming Chrome Enterprise Core updates</strong></h3>

<p><strong>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeECA139" name="upChromeECA139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Inactive profile deletion in Chrome Enterprise Core</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In June 2025, the inactive period for profile deletion setting started to roll out. In August 2025, the setting will begin to automatically delete managed profiles in the Admin console that have been inactive for more than the defined inactivity period. When releasing the setting, the inactivity period of time has a default value of 90 days. Meaning that by default, all managed profiles that have been inactive for more than 90 days are deleted from your account. Administrators can change the inactive period value <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/2657289#inactive_period_for_profile_deletion&amp;zippy=%2Cinactive-period-for-profile-deletion" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>using this setting</u></a>. The maximum value to determine the profile inactivity period is 730 days and the minimum value is 28 days.</p>

    <p>If&nbsp; the set value is lowered, it might have a global impact on any currently managed profiles. All impacted profiles will be considered inactive and, therefore, be deleted. This does not delete the user account. If an inactive profile is reactivated on a device, that profile will reappear in the console.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: </strong>Policy was rolled out in June. Deletion will start in August and the initial wave of deletion will complete by the beginning of September. After the initial deletion rollout, inactive profiles will continue to be deleted once they have reached their inactivity period.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome Enterprise Premium changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeEPA139" name="upChromeEPA139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Increased file size support for Data Loss Prevention scans&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise Premium now extends its Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and malware scanning capabilities to include large and encrypted files. Previously, files larger than 50 MB and all encrypted files were skipped during content scanning. This update closes that critical security gap. For policies configured to save evidence, files <strong>up to 2GB</strong> can now be sent to the Evidence Locker. This provides administrators with greater visibility and control, significantly reducing the risk of data exfiltration through large file transfers.</p>

    <p>No new policy is required to enable this feature. It is automatically controlled by the existing DLP rule configurations in the Google Admin Console. If admins have rules that apply to file uploads, downloads, or printing, they will now also apply to large and encrypted files.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: </strong>Feature is rolled out</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeEPB139" name="upChromeEPB139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Watermarking customization&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise Premium now allows administrators to customize the appearance of watermarks. This enhancement is motivated by the need to improve user experience, addressing concerns such as eyestrain and readability on pages with existing watermarks.</p>

    <p>To control the watermark's appearance, administrators should use the new <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#WatermarkStyle" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WatermarkStyle</u></a> policy. Within this policy, admins can configure the following:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>'font_size': Sets the font size of the text in pixels.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>'fill_opacity': Sets the fill opacity of the text, from 0 (transparent) to 100 (opaque).&nbsp;</li>
      <li>'outline_opacity': Sets the outline opacity of the text, from 0 (transparent) to 100 (opaque).&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>This provides administrators with greater flexibility to balance security requirements with end-user productivity.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: </strong>This launch enables administrators to customize watermark font size and opacity using the new <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#WatermarkStyle" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WatermarkStyle</u></a> policy in the Google Admin Console.</li>
      <li>Chrome 141 on ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows:<strong> </strong>As an enhancement, a new chrome:// enterprise page is introduced that allows administrators to preview their configured watermark style before deployment.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeEPC139" name="upChromeEPC139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome browser rule UX refactor&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To enhance the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13876556" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Data Loss Prevention (DLP)</u></a> rule creation experience, the Google Admin console is being updated to streamline how administrators define policies for different applications like Chrome and Workspace. This first introduces mutually exclusive application groups, meaning that a single DLP rule can now only target one application group at a time—either Workspace apps (like Drive, Gmail), Chrome browser triggers (like file upload, URL visited), or ChromeOS triggers. This change simplifies rule configuration, eliminates potential conflicts from overlapping app selections, and lays the groundwork for more specialized and user-friendly workflows tailored to each platform's needs.</p>

    <p>Administrators will see an updated "Apps" selection interface using radio buttons to enforce this single-group selection for new rules. Existing rules that previously combined applications from multiple groups will be transparently migrated by the system into separate, compliant, single-platform rules to ensure continued protection and a seamless transition. Banners within the Admin console will provide information regarding these changes and the migration process. No new enterprise policies are introduced with this update; the changes are to the rule configuration interface.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 141 on ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: </strong>Enables mutually exclusive app selection for DLP rule configuration in Admin Console</li>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>ChromeOS updates</h4>

<p><a id="chromeOSA139" name="chromeOSA139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>ChromeOS desk sync</strong><strong>&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p dir="ltr">Starting from ChromeOS 139, ChromeOS desk sync helps users quickly pick up from where they left off when switching to another device. Desk sync restores all windows, tabs, and even cookies from the previous session to allow for a seamless transition. Admins can switch on this feature for managed users. Desk sync is particularly useful for shared devices and frontline workers in healthcare, hospitality, and manufacturing settings. For more details, see our <a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/chrome-enterprise/chromeos-desk-sync-keeps-your-momentum-going-across-devices/?e=48754805" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>blog post</u></a> or our <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16465307" rel="noopener"><u>help center</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
    <img height="321" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXelJwLRlp0zhQ0xBRRt6v-F68CG9EEowtBNWILYl37PMFXYa3SFxCs_SYD4E0IIA34na7CtCz0nlEJootQ4o1rhGFWLC8RhGCyRF9yDAZNKy3Yc89yCNeJXa0eaZjU6rQtVSB7Lgw?key=CFZcym94sohYneMoogHZGw" width="642"><br>
    </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB139" name="chromeOSB139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome apps changes</strong><strong>&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p dir="ltr">Starting with ChromeOS 139, planned for stable release on August 19th, user-installed Chrome apps on ChromeOS will stop working. Apps that are force-installed through the admin console for Managed Guest sessions (MGS) and user sessions will continue to be supported. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15950395" rel="noopener" target="_blank">End of support for Chrome apps</a>.</p>

    <p dir="ltr">A new policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#KioskChromeAppsForceAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank">KioskChromeAppsForceAllowed</a>, is available for administrators to re-enable Chrome apps in kiosk sessions. With this policy turned on, Chrome apps in kiosk sessions will be supported through ChromeOS 150.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSC139" name="chromeOSC139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Native Client (NaCl) deprecation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p dir="ltr">ChromeOS 139 and later no longer supports <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Native Client (NaCl)</a> in managed environments with the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/?policy=NativeClientForceAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank">NaCl allow policy</a> enabled. For devices on the Long-term Support (LTS) channel with this policy active, NaCl support will continue to be supported until the ChromeOS 138 LTS Last Refresh in April 2026.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSD139" name="chromeOSD139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Touchscreen calibration tool</strong><strong>&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p dir="ltr">With ChromeOS 139, you can now calibrate boundaries of external touch screen displays. Chromebook users can now calibrate boundaries of external touch screen displays connected to a Chromebook. This setting helps with aligning external display boundaries, so that touch inputs correspond correctly to the displayed content. To calibrate the external touch screen display, go to Settings &gt; Device &gt; Display, go to the corresponding external touchscreen display and access Calibrate touchscreen. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/1060909" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Connect your Chromebook to a monitor</a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<p class="align-right"><a href="#top">↑ back to top</a> &nbsp;</p>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA139" name="upChromeOSA139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Chrome Sign Builder deprecation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p dir="ltr">The Chrome Sign Builder Chrome App is scheduled to reach its end of life in July 2026, with ChromeOS M150 being the final release to support it in kiosk mode. Devices on the Long-term Support (LTS) channel will continue to receive support until April 2027. This deprecation means that after the specified timelines, Chrome Sign Builder will no longer be available for installation or configuration, potentially leading to service disruptions for organizations currently utilizing it for digital signage.</p>

    <p dir="ltr">To avoid any interruptions, organizations must migrate to an alternative solution before July 2026. Two recommended options are</p>

    <ul>
      <li dir="ltr">
        <p dir="ltr">Migrate to Comeen: A Chrome Enterprise Recommended Partner that offers a web app replacement (<a href="http://comeen.com" rel="noopener" target="_blank">comeen.com</a>)</p>
      </li>
      <li dir="ltr">
        <p dir="ltr">Deploy alternative web apps: Utilize the Google Admin console to deploy other web apps to ChromeOS kiosk devices.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB139" name="upChromeOSB139"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>EAP/TLS server certificate validation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p><strong>Note: </strong>This change only affects customers utilizing EAP/TLS network setups and only affects networks set up before January of 2022.</p>

    <p>Starting October 1, 2025, we will roll out this fix to the ChromeOS stable channel. A very small number of customers using EAP/TLS configurations might experience connectivity issues if their server certificates are signed by a Certificate Authority (CA) that is currently included in ChromeOS as a System CA.</p>

    <p>To minimize disruption, admins can perform one of the following actions:</p>

    <p><strong>Option 1</strong> (providing a higher level of security):</p>

    <ol>
      <li>Generate a new certificate for your Authentication Server, and ensure it is signed by the same Certificate Authority (CA) as used previously.</li>
      <li>Replace the existing certificates on your Authentication Server with the newly-generated certificates.</li>
    </ol>
    &nbsp;

    <p><strong>Option 2</strong> ( if more time is needed before implementing Option 1):</p>

    <ol>
      <li>Sign in to Google Admin console.</li>
      <li>
        <p>From August 15 to October 1, to check for affected devices, admins can follow these instructions on the Beta channel:</p>

        <ul>
          <li>Access chrome://histograms in Chrome browser.</li>
          <li>Perform several disconnect and reconnect cycles for your Ethernet or Wi-Fi network.</li>
          <li>Allow approximately 10 seconds for data aggregation.</li>
          <li>Within the chrome://histograms page, search the histogram identified as <code>Network.Shill.Eap.EventCaCertExperiment1</code>:
            <ol>
              <li>If the histogram is not present, your configuration is not impacted.</li>
              <li>Your configuration is likely to be impacted if a positive value is observed for both Event 8 (<code>FirstCertVerificationFailure</code>) and Event 9 (<code>CertVerificationRetryAttempt</code>).</li>
            </ol>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>Navigate to the configuration settings for the affected EAP/TLS network.</li>
      <li>Modify the <strong>Server Certificate Authority</strong> setting to <strong>System default certificate authorities</strong>.</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

    <p>AI Mode is a feature that helps users dive deeper into topics they care about by showing AI Mode for search recommendations in Chrome. A new policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AIModeSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AIModeSettings</u></a>, is available to control search recommendations in the address bar and <strong>New tab</strong> page search box.&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Bookmarks and reading list improvements on Chrome Desktop&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>For Chrome 138 on Desktop, some users who sign in to Chrome upon saving a new bookmark can now use and save bookmarks and reading list items in their Google Account. Relevant enterprise policies controlling bookmarks, as well as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncDisabled</u></a> or <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a>, continue to work as before, so admins can configure whether or not users can use and save items in their Google Account. Setting <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EditBookmarksEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EditBookmarksEnabled</u></a> to false also prevents users from uploading a bookmark saved on their device to their Google Account.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC138" name="chromeBrsrC138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Client’s LLM assistance in mitigating scams&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Users on the web are facing significant amounts of different kinds of scams a day. To combat these scams, Chrome now uses on-device LLM to identify scam websites for Enhanced Safe Browsing users. Chrome sends the page content to an on-device LLM to infer security-related signals of the page and send these signals to the Safe Browsing server for a final verdict. When enabled, Chrome can consume more bandwidth to download the LLM.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Enhanced Safe Browsing is an existing feature, controlled by the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 134 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Gather the brand name and intent summary of the page that triggers keyboard lock to identify scam websites.</li>
      <li>Chrome 135 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Show the warnings to the user based on the server verdict, which uses the brand and intent summary of the page that triggered keyboard lock.</li>
      <li>Chrome 137 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Gather brand and intent summary of the page based on server reputation scoring system.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>: Show the warnings to the user based on the server verdict, which uses the brand and intent of the pages that the server reputation system scored.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD138" name="chromeBrsrD138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Contextual search suggestions in Chrome Address bar&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>With this feature you can ask anything about the page you’re on, directly in context. Building on the existing Search habit of the address bar, users can ask a question with Google Lens by selecting anything on screen or asking with words. A Google Lens action in the address bar and contextual suggestions guide people to the feature when it’s most helpful. This feature is gated by the existing <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Feature starts rollout</li>
      <li>Chrome 140 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: If the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a> policy is not set this feature will respect the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> policy if present.</li>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE138" name="chromeBrsrE138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Enhanced Safe Browsing is a synced setting&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In Chrome 138, Chrome's Enhanced Safe Browsing is a synced feature. This means that if a user opts into Enhanced Safe Browsing on one device, this protection level automatically applies across all other devices where they are signed into Chrome with the same account. The goal is to provide stronger, more consistent security protection and a standardized user experience.</p>

    <p>Users who enable Enhanced Safe Browsing benefit from its protections, for example, proactive phishing protection, improved detection of malware and malicious extensions&nbsp;consistently across their synced Chrome instances on Desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS), Android, and iOS. Users receive onscreen notifications&nbsp;when their Enhanced Safe Browsing setting is synced.</p>

    <p>The Safe Browsing protection level is an existing feature, controlled by the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrF138" name="chromeBrsrF138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Generating insights for Chrome DevTools console warnings and errors&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>A new Generative AI (GenAI) feature is now available for unmanaged users: Generating insights for Chrome <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/console/understand-messages" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DevTools console warnings and errors</u></a>. These insights provide a personalized description and suggested fixes for the selected errors and warnings. Initially, this feature is available to users (18+) in English only. Admins can control this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DevToolsGenAiSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DevToolsGenAiSettings</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 131 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: In Chrome 131, a new Generative AI (GenAI) feature becomes available for managed users: a dedicated <em>AI assistance</em> panel in Chrome DevTools which assists the human operator investigating &amp; fixing styling challenges and helps debugging the CSS.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: The AI assistance panel can now explain resources in the Performance panel, Sources panel, and Network panel, in addition to the previous support for style debugging.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The AI assistance panel exposes an internal API that simplifies the use of AI assistance panel features by external tools such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.</li>

<ul>
  <li><strong>History sync opt-in using the profile pill&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In Chrome 138, some signed-in users see a new option to opt in to history and tab sync. This change is designed to offer the benefits of history sync in a non-disruptive way by using the profile pill to display a short in-line message. Users who click on the profile pill are taken to their profile menu where they can choose to turn on sync. The goal is to provide users with an intuitive and contextually relevant entry point for syncing data like browsing history, separate from the sign-in flow. For Enterprise users, the expanded profile pill only appears after 4 hours of browser inactivity.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Relevant enterprise policies controlling History or Tab sync (<a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncDisabled</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SavingBrowserHistoryDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SavingBrowserHistoryDisabled</u></a>) continue to work as before.</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrH138" name="chromeBrsrH138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New tab page footer&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>An update to the <strong>New tab</strong> page includes a new footer designed to provide users with greater transparency and control over their Chrome experience.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Extension Attribution&nbsp;will begin to show on the NTP. If an extension has changed your default <strong>New tab</strong> page, you'll now see a message in the footer that attributes the change to that specific extension. This message often includes a link directly to the extension in the Chrome Web Store, making it easier to identify and manage unwanted extensions. If you're an administrator, you can disable this attribution using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#NTPFooterExtensionAttributionEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>NTPFooterExtensionAttributionEnabled</u></a> policy.</li>
      <li>Chrome 139 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Browser management disclosure will be shown if one of the policies to customize the footer is set by an enterprise admin. For users whose Chrome browser is managed by a trusted source, the <strong>New tab</strong> page footer will now display a management disclosure notice. This helps you understand how your browser is being managed. Administrators can disable this notice with the <strong>NTPFooterManagementNoticeEnabled</strong> policy. Additionally, organizations can customize the footer's appearance using the <strong>EnterpriseLogoUrlForBrowser</strong> and <strong>EnterpriseCustomLabelForBrowser</strong> policies to display a custom logo and label.</li>
      <li>Chrome 140 on Linux, macOS, Windows: A default notice (<em>Managed by &lt;domain name&gt;</em>) will start to be shown in the <strong>New tab</strong> page footer for all managed browsers. Visibility can be changed with the <strong>NTPFooterManagementNoticeEnabled</strong> policy.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/C3w5leJiEnB6OeDPhAscnjs5MKbzsr78OdD3N-hTlkSEe4pOkKMsfkBWbwz9khmBXiM=w895" width="1015" height="748" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/C3w5leJiEnB6OeDPhAscnjs5MKbzsr78OdD3N-hTlkSEe4pOkKMsfkBWbwz9khmBXiM"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrI138" name="chromeBrsrI138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Per-extension user script toggle&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In Chrome 138, the way that users and administrators control an extension’s ability to run user created scripts and use the <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/userScripts" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>userScripts API</u></a> is changing. This change enhances security. Users won’t unintentionally grant user script permissions to every extension when enabling <strong>Developer mode</strong> by explicitly deciding which extensions can run these potentially powerful scripts. For more detail on the motivation for the change, see this <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-userscript" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome for developers</u></a> blog.</p>

    <p>End users will now toggle this per extension on the <code>chrome://extensions</code> page via a <strong>Allow User Scripts</strong> toggle, replacing the global <strong>Developer mode</strong> toggle for more granular control. Existing extensions will have this toggle automatically enabled if <strong>Developer mode</strong> is on and the extension has been granted the User Scripts permission.</p>

    <p>Administrators who currently manage user scripts by disabling developer mode should now use the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/9867568" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>blocked_permissions field of the </u></a><a href="https://cloud.google.com/docs/chrome-enterprise/policies/?policy=ExtensionSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensionSettings policy</u></a> or the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7515036" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Google Admin console</u></a> to independently control the User Scripts permission and extension <strong>Developer mode</strong>.</p>

    <p>Extension developers are advised to update their documentation to reflect the new toggle. See the <a href="https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium Extensions Google Groups</u></a> mailing list for more information and other changes to usage of the API.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Feature rolls out</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/TEzlOVmxNOpvDyzSFjL6m5tnsCFrj6G2gl4CQyPWHzqb_kkO-RsNKBQ_RqFJbF6DYhU=w512" width="512" height="70" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/TEzlOVmxNOpvDyzSFjL6m5tnsCFrj6G2gl4CQyPWHzqb_kkO-RsNKBQ_RqFJbF6DYhU"></li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrJ138" name="chromeBrsrJ138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Removal of Private Network Access enterprise policies&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Private Network Access (PNA 1.0) is an unshipped security feature designed to limit website access to local networks. Due to deployability concerns, PNA 1.0 was never able to ship by default, as it was incompatible with too many existing devices.</p>

    <p>PNA 1.0 required changes to devices on local networks. Instead, Chrome is implementing an updated proposal, Private Network Access 2.0 (PNA 2.0) (<a href="https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/local-network-access" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>). PNA 2.0 only requires changes to sites that need to access the local network, rather than requiring changes to devices on the local network. Sites are much easier to update than devices, and so this approach should be much more straightforward to roll out.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>The only way to enforce PNA 1.0 is via enterprise policy. To avoid regressing security for enterprise customers opting-in to PNA 1.0 prior to shipping PNA 2.0, we will maintain the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled</u></a> policy, which causes Chrome to send special preflight messages, until such time that it becomes incompatible with PNA 2.0.</p>

    <p>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed</u></a> policies, which loosen PNA 1.0 restrictions, will be removed immediately. These policies currently have no effect, since PNA 1.0 is not shipped, and they will have no meaning once PNA 1.0 is removed.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 135 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia: Deprecate <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed</u></a>, and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled</u></a> policies.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia:</strong> Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed</u></a>. There should be a PNA2 replacement policy available in Chrome 138.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrK138" name="chromeBrsrK138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Search your screen with Google Lens on iPad&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Expand <strong>Search your screen with Google Lens</strong> on iOS so it is available on iPad devices. iPad is a form factor typically associated with more complex tasks, for example, shopping, and expanding Lens functionality on iPad enables users to perform these tasks easily. Admins can control this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a> policy.&nbsp;</p>
