<p><a id="chromeBrsrL138" name="chromeBrsrL138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Shared tab groups&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Users can now collaborate on tabs using the shared tab groups feature. With this feature, users can create and use a set of tabs on their desktop or mobile device and their collaborative partners can browse the same tabs on their devices. When one person changes a tab in the group, the changes are reflected across all users’ browsers in the group. An enterprise policy, TabGroupSharingSettings, is available to control this feature.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Rollout of the ability to join and use a shared tab group. Users on Stable Chrome will not be able to create a shared tab group (the entry point will not be available) - this part of the feature will only be available on Beta/Dev/Canary for this phase of rollout.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>Chrome 139 on iOS:&nbsp; As early as Chrome 139, support for iOS will roll out.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrM138" name="chromeBrsrM138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Speculation rules prefetch for ServiceWorker&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature enables Service Worker-controlled prefetches, that is, a speculation rules prefetch to URLs controlled by a Service Worker. Previously, the prefetch is cancelled upon detecting a controlling Service Worker, thus subsequent navigation to the prefetch target is served by the non-prefetch path. This feature enables the prefetch request to go through the Service Worker's fetch handler and the response with the Service Worker interception is cached in the prefetch cache, resulting in a subsequent navigation being served by the prefetch cache. Please use the enterprise policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrefetchWithServiceWorkerEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrefetchWithServiceWorkerEnabled</u></a> to control this feature. For more details, see <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/192ZLkKcaUE_9Qt8bW9OZLViEEbtxOAgq5WYR87m79IE/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.8i2u299uv5yh" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>this</u></a> explainer.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrN138" name="chromeBrsrN138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>TLS 1.3 Early Data&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>TLS 1.3 Early Data allows GET requests to be sent during the handshake when resuming a connection to a compatible TLS 1.3 server. The feature is expected to demonstrate performance improvements and will be available in Chrome 138 with a policy (<a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TLS13EarlyDataEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TLS13EarlyDataEnabled</u></a>) to control this change.</p>

    <p>TLS 1.3 Early Data is an established protocol. Existing TLS servers, middleboxes, and security software are expected to either handle or reject TLS 1.3 Early Data without dropping the connection. However, devices that do not correctly implement the TLS standard (RFC8446) might malfunction and disconnect when TLS 1.3 Early Data is in use. If this occurs, administrators should contact the vendor for a fix.</p>

    <p>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TLS13EarlyDataEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TLS13EarlyDataEnabled</u></a>&nbsp;policy is a temporary measure to control the feature and will be removed in a future milestone. You can turn on the feature using the policy&nbsp;to allow you to test for issues and turn it off again&nbsp;as issues are resolved.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrO138" name="chromeBrsrO138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate asynchronous range removal for Media Source extensions&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/media-source-2/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Media Source standard</u></a> changed in the past to disallow ambiguously-defined behavior involving asynchronous range removals:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><code>SourceBuffer.abort()</code> no longer aborts <code>SourceBuffer.remove()</code> operations</li>
      <li>Setting <code>MediaSource.duration</code> can no longer truncate currently buffered media</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>Exceptions are thrown in both of these cases now. Safari and Firefox have long shipped this behavior; Chromium is the last browser remaining with the old behavior. Use counters show ~0.001%-0.005% of page loads hit the deprecated behavior. If a site hits this issue, playback may now break. Usage of abort() cancelling removals is increasing, so it's prudent to resolve this deprecation before more incompatible usage appears.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrP138" name="chromeBrsrP138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Language Detector API&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Language Detector API is a JavaScript API for detecting the language of text, with confidence levels. An important supplement to translation is language detection. This can be combined with translation, for example, taking user input in an unknown language and translating it to a specific target language. Browsers today often already have language detection capabilities, and we want to offer them to web developers through a JavaScript API, supplementing the translation API. An enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings</u></a>, is available to disable the underlying model downloading, which would render this API unavailable.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrQ138" name="chromeBrsrQ138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Summarizer API&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Summarizer API is a JavaScript API for producing summaries of input text, backed by an AI language model. Browsers and operating systems are increasingly expected to gain access to a language model. By exposing this built-in model, we avoid every website needing to download their own multi-gigabyte language model, or send input text to third-party APIs. The Summarizer API, in particular, exposes a high-level API for interfacing with a language model to summarize inputs for a variety of use cases (<a href="https://github.com/webmachinelearning/writing-assistance-apis/blob/main/README.md#summarizer-api" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>), in a way that does not depend on a specific language model.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>An enterprise policy (<a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings</u></a>) is available to disable the underlying model downloading, which would render this API unavailable.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrR138" name="chromeBrsrR138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>

    <p>Translator API is a JavaScript API to provide language translation capabilities to web pages. Browsers are increasingly offering language translation to their users. Such translation capabilities can also be useful to web developers. This is especially the case when the browser's built-in translation abilities cannot help. An enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings</u></a>, is available to disable the underlying model downloading, which would render this API unavailable.</p>

  <li><strong>Inactive profile deletion in Chrome Enterprise Core&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In June 2025, the inactive period for profile deletion setting started to roll out. In July 2025, the setting will begin to automatically delete managed profiles in the Admin console that have been inactive for more than the defined inactivity period. The inactivity period of time has a default value of 90 days. By default, all managed profiles that have been inactive for more than 90 days are deleted from your account. Administrators can change the inactive period value using this setting. The maximum value to determine the profile inactivity period is 730 days and the minimum value is 28 days.</p>

    <p>If you lower the set value, it might have a global impact on any currently managed profiles. All impacted profiles will be considered inactive and, therefore, be deleted. This does not delete the user account. If an inactive profile is re-activated on a device, that profile will reappear in the console.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Policy will roll out in June. Deletion will start in July and the initial wave of deletion will complete by the end of August. After the initial deletion rollout, inactive profiles will continue to be deleted once they have reached their inactivity period.</li>
    </ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome Enterprise Premium changes</h2>

<p>Read more about the differences between <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/products/chrome-enterprise-premium" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise Core and Chrome Enterprise Premium</u></a>.</p>

<p><a id="chromeEPA138" name="chromeEPA138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SecOps integration&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>This feature delivers a native integration between Chrome Enterprise Premium (CEP) and Google Security Operations (SecOps), enabling organizations to send a richer set of security events and detailed browser telemetry from Chrome directly to their SecOps instance. The motivation for this change is to use the browser as a primary security sensor for web-based threats like phishing, malware, and data exfiltration. This can significantly improve an organization's ability to:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>prevent</li>
      <li>detect</li>
      <li>investigate</li>
      <li>and respond to web-based threats.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>For administrators, this integration introduces new, enhanced security event types, including URL navigation telemetry and suspicious URL visits. These events are automatically enriched with Safe Browsing risk scores and other threat intelligence before being sent to SecOps. The launch also includes a new, streamlined "one-click" setup process in the Admin console to replace the previous manual workflow, simplifying the connection to SecOps.</p>

    <p>To use this feature, administrators must have a Chrome Enterprise Premium subscription and will need to enable the integration through the new workflow in the Admin console. The collection of certain high-volume event types, such as URL navigation events, is an opt-in setting within the connector configuration. This feature does not add or modify any enterprise policies.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 137 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Adds referrer data to <code>URLFilteringInterstitialEvent</code> and <code>SafeBrowseInterstitialEvent</code></li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Linux, macOS, Windows:</strong> Extends referrer data population to <code>SafeBrowseDangerousDownloadEvent</code> and <code>DlpSensitiveDataEvent</code></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeEPB138" name="chromeEPB138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>URL Filtering capabilities on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>The current WebProtect URL Filtering capabilities on Desktop are being extended to mobile so that organizations can audit, warn, or block certain URLs or categories of URLs from loading on managed Chrome browsers or managed user profiles on mobile devices. This feature is part of Chrome Enterprise Premium and aims to provide secure and safe internet access for enterprise users on any device. Admins can create URL filtering rules to ensure that employees can only access safe and authorized URLs on iOS devices. Chrome reports URL filtering events and unsafe site events via the Reporting Connector on mobile. This feature allows administrators to manage which URLs can be accessed on managed Chrome browsers or profiles on company-owned or BYOD iOS devices.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Key changes include:</p>

    <p>- Admins can block, warn, or audit users when accessing certain sites or categories.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>- Users see interstitial pages when attempting to visit blocked or warned URLs.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>- Chrome reports URL filtering events.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>- Updates to the <code>chrome://management</code> page reflect the new functionality.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on iOS:</strong> The URL Filtering feature becomes available on iOS.</li>
    </ul>

<p><a id="chromeEPC138" name="chromeEPC138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>DLP Download Support for File System Access API (FSA)&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>Data Loss Prevention (DLP) protection now covers files and directories downloaded using the <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/file-system-access" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>File System Access (FSA) API</u></a>. This enhancement ensures that downloads from modern web applications, such as browser-based editors, are scanned according to your organization's DLP rules. Users and websites receive notifications on scan verdicts, strengthening data security and compliance. If a download violates a DLP policy, it is blocked, resulting in an empty file, and the website might indicate a "Blocked by Safe Browsing" error. This change primarily benefits security by preventing data exfiltration through this vector. Administrators should test this with web applications using the FSA API to observe the behavior with their current DLP configurations.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Enables DLP content analysis for downloads initiated via File System Access API on selected platforms, governed by existing enterprise policies.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

  <li><strong>Malicious APK download checks</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome on Android will now contact Google servers about APK files downloaded in Chrome, to get a verdict about their safety. If a downloaded APK file is determined to be dangerous, Chrome will show a warning and block the download, to protect users against mobile malware. Such download warnings will be bypassable by the user through the Chrome UI. These malicious APK download checks will be performed for users enrolled in Standard Protection or Enhanced Protection from Google Safe Browsing. This feature can be disabled by setting the Safe Browsing mode to "No Protection" via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel</u></a> policy.</p>

    <p><a href="https://img536-dot-cr-status.appspot.com/feature/6284403671826432/attachment/5121779097665536"><strong><u><img height="530" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd45OHLT6Nxcz8gy5_434myxfDxLcygmCnSzIVZ959W5RuoNipr1ujj9SlJrQEfj85FMFLV8-9ZsxUXCDxeMLEsmsVhlpXa5gEP6Bh2pMv2EJNBw8rJfKR78CMuvxym_c-o1ZCvbFzdkyO-R_SlJJUQL_dYKR4XVxWKhFHbKUmS2NNM?key=T_n_QOlTLKvRPMS_dO8mww" width="316"></u></strong></a></p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrD138" name="upChromeBrsrD138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Upcoming change for CA certificates included in the Chrome Root Store</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In response to sustained compliance failures, Chrome 139 changes how publicly-trusted TLS server authentication, that is, websites or certificates issued by Chunghwa Telecom and Netlock, are trusted by default. This applies to Chrome 139 and later on Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, and Linux; iOS policies do not allow use of the Chrome Root Store in Chrome for iOS.</p>

    <p>Specifically, TLS certificates validating to the Chunghwa Telecom or Netlock root CA certificates included in the Chrome Root Store and issued:</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- after July 31, 2025, will no longer be trusted by default.</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- on or before July 31, 2025, will be unaffected by this change.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>If a Chrome user or an enterprise explicitly trusts any of the affected Chunghwa Telecom or Netlock certificates on a platform and version of Chrome relying on the Chrome Root Store, for example, when explicit trust is conveyed through a Windows Group Policy Object, the Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT) constraints described above will be overridden and certificates will function as they do today.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For additional information and testing resources, see <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2025/05/sustaining-digital-certificate-security-chrome-root-store-changes.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Sustaining Digital Certificate Security - Upcoming Changes to the Chrome Root Store</u></a>.</p>

    <p>To learn more about the Chrome Root Store, see this <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/net/data/ssl/chrome_root_store/faq.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>FAQ</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows:</strong> All versions of Chrome 139 and higher that rely on the Chrome Root Store will honor the blocking action, but the blocking action will only begin for certificates issued after July 31, 2025.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrE138" name="upChromeBrsrE138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Migrate extensions to Manifest V3 before June 2025</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Extensions must be updated to leverage Manifest V3. Chrome extensions are transitioning to a new manifest version, Manifest V3. This will bring improved privacy for your users—for example, by moving to a model where extensions modify requests declaratively, without the ability to see individual requests. This also improves extension security, as remotely hosted code will be disallowed on Manifest V3.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>In June 2024, Chrome began to gradually disable Manifest V2 extensions running in the browser. An Enterprise policy - <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensionManifestV2Availability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensionManifestV2Availability</u></a> - can be used to test Manifest V3 in your organization ahead of the migration. Additionally, machines on which the policy is enabled will not be subject to the disabling of Manifest V2 extensions until the following year - June 2025 - at which point the policy will be removed.</p>

    <p>You can see which Manifest version is being used by all Chrome extensions running on your fleet using the Apps &amp; extensions usage page in Chrome Enterprise Core.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 127 on ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Chrome will gradually disable Manifest V2 extensions on user devices. Only those with the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensionManifestV2Availability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensionManifestV2Availability</u></a> enterprise policy enabled would be able to continue using Manifest V2 extensions in their organization.</li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Remove <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensionManifestV2Availability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensionManifestV2Availability</u></a> policy.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrG138" name="upChromeBrsrG138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove risky extension flags in Google Chrome</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To enhance the security and stability of the Chrome browser for our users, official Chrome branded builds will be removing <code>--extensions-on-chrome-urls</code> and <code>--disable-extensions-except</code> command-line flags starting in Chrome 139. This change aims to mitigate the risks associated with harmful and unwanted extensions.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Developers can still use the both flags in non-branded builds such as <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium and Chrome For Testing</u></a><strong>.</strong></p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Gradual roll-out&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH138" name="upChromeBrsrH138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove SwiftShader fallback</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Allowing automatic fallback to <a href="https://get.webgl.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebGL</u></a> backed by <a href="https://github.com/google/swiftshader" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SwiftShader</u></a> is deprecated and WebGL context creation now fails instead of falling back to SwiftShader.&nbsp; This was done for two primary reasons:&nbsp;</p>

    <ol>
      <li>SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process.</li>
      <li>Users have a poor experience when falling back from a high-performance GPU-backed WebGL to a CPU-backed implementation. Users have no control over this behavior and it is difficult to describe in bug reports.</li>
    </ol>

    <p>SwiftShader is a useful tool for web developers to test their sites on systems that are headless or do not have a supported GPU. This use case will still be supported by opting in but is not intended for running untrusted content. To opt in to lower security guarantees and allow SwiftShader for WebGL, run the chrome executable with the <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> command-line switch.</p>

    <p>During the deprecation period, a warning will appear in the javascript console when a WebGL context is created and backed with SwiftShader. Passing <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> will remove this warning message.</p>

    <p>Chromium and other browsers do not guarantee WebGL availability. It is important to test and handle WebGL context creation failure and fall back to other web APIs such as Canvas2D or an appropriate message to the user. A temporary enterprise policy will be available in Chrome 138 to revert the change.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 137 on Windows: SwiftShader will be disabled and replaced with another software WebGL fallback, WARP. Tests depending on the exact pixel values generated by SwiftShader may start failing.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Linux, macOS: </strong>Swiftshader will be disabled on macOS and Linux as early as Chrome 138. Users on machines without a GPU will not be able to use WebGL.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrI138" name="upChromeBrsrI138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support accounts in pending state on Chrome iOS</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Accounts whose credentials somehow became invalid will no longer be automatically signed out and removed from Chrome on iOS. Instead, these accounts will stay signed in to the browser, in a newly introduced "pending state" associated with a persistent error indication in the UI so users are encouraged to resolve it. This also means that local data associated with these accounts will no longer be automatically deleted, but instead kept on disk. Existing policies controlling sign-in (for example, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a>) will continue to work as before.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on iOS:</strong> Feature will gradually roll out&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ138" name="upChromeBrsrJ138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome to remove support for macOS 11</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 138 will be the last release to support macOS 11; Chrome 139+ will no longer support macOS 11, which is outside of its support window with Apple. Running on a supported operating system is essential to maintaining security.</p>

    <p>On Macs running macOS 11, Chrome will continue to work, showing a warning infobar, but will not update any further. If a user wishes to have their Chrome&nbsp;updated, they need to update their computer to a support version of macOS. For new installations of Chrome 139+, macOS 12+ will be required.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK138" name="upChromeBrsrK138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Clear window name for cross-site navigations that switches browsing context group</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The value of the <code>window.name</code> property is currently preserved throughout the lifetime of a tab, even with navigation that switches browsing context groups, which can leak information and potentially be used as a tracking vector. Clear the <code>window.name</code> property in this case addresses this issue.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This update will introduce a new temporary enterprise policy, <strong>ClearWindowNameCrossSiteBrowsing</strong>, which will stop working in Chrome 142.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL138" name="upChromeBrsrL138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Fire error event instead of throwing exception for CSP blocked worker</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>When blocked by <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Content Security Policy (CSP)</u></a>, Chromium currently throws a SecurityError from the constructor of Worker and SharedWorker. To be spec-compliant,&nbsp; the CSP needs to be checked as part of fetch and then fire error events asynchronously instead of throwing an exception when the script runs "<code>new Worker(url)</code>" or "<code>new SharedWorker(url)</code>".&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This update aims to make Chromium spec-conformant, which is, it no longer throws exceptions following constructor calls, and fires error events asynchronously.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrM138" name="upChromeBrsrM138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Web App Manifest: specify update eligibility, icon URLs are Cache-Control: immutable</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As early as Chrome 139, the Web App manifest will specify an update eligibility algorithm. This makes the update process more deterministic and predictable, giving the developer more control over whether (and when) updates should apply to existing installations, and allowing removal of the 'update check throttle' that user agents currently need to implement to avoid wasting network resources.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
      <li>Chrome 140 on Android</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrN138" name="upChromeBrsrN138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>2SV enforcement for admins</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To better protect your organization’s information, Google will soon require all accounts with access to admin.google.com to have 2-Step Verification (2SV) enabled. As a Google Workspace administrator, you need to confirm your identity with 2SV, which requires your password plus something additional, such as your phone or a security key.</p>

    <p>The enforcement will be rolled out gradually over the coming months. You should enable 2SV for the admin accounts in your organization before Google enforces it. For more information, see this <a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/16271818" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Help Center article</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 137 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: 2SV enforcement starts</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: 2SV mandatory</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrO138" name="upChromeBrsrO138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Happy Eyeballs V3</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This launch is an internal optimization in Chrome that implements <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-happy-happyeyeballs-v3/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Happy Eyeballs V3</u></a> to achieve better network connection concurrency. Happy Eyeballs V3 performs DNS resolutions asynchronously and staggers connection attempts with preferable protocols (H3/H2/H1) and address families (IPv6 or IPv4) to reduce user-visible network connection delay. This feature is gated by a temporary policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HappyEyeballsV3Enabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HappyEyeballsV3Enabled</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrP138" name="upChromeBrsrP138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Isolated Web Apps</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Isolated Web Apps (IWAs) are an extension of existing work on PWA installation and Web Packaging that provide stronger protections against server compromise and other tampering that is necessary for developers of security-sensitive applications.</p>

    <p>Rather than being hosted on live web servers and fetched over HTTPS, these applications are packaged into Web Bundles, signed by their developer, and distributed to end-users through one or more of the potential methods described in the <a href="https://github.com/WICG/isolated-web-apps/blob/main/README.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>explainer</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>In this initial release, IWAs will only be installable through an admin policy on enterprise-managed ChromeOS devices.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows </strong>This rollout adds support for Isolated Web Apps in enterprise-managed browser configurations on Windows.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrQ138" name="upChromeBrsrQ138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow non-trustworthy plaintext HTTP prerendering</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This launch will provide the capability to disallow non-trustworthy plaintext HTTP prerendering.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrR138" name="upChromeBrsrR138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>HSTS tracking prevention</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This update will mitigate user tracking by third-parties via the <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6797" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)</u></a> cache. This feature only allows HSTS upgrades for top-level navigations and blocks HSTS upgrades for sub-resource requests. Doing so makes it infeasible for third-party sites to use the HSTS cache in order to track users across the web.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrS138" name="upChromeBrsrS138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>IP Protection</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature&nbsp; limits availability of a user’s original IP address in third-party contexts in <strong>Incognito mode</strong>, enhancing Incognito's protections against cross-site tracking when users choose to browse in this mode. IP addresses facilitate a range of use cases, including routing traffic and preventing fraud and spam. However, they can also be used for tracking. For Chrome users who choose to browse in Incognito mode, we want to provide additional control over their IP address, without breaking essential web functionality. To strike this balance between protection and usability, this proposal focuses on limiting the use of IP addresses in a third-party context in Incognito mode. To that end, this proposal uses a list-based approach, where only domains on the <a href="https://support.google.com/privacysandbox/answer/16085975?hl=en&amp;ref_topic=16076404#:~:text=The%20Masked%20Domain%20List%20(MDL)%20is%20a%20list%20of%20domains,in%20the%20IP%20Protection%20explainer." rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Masked Domain List (MDL)</u></a> in a third-party context will be impacted. For enterprises, this feature can be controlled via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivacySandboxIpProtectionEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivacySandboxIpProtectionEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrT138" name="upChromeBrsrT138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Strict Same Origin Policy for Storage Access API</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>We plan to adjust the <a href="https://privacysandbox.google.com/cookies/storage-access-api" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Storage Access API</u></a> semantics to strictly follow the Same Origin Policy, to enhance&nbsp;security. Using <code>document.requestStorageAccess()</code> in a frame only attaches cookies to requests to the iframe's origin (not site) by default. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a> policy or Storage Access Headers can still be used to unblock cross-site cookies.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrU138" name="upChromeBrsrU138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL hosts</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>According to the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL Standard specification</u></a>, URL hosts cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host. This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a> and <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL focus</u></a> areas. To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows <code>file://</code> URLs (<a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>).</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 141 on Android, ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrV138" name="upChromeBrsrV138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 → v5 migration</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/reference" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>v5 API</u></a> instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5. If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4*</code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead: <code>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</code>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users. For more details, see <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/reference/Migration.From.V4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Migration From V4 - Safe Browsing</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 145 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Feature would gradually roll-out&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrW138" name="upChromeBrsrW138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome will start directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Administrators may use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy starting in Chrome 125 to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 146, and will be removed in Chrome 147. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows: The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that administrators can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise administrators may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt out through Chrome 146.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147 on Windows:</strong> The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome Enterprise Premium changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeEPA138" name="upChromeEPA138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome browser rule UX refactor&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To enhance the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13876556" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Data Loss Prevention (DLP)</u></a> rule creation experience, the Google Admin console is being updated to streamline how administrators define policies for different applications like Chrome and Workspace. This first introduces mutually exclusive application groups, meaning that a single DLP rule can now only target one application group at a time—either Workspace apps (like Drive, Gmail), Chrome browser triggers (like file upload, URL visited), or ChromeOS triggers. This change simplifies rule configuration, eliminates potential conflicts from overlapping app selections, and lays the groundwork for more specialized and user-friendly workflows tailored to each platform's needs.</p>

    <p>Administrators will see an updated "Apps" selection interface using radio buttons to enforce this single-group selection for new rules. Existing rules that previously combined applications from multiple groups will be transparently migrated by the system into separate, compliant, single-platform rules to ensure continued protection and a seamless transition. Banners within the Admin console will provide information regarding these changes and the migration process. No new enterprise policies are introduced with this update; the changes are to the rule configuration interface.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows:&nbsp; </strong>Enables mutually exclusive app selection for DLP rule configuration in Admin console</li>
    </ul>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/_4uAw49xDsyDyZ3YYiGVwj0Hq23Vw_2vpTv5ZxOwiSbhCspklevaWLQ8VZJ1ovZbjfM=w509" width="509" height="512" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/_4uAw49xDsyDyZ3YYiGVwj0Hq23Vw_2vpTv5ZxOwiSbhCspklevaWLQ8VZJ1ovZbjfM"> &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeEPB138" name="upChromeEPB138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Copy and Paste rules protection&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To help organizations better prevent data exfiltration on mobile devices, Chrome is extending its existing desktop clipboard data controls. Administrators can now use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DataControlsRules" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DataControlsRules</u></a> policy to set rules that block or warn users when they attempt to copy or paste content that violates organizational policies. This feature allows admins to define data boundaries and prevent sensitive information from being pasted from a work context into personal apps or websites on their mobile fleet. This addresses a significant security gap and a frequently requested feature from enterprise customers who have cited the lack of mobile data controls as a concern. To use this feature, administrators can configure clipboard restrictions within the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DataControlsRules" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DataControlsRules</u></a> policy, providing a consistent management experience across desktop and mobile to strengthen their organization's overall security posture.</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>ChromeOS updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeOSA138" name="chromeOSA138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Class Tools&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Class Tools are premium teaching and learning tools built for Chromebooks. They aim to provide teachers with real-time classroom management tools and enhance learning for students. Class Tools help teachers to:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>send and lock website content on student Chromebooks.</li>
      <li>offer students on-screen captions and real-time translations.</li>
      <li>view and share students' screens.</li>
    </ul>

    <p>To learn more, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a?p=class_tools" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Overview of Class Tools</u></a> in the Help Center. To use Class Tools, your organization needs to have a <a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/6043385?co=DASHER._Family%3DEducation&amp;oco=0" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Google Workspace for Education Plus</a> or a&nbsp;<a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/15872457" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Teaching and Learning add-on</a> license. For more details, see <a href="https://edu.google.com/intl/ALL_us/workspace-for-education/editions/education-plus/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Education Plus edition</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/SmrK0gcHkOfvNOWcMRx9kf-Q6kirEbSzxGFsNc3MTivkEbMC3TGk536YPSyNBxQToBAB=w895" width="1015" height="350" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/SmrK0gcHkOfvNOWcMRx9kf-Q6kirEbSzxGFsNc3MTivkEbMC3TGk536YPSyNBxQToBAB"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB138" name="chromeOSB138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS freeform wallpapers&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 138, freeform wallpapers offer an unrestricted input field that empowers users to express their individuality, creativity, and passions by turning their background into a personal canvas. Users can generate wallpapers by inputting different prompts in the text field, or use the <strong>Inspire me</strong> feature, which will generate random prompts and wallpapers until you find one you like. This feature is available on Chromebook Plus devices only. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15966259" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Wallpaper settings</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Admins can control this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAIWallpaperSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAIWallpaperSettings</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>For 18+ consumers, the default is <em>Allow with data collection</em>.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>For 18+ managed users, the default is <em>Allow without data collection</em>.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>Users under 18 cannot access the feature.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>&nbsp;</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/Yb0szBpVsyt1WZa1iazy7BPpBzDtwgNYB7ZUy91ZRwt_C6Dr5FSjVhksz6KA-tZgeA=w895" width="941" height="692" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/Yb0szBpVsyt1WZa1iazy7BPpBzDtwgNYB7ZUy91ZRwt_C6Dr5FSjVhksz6KA-tZgeA"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSC138" name="chromeOSC138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Help me read on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 138, <strong>Help me read</strong> on ChromeOS provides an AI-powered solution to help you quickly understand text information written in verbose and convoluted language or with jargon. Select a piece of text and right-click on it to reveal the simplify button that can give you a straightforward version of the source, which can be digested at a glance.</p>

    <p>Admins can control access to this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HelpMeReadSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HelpMeReadSettings</u></a> policy, but users need to explicitly opt in to use <strong>Help me read</strong> on ChromeOS. This feature is available on <a href="https://www.google.com/chromebook/discover/chromebookplus/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromebook Plus</u></a> devices only. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14443058" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Chrome—Generative AI features and policies</a>.&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Expansion of the <em>Disabled system features</em> policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>We're releasing a significant expansion of the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/2657289?sjid=13736349125814409090-EU#system_features_disable_list&amp;zippy=%2Cdisabled-system-features" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Disabled system features</a> policy. You now have granular control over a wider range of applications, to allow for more tailored device management.<br>
      ChromeOS 138 supports disabling the following additional applications:</p>

    <p>This update provides administrators with enhanced flexibility to configure available apps according to specific organizational needs and security requirements.</p>

<p><a id="chromeOSF138" name="chromeOSF138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Accessibility updates&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 138, we've focused on refining the accessibility experience by addressing several key issues to improve usability and conformance.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Resolved issues:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Incorrect Heading Levels: The <strong>Wallpaper and style</strong> page now uses correct heading levels, improving navigation for screen reader users.</li>
      <li>Gallery App - Date Announcement: ChromeVox now accurately announces date information when browsing the Google Photos image list within the Gallery App.</li>
      <li>Gallery App - <strong>px</strong> Unit Announcement: To provide clearer context, the <strong>px</strong> unit is now announced by ChromeVox when navigating <strong>Width</strong> and <strong>Height</strong> fields for image rescaling in the Gallery App.</li>
      <li>Out-of-Box Experience (OOBE) - Redundant Announcements: We've streamlined ChromeVox announcements during OOBE updates. The progress indicator is now hidden from screen readers to prevent redundant announcements like <strong>Progress indicator, min 0 max 100</strong> and incorrect <strong>image</strong> announcements.</li>
      <li>Out-of-Box Experience (OOBE) - Focus Disruption: We’ve addressed an issue in OOBE where switching between personal and corporate account enrollment buttons with ChromeVox incorrectly shifted focus to the calendar. Focus now correctly remains on the updated screen or dialog.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA138" name="upChromeOSA138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Chrome apps changes&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Starting with ChromeOS 138, admin-installed Chrome apps in kiosk sessions will be disabled by default. A new policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#KioskChromeAppsForceAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>KioskChromeAppsForceAllowed</u></a>, will be available prior to the release of ChromeOS 138 for administrators to re-enable Chrome apps in kiosk sessions. With this policy turned on, Chrome apps in kiosk sessions will be supported through ChromeOS 150.</p>

    <p>Starting with ChromeOS 139, planned for stable release on August 19th, user-installed Chrome apps on ChromeOS will stop working. Apps that are force-installed through the admin console for Managed Guest sessions (MGS) and user sessions will continue to be supported. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15950395" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>End of support for Chrome apps</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a name="upChromeOSA138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Native Client (NaCl) deprecation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 138 will be the final release to support <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Native Client (NaCl)</u></a> in managed environments with the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/?policy=NativeClientForceAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>NaCl allow policy</u></a> enabled. For devices on the Long-term Support (LTS) channel with this policy active, NaCl support will continue until the LTS Last Refresh in April 2026.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a name="upChromeOSA138"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>EAP/TLS server certificate validation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p><strong>Note: </strong>This change only affects customers utilizing EAP/TLS network setups and only affects networks set up before January of 2022.</p>

    <p>Starting October 1, 2025, we will roll out this fix to the ChromeOS stable channel. A very small number of customers using EAP/TLS configurations might experience connectivity issues if their server certificates are signed by a Certificate Authority (CA) that is currently included in ChromeOS as a System CA.</p>

    <p>To minimize disruption, admins can perform one of the following actions:</p>

    <p><strong>Option 1</strong> (providing a higher level of security):</p>

    <ol>
      <li>Generate a new certificate for your Authentication Server, and ensure it is signed by the same Certificate Authority (CA) as used previously.</li>
      <li>Replace the existing certificates on your Authentication Server with the newly-generated certificates.</li>
    </ol>
    &nbsp;

    <p><strong>Option 2</strong> ( if more time is needed before implementing Option 1):</p>

    <ol>
      <li>Sign in to Google Admin console.</li>
      <li>
        <p>From August 15 to October 1, to check for affected devices, admins can follow these instructions on the Beta channel:</p>

        <ul>
          <li>Access chrome://histograms in Chrome browser.</li>
          <li>Perform several disconnect and reconnect cycles for your Ethernet or Wi-Fi network.</li>
          <li>Allow approximately 10 seconds for data aggregation.</li>
          <li>Within the chrome://histograms page, search the histogram identified as <code>Network.Shill.Eap.EventCaCertExperiment1</code>:
            <ol>
              <li>If the histogram is not present, your configuration is not impacted.</li>
              <li>Your configuration is likely to be impacted if a positive value is observed for both Event 8 (<code>FirstCertVerificationFailure</code>) and Event 9 (<code>CertVerificationRetryAttempt</code>).</li>
            </ol>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>Navigate to the configuration settings for the affected EAP/TLS network.</li>
      <li>Modify the <strong>Server Certificate Authority</strong> setting to <strong>System default certificate authorities</strong>.</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes &nbsp;</h2>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA137" name="chromeBrsrA137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Gemini in Chrome&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Gemini is now integrated into Chrome on macOS and Windows, and can understand the content of your current page. Users can now seamlessly get key takeaways, clarify concepts, and find answers, all without leaving their Chrome tab. This integration includes both chat—where users can interact with Gemini via text, and Gemini Live&nbsp;<img height="24" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfWX0Yv-GoWwZ94KZmBHx8p2JCkkQrOi4SDzfW_HWB5pe5ZtOuDYLL25Gu4TUk05pZwSxO8nVylPeMrDtu4t-g9PUAKhSYhaU-DtFq1BS8rDRXefw3Qg15c6XSAIifiRCe-K7POa28?key=O_4ml0A9doys7qE1X2IgS9q0" width="24">, by which users can interact with Gemini via voice.</p>

    <p>In Chrome 137, <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16291696" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Gemini in Chrome</u></a> is available for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the US. A broader rollout will come in future milestones. You can check the upcoming publications of these Enterprise Release Notes for availability updates.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Admins can turn off this feature (value 1) using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GeminiSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GeminiSettings</u></a> policy or by using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> (value 2). For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16291696" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Gemini in Chrome</u></a> in the Help Center.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137:</strong> Feature becomes available for some Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the US and on pre-Stable (Dev, Canary, Beta) channels in the US.</li>
      <li>A broader rollout will come in future milestones. You can check the upcoming publications of the Enterprise Release Notes for availability updates.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB137" name="chromeBrsrB137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Blob URL Partitioning: Fetching/Navigation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As a continuation of Storage Partitioning, Chrome 137 now implements partitioning of Blob URL access by Storage Key (top-level site, frame origin, and the has-cross-site-ancestor boolean), with the exception of top-level navigations which will remain partitioned only by frame origin. This behavior is similar to what’s currently implemented by both Firefox and Safari, and aligns Blob URL usage with the partitioning scheme used by other storage APIs as part of Storage Partitioning. In addition, Chrome 137 now enforces noopener on renderer-initiated top-level navigations to Blob URLs where the corresponding site is cross-site to the top-level site performing the navigation. This aligns Chrome with similar behavior in Safari, and the relevant specs have been updated to reflect these changes.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This change can be temporarily reverted by setting the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PartitionedBlobUrlUsage" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PartitionedBlobURLUsage</u></a> policy. The policy will be deprecated when the other storage partitioning related enterprise policies are deprecated.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137</strong> on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC137" name="chromeBrsrC137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Client’s LLM assistance in mitigating scams&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Users on the web are facing significant amounts of different kinds of scams a day. To combat these scams, Chrome now leverages on-device LLM to identify scam websites for Enhanced Safe Browsing users. Chrome sends the page content to an on-device LLM to infer security-related signals of the page and send these signals to Safe Browsing server side for a final verdict. When enabled, Chrome might consume more bandwidth to download the LLM.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Enhanced Safe Browsing is an existing feature, controlled by the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 134 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Gather the brand name and intent summary of the page that triggers keyboard lock to identify scam websites.</li>
      <li>Chrome 135 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Show the warnings to the user based on the server verdict which uses the brand and intent summary of the page that triggered keyboard lock.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Linux, macOS, Windows:</strong> Gather brand and intent summary of the page based on server reputation scoring system.</li>
      <li>Chrome 138 on Linux, macOS, Windows: Show the warnings to the user based on the server verdict which uses the brand and intent of the pages that the server reputation system scored.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD137" name="chromeBrsrD137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>DTLS 1.3&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 137 adds support for <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9147/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Datagram Transport Layer Security (<u>DTLS) 1.3</u></a> for Web Realtime Communication (<a href="https://webrtc.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebRTC</u></a>) connections. Previously, DTLS 1.2 was used for all WebRTC connections. This is required to add quantum-resistant cryptography to WebRTC.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE137" name="chromeBrsrE137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove --load-extension command line switch in Google Chrome&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To enhance the security and stability of the Chrome browser for our users, official Chrome-branded builds now deprecate the ability to load extensions via the <code>--load-extension</code> command-line flag, starting in Chrome 137. This change aims to mitigate the risks associated with harmful and unwanted extensions.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Unpacked extensions can be loaded via the <strong>Load Unpacked</strong> button on the extension management page (<code>chrome://extensions/</code>) with developer mode enabled. Developers can still use the <code>--load-extension</code> switch in non-branded builds such as Chromium and <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome For Testing</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrF137" name="chromeBrsrF137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove SwiftShader fallback&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Allowing automatic fallback to <a href="https://get.webgl.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebGL</u></a> backed by <a href="https://github.com/google/swiftshader" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SwiftShader</u></a> is deprecated and WebGL context creation now fails instead of falling back to SwiftShader.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This was done for two primary reasons:&nbsp;</p>

    <ol>
      <li>SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process.</li>
      <li>Users have a poor experience when falling back from a high-performance GPU-backed WebGL to a CPU-backed implementation. Users have no control over this behavior and it is difficult to describe in bug reports.</li>
    </ol>

    <p>SwiftShader is a useful tool for web developers to test their sites on systems that are headless or do not have a supported GPU. This use case will still be supported by opting in but is not intended for running untrusted content. To opt in to lower security guarantees and allow SwiftShader for WebGL, run the chrome executable with the <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> command-line switch.</p>

    <p>During the deprecation period, a warning will appear in the JavaScript console when a WebGL context is created and backed with SwiftShader. Passing <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader </code>will remove this warning message.</p>

    <p>Chromium and other browsers do not guarantee WebGL availability. It is important to test and handle WebGL context creation failure and fall back to other web APIs such as Canvas2D or an appropriate message to the user. A temporary enterprise policy will be available in Chrome 138 to revert the change.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows:</strong> SwiftShader will be disabled and replaced with another software WebGL fallback, WARP. Tests depending on the exact pixel values generated by SwiftShader may start failing.</li>
      <li>Chrome 138 on Linux, macOS:<strong> </strong>Swiftshader will be disabled on macOS and Linux as early as Chrome 138. Users on machines without a GPU will not be able to use WebGL.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrG137" name="chromeBrsrG137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Customizing managed profiles with custom logo and label&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 137 has a new toolbar and profile menu customizations that help users easily identify if their Chrome profile is managed, whether they're on a work or personal device. This is especially useful for BYOD scenarios where employees use their own devices with managed accounts.</p>

    <p>To help tailor this experience, we're adding three new policies:</p>

    <p>- <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseCustomLabel" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseCustomLabel</u></a>: Customize the text displayed on the toolbar element to match your organization's branding.</p>

    <p>- <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseLogoUrl" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseLogoUrl</u></a>: Add your company logo to the profile menu.</p>

    <p>- <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings</u></a>: This policy can disable the default label for a managed profile in the Chrome toolbar.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>In Chrome 134, these policies became available to customize the logo and label shown on a managed profile. Starting Chrome 137, there are updates to the default behavior of the profile label and icon overlaid on the account avatar. In Chrome 138, managed profiles will show a <em>work</em> or <em>school</em> label in addition to the profile disk. In the profile menu, there will be a building icon overlaid on the account avatar. The expanded profile disk can be disabled via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 134 on LaCrOS, macOS, Windows: Policies to customize the toolbar label and icon (in profile menu).&nbsp;</li>
      <li>Chrome 136&nbsp;on Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout of <em>Managed by your organization</em> in profile menu . The logo can be customized via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseLogoUrl" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseLogoUrl</u></a> policy.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137&nbsp;on Linux, macOS, Windows:</strong> Rollout of default <em>work</em> and <em>school</em> labels in Chrome toolbar. The label can be turned off via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings</u></a>.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/GzJY-yWIre175Lgx0g57IQxbPgSSYvgsEiah-LW4SF84E3FUKGOPdcF-NczvrUAVczo=w512" width="512" height="291" alt="&quot; &quot;" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/GzJY-yWIre175Lgx0g57IQxbPgSSYvgsEiah-LW4SF84E3FUKGOPdcF-NczvrUAVczo"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrH137" name="chromeBrsrH137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Align error type thrown for </strong><strong><em>payment</em></strong><strong> WebAuthn credential creation: SecurityError =&gt; NotAllowedError&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This change corrects the error type thrown during WebAuthn credential creation for <em>payment</em> credentials. Due to a historic specification mismatch, creating a <em>payment</em> credential in a cross-origin iframe without a user activation would throw a <code>SecurityError</code> instead of a <code>NotAllowedError</code>, which is what is thrown for non-payment credentials.</p>

    <p>Code that previously detected the type of error thrown, for example,&nbsp; `<code>e instanceof SecurityError</code>`, would be affected. Code that just generally handles errors during credential creation, for example,&nbsp; `<code>catch (e)</code>`, will continue to function correctly.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrI137" name="chromeBrsrI137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>HSTS tracking prevention&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>HTTP Strict Transport Security (<a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6797" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HSTS</u></a>) tracking prevention mitigates user tracking by third-parties via the HSTS cache. This feature only allows HSTS upgrades for top-level navigations and blocks HSTS upgrades for sub-resource requests. Doing so makes it infeasible for third-party sites to use the HSTS cache in order to track users across the web.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrJ137" name="chromeBrsrJ137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>2SV enforcement for admins&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To better protect your organization’s information, Google will soon require all accounts with access to admin.google.com to have 2-Step Verification (2SV) enabled. As a Google Workspace administrator, you need to confirm your identity with 2SV, which requires your password plus something additional, such as your phone or a security key.</p>

    <p>The enforcement will be rolled out gradually over the coming months. You should enable 2SV for the admin accounts in your organization before Google enforces it. For more information, see this <a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/16271818" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Help Center article</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrK137" name="chromeBrsrK137"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 137, some users can turn on <strong>Autofill with AI</strong>, a new feature that helps users fill out online forms more easily. On relevant forms, Chrome can use AI to better understand the form and offer users to automatically fill in previously saved info. Admins can control the feature using the existing <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a> policy and a new <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AutofillPredictionSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AutofillPredictionSettings</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Linux, macOS, Windows, ChromeOS</strong></li>
