<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrG136" name="upChromeBrsrG136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Happy Eyeballs V3</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This launch is an internal optimization in Chrome that implements <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ma_jfmHoOeOj6IyLFZyn0QF82sY5zjJb7ny3CwPkZOM/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.7nki9mck5t64" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Happy Eyeballs V3</u></a> to achieve better network connection concurrency. Happy Eyeballs V3 performs DNS resolutions asynchronously and staggers connection attempts with preferable protocols (H3/H2/H1) and address families (IPv6/IPv4) to reduce user-visible network connection delay. This feature is gated by a temporary policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HappyEyeballsV3Enabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HappyEyeballsV3Enabled</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH136" name="upChromeBrsrH136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Strict Same Origin policy for Storage Access API</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature updates the Storage Access API semantics to strictly follow the Same Origin policy, to enhance security. This means using <code>document.requestStorageAccess()</code> in a frame only attaches cookies to requests to the iframe's origin (not site) by default. Note: the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a> policy or Storage Access Headers might still be used to unblock cross-site cookies.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrI136" name="upChromeBrsrI136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Web App Manifest: </strong><strong><em>update_token</em></strong><strong> and update eligibility</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Introduces an <code>update_token</code> field and updates the eligibility algorithm to the manifest spec. This makes the update process more deterministic and predictable, giving the dev more control over whether (and when) updates should apply to existing installations, and allowing removal of the update check throttle that user agents currently need to implement to avoid wasting network resources.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
      <li>Chrome 139 on Android</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ136" name="upChromeBrsrJ136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Migrate extensions to Manifest V3 before June 2025</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Extensions must be updated to leverage Manifest V3. Chrome extensions are transitioning to a new manifest version, Manifest V3. This will bring improved privacy for your users—for example, by moving to a model where extensions modify requests declaratively, without the ability to see individual requests. This also improves extension security, as remotely hosted code will be disallowed on Manifest V3.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Beginning June 2024, Chrome will gradually disable Manifest V2 extensions running in the browser. An enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensionManifestV2Availability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensionManifestV2Availability</u></a>, can be used to test Manifest V3 in your organization ahead of the migration. Additionally, machines on which the policy is enabled will not be subject to the disabling of Manifest V2 extensions until the following year - June 2025 - at which point the policy will be removed.</p>

    <p>You can see which Manifest version is being used by all Chrome extensions running on your fleet using the <strong>Apps &amp; extensions usage</strong> page in Chrome Enterprise Core.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 127 on ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows: Chrome will gradually disable Manifest V2 extensions on user devices. Only those with the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensionManifestV2Availability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensionManifestV2Availability</u></a> enterprise policy enabled would be able to continue using Manifest V2 extensions in their organization.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensionManifestV2Availability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensionManifestV2Availability</u></a> policy.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK136" name="upChromeBrsrK136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome will remove support for macOS 11</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 138 will be the last release to support macOS 11; Chrome 139+ will no longer support macOS 11, which is outside of its support window with Apple. Running on a supported operating system is essential to maintaining security.</p>

    <p>On Macs running macOS 11, Chrome will continue to work, showing a warning infobar, but will not update any further. If a user wishes to have their Chrome be updated, they need to update their computer to a support version of macOS.</p>

    <p>For new installations of Chrome 139+, macOS 12+ will be required.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL136" name="upChromeBrsrL136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Isolated Web Apps</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Isolated Web Apps (IWAs) are an extension of existing work on PWA installation and Web Packaging that provide stronger protections against server compromise and other tampering that is necessary for developers of security-sensitive applications.</p>

    <p>Rather than being hosted on live web servers and fetched over HTTPS, these applications are packaged into Web Bundles, signed by their developer, and distributed to end-users through one or more of the potential methods described in the <a href="https://github.com/WICG/isolated-web-apps/blob/main/README.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Isolated Web Apps explainer</u></a> on GitHub.</p>

    <p>In this initial release, IWAs will only be installable through an admin policy on enterprise-managed ChromeOS devices.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows: </strong>This rollout adds support for Isolated Web Apps in enterprise-managed browser configurations on Windows.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrM136" name="upChromeBrsrM136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL hosts</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>According to the <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL Standard specification</u></a>, URL hosts cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host. This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a> and <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL focus</u></a> areas. To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows file:// URLs (<a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>).</p>

    <p>Thus this status entry tracks the work to bring Chromium closer to spec compliance by forbidding spaces for non-file URLs only.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 141 on Android, ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrN136" name="upChromeBrsrN136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 → v5 migration</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a>&nbsp;will be migrated to call into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/reference" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>v5 API</u></a> instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5. If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4*</code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead: <code>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</code>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users. For more details, see <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/reference/Migration.From.V4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Migration From V4 - Safe Browsing</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 145 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrO136" name="upChromeBrsrO136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome will start directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Administrators can use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy starting in Chrome 125 to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 146, and will be removed in Chrome 147. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows: The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that administrators can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise administrators may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt out through Chrome 146.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise will enhance security monitoring and incident response capabilities by collecting and reporting local and remote IP addresses and sending those IP addresses to the <a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/7575955" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Security Investigation Tool</u></a> (SIT) logs. In addition, Chrome Enterprise will allow admins to optionally send the IP addresses to first-party and third-party security information and event management (SIEM) providers via the Chrome Enterprise reporting connector. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11375053" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Manage Chrome Enterprise reporting connectors</u></a>. This will be available for Chrome Enterprise Core and Chrome Enterprise Premium customers.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeECB136" name="upChromeECB136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Inactive profile deletion in Chrome Enterprise Core</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In April 2025, the inactive period for profile deletion policy starts rolling out. In June 2025 (Chrome 138), the policy will begin to automatically delete managed profiles in the Admin console that have been inactive for more than the defined inactivity period. When releasing the policy, the inactivity period of time has a default value of 90 days. Meaning that by default, all managed profiles that have been inactive for more than 90 days are deleted from your account. Administrators can change the inactive period value using this policy. The maximum value to determine the profile inactivity period is 730 days and the minimum value is 28 days.</p>

    <p>If you lower the set policy value, it might have a global impact on any currently managed profiles. All impacted profiles will be considered inactive and, therefore, be deleted. This does not delete the user account. If an inactive profile is reactivated on a device, that profile will reappear in the console.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Policy will roll out in April. Deletion will start in June and the initial wave of deletion will complete by the end of July. After the initial deletion rollout, inactive profiles will continue to be deleted once they have reached their inactivity period.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

    <p>Chrome on iOS is introducing support for multiple accounts, particularly for managed (work/school) accounts. This update introduces separate browser profiles for each managed account, ensuring strict data separation between work and personal browsing. Regular accounts will continue to share a single profile. This change aims to improve Chrome's enterprise offering and provide a more secure and organized browsing experience, especially for end users with both personal and work accounts on their device. Users will experience a one-time onboarding flow when adding a managed account to the device. They will be able to switch between accounts by tapping on the account particle disk on the <strong>New tab</strong> page.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Admins can continue to use the following existing policies to manage iOS accounts:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome on iOS: Allows admins to apply policies to signed in users on iOS. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6304822?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Turn on Chrome browser management (Android and iOS)</u></a>.</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ProfileSeparationDataMigrationSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ProfileSeparationDataMigrationSettings</u></a>: This policy affects the onboarding experience and how prior browsing data is handled when a user adds a work profile.&nbsp;</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a>: It allows you to specify if the user can sign in to Google Chrome.&nbsp;</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#RestrictAccountsToPatterns" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>RestrictAccountsToPatterns</u></a>: Controls which accounts are visible on the device.</li>
    </ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome Enterprise Premium changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeEPA136" name="upChromeEPA136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>URL filtering capabilities on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The current WebProtect URL filtering capabilities on Desktop are being extended to mobile so that organizations can audit, warn, or block certain URLs or categories of URLs from loading on managed Chrome browsers or managed user profiles on mobile devices. This feature is part of Chrome Enterprise Premium and aims to provide secure and safe internet access for enterprise users on any device. Admins will be able to create URL filtering rules to ensure that employees can only access safe and authorized URLs on iOS devices.&nbsp;Chrome will report URL filtering events and unsafe site events via the Reporting Connector on mobile.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on iOS: </strong>In this milestone, the URL Filtering feature will be launched on iOS for Chrome Enterprise Premium customers. This will enable administrators to manage which URLs can be accessed on managed Chrome browsers or profiles on company-owned or BYOD iOS devices.

        <p>Key changes include:</p>

        <p>- Admins can block, warn, or audit users when accessing certain sites or categories.</p>

        <p>- End users will see interstitial pages when attempting to visit blocked or warned URLs.</p>

        <p>- Chrome will report URL filtering events.</p>

        <p>- Updates to the <code>chrome://management</code> page will reflect the new functionality.</p>
      </li>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>ChromeOS updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeOSA136" name="chromeOSA136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Quick Share enhancements&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 136, Quick Share extends <strong>Visible to everyone</strong> mode duration to a maximum of 10 minutes from 5. This feature allows your device to share files with and receive files from Android devices and other Chromebooks. Users can set device visibility, enter <strong>Visible to everyone</strong> mode, toggle Quick Share, and go to the Quick Share settings page, all from quick settings. This setting can be managed with the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#NearbyShareAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>NearbyShareAllowed</u></a> policy.</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/7pYMrgOLNDNrKBFmf47ZvJKOLT2vMjY1p6iNW3ZMkPTObjJlR24Qg-llyCimOpP6Cw=w512" width="512" height="288" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/7pYMrgOLNDNrKBFmf47ZvJKOLT2vMjY1p6iNW3ZMkPTObjJlR24Qg-llyCimOpP6Cw"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB136" name="chromeOSB136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Admin initiated Chrome Remote Desktop (CRD) sessions&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Starting in ChromeOS&nbsp;136, auto-approved Chrome Remote Desktop (CRD) connections allow IT teams to better support their ChromeOS users.</p>

    <p>In previous releases, users had to manually accept remote CRD connections via a notification to allow for remote connections. The new feature automatically accepts remote connections after 30 seconds (if the user does not decline) while ensuring user privacy through a combination of measures, for example, requirement of connection to managed network and end user activity in the last 5 minutes. Auto-accepted CRD connections are expected to significantly streamline support workflows by removing the need for additional end user intervention.</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/8xRbhmwOvZ93CcTpJgz2q0zPZs82sLVtdk4Pzp2m2a5BvpGq2enIjGS8vJbRGkGOVg=w512" width="512" height="341" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/8xRbhmwOvZ93CcTpJgz2q0zPZs82sLVtdk4Pzp2m2a5BvpGq2enIjGS8vJbRGkGOVg"></li>
</ul>
</div>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB136" name="upChromeOSB136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Event-based device log collection for troubleshooting (Admin console)&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>To help troubleshoot device issues (like crashes or failed OS updates), ChromeOS automatically collects and uploads device logs. This happens when these specific settings are turned on:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Enable device system log upload: turns on the overall log collection</li>
      <li>Report device OS information -&gt; OS update status: collects data about OS updates</li>
      <li>Report device telemetry -&gt; Crash information: gathers fatal crash information</li>
    </ul>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 137, when a problem occurs, IT admins will see a notification with a direct link to the uploaded logs on the ChromeOS device's details page in the Admin console. You can also see a history of device events. Log uploads happen a maximum of two times a day, and each file is typically 400KB to 1MB in size.</p>

    <p>For details, see these articles in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13739279?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Remote log collection for ChromeOS devices</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1698333?hl=en#zippy=%2Cview-device-details" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>View ChromeOS Device List and Details&nbsp;</u></a></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSC136" name="upChromeOSC136"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Face control policy on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>With ChromeOS 137, we will introduce a new policy to allow admins to have more control over access to face control on an organisational level.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/15824371" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Use facial gestures &amp; head movements to control your Chromebook with face control</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes</h2>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA135" name="chromeBrsrA135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>3P profile enrollment migrates to OIDC auth code flow&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 135 migrates the landing page for profile registration from the marketing website to a dynamic website. This update also migrates the OpenID Connect (<a href="https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OIDC</u></a>) implicit flow to an auth code flow. This aims to improve both the security and the user experience for third party (3P) managed profiles.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB135" name="chromeBrsrB135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Auto-deletion of downloads for Chrome on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Users of Chrome browser on iOS can now choose to automatically delete their browser downloads on a scheduled basis.</p>

    <p>This feature is likely to both improve device performance related to storage capacity, and to improve privacy by automating the deletion of files that users might otherwise forget to on their own.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on iOS</strong><br>
        Initial experiment at 1% in 135 for Chrome for iOS only. No planned rollout for other platforms.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/ouRTd0_iI4NOBALGAC6JqECEl_Jj3sUWDirRZhzkKK3ANI_NiThq86sJDhFU8nOUvBI=w439" width="439" height="771" alt="&quot; &quot;" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/ouRTd0_iI4NOBALGAC6JqECEl_Jj3sUWDirRZhzkKK3ANI_NiThq86sJDhFU8nOUvBI"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC135" name="chromeBrsrC135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Better password form detection with ML&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 135 introduces a new client-side Machine Learning (ML) model to better parse password forms on the web to increase detection and filling accuracy. You can control this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PasswordManagerEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PasswordManagerEnabled</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD135" name="chromeBrsrD135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Client’s LLM assistance in mitigating scams&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Users on the web are facing significant amounts and varieties of scams on a daily basis. To combat these scams, Chrome 135 uses on-device Large Language Models (LLMs) to identify scam websites for <strong>Enhanced protection</strong> users. Chrome sends the page content to an on-device LLM to infer security-related signals for that page. Chrome then sends these signals to Safe Browsing server side for a final verdict. When turned on, Chrome might consume more bandwidth to download the LLM.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 134 on Linux, macOS, Windows<br>
        Gather the brand name and intent summary of the page that requested keyboard lock API to identify scam websites.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        Show the warnings to the user based on the server verdict which uses the brand and intent summary of the page that requested keyboard lock API.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE135" name="chromeBrsrE135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate mutation events&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Synchronous mutation events, including <code>DOMSubtreeModified</code>, <code>DOMNodeInserted</code>, <code>DOMNodeRemoved</code>, <code>DOMNodeRemovedFromDocument</code>, <code>DOMNodeInsertedIntoDocument</code>, and <code>DOMCharacterDataModified</code>, negatively affect page performance, and also significantly increase the complexity of adding new features to the Web. These APIs were deprecated from the spec in 2011, and were replaced (in 2012) by the much better-behaved Mutation Observer API. Usage of the obsolete mutation events must be removed or migrated to Mutation Observer.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Since Chrome 124, a temporary enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a>, is available to re-enable deprecated or removed mutation events. To read more, see this <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/mutation-events-deprecation" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome for Developers</u></a> blog post. If you encounter any issues, you can file a <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium bug</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Mutation event support is disabled by default, since Chrome 127, or around July 30, 2024. Code should have been migrated before that date to avoid site breakage. If more time is needed, there are a few options:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/origintrials/#/view_trial/919297273937002497" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Mutation Events Deprecation Trial</u></a> can be used to re-enable the feature for a limited time on a given site. This can be used up until Chrome 135, ending March 25, 2025.</li>
      <li>A <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy can also be used for the same purpose, also through Chrome 135.</li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy will be deprecated.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrF135" name="chromeBrsrF135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Download file type extension-based warnings - documentation correction&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>We’ve updated the policy documentation for <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExemptDomainFileTypePairsFromFileTypeDownloadWarnings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExemptDomainFileTypePairsFromFileTypeDownloadWarnings</u></a> to correctly reflect its interaction with the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DownloadRestrictions" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DownloadRestrictions </u></a>policy. The behavior in Chrome has not changed.</p>

    <p>The behavior is: <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExemptDomainFileTypePairsFromFileTypeDownloadWarnings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExemptDomainFileTypePairsFromFileTypeDownloadWarnings</u></a> can specify exemptions that override <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DownloadRestrictions" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DownloadRestrictions</u></a> settings for blocking dangerous file types. Other types of security measures specified by <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DownloadRestrictions" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DownloadRestrictions</u></a>, such as blocking malicious downloads, cannot be overridden by <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExemptDomainFileTypePairsFromFileTypeDownloadWarnings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExemptDomainFileTypePairsFromFileTypeDownloadWarnings</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>

        <p>No Chrome changes - documentation change only.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrG135" name="chromeBrsrG135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Extensions improvements on Chrome Desktop&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>On Chrome 135 on Desktop, some users who sign in to Chrome when installing a new extension can now use and save extensions in their Google Account.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Relevant enterprise policies controlling extensions, as well as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncDisabled</u></a> or <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a>, continue to work as before, so admins can configure whether users can use and save items in their Google Account.</p>

    <p>For more information about how to use extensions on any computer, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome_webstore/answer/2664769" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Install and manage extensions</u></a> in the Chrome Web Store Help Center.</p>

    <p>Note: This change is a follow-up to the launch of the new identity model on Chrome Desktop. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/185277" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Sign in and sync in Chrome</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrH135" name="chromeBrsrH135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Generic Device Trust Connector&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Integrations created through the Device Trust Connector allow customers to implement granular controls for authentication into enterprise resources, for example, SaaS apps or your corporation intranet,&nbsp;based on the properties of the end user’s device and browser instance sent by Chrome. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13570263" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Manage Chrome Enterprise device trust connectors</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrI135" name="chromeBrsrI135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove Private Network Access enterprise policies&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Private Network Access (PNA 1.0) is an unshipped security feature designed to limit website access to local networks. Due to deployability concerns, PNA 1.0 was never able to ship by default, as it was incompatible with too many existing devices.</p>

    <p>PNA 1.0 required changes to devices on local networks. Instead, Chrome is implementing an updated proposal, Private Network Access 2.0 (PNA 2.0). PNA 2.0 only requires changes to sites that need to access the local network, rather than requiring changes to devices on the local network. Sites are much easier to update than devices, and so this approach should be much more straightforward to roll out.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>The only way to enforce PNA 1.0 is via enterprise policy. To avoid regressing security for enterprise customers opting-in to PNA 1.0 prior to shipping PNA 2.0, we will maintain the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled</u></a> policy, which causes Chrome to send special preflight messages, until such time that it becomes incompatible with PNA 2.0.</p>

    <p>Chrome 135 removes the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed</u></a> policies, which loosen PNA 1.0 restrictions. These policies currently have no effect, since PNA 1.0 is not shipped, and they will have no meaning once PNA 1.0 is removed.</p>

    <p>PNA 2.0 is described in this <a href="https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/local-network-access" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>explainer on GitHub</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong>

        <p>Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed</u></a> policies.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 137 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia
        <p>Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled</u></a>.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrK135" name="chromeBrsrK135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Settings, site shortcuts, and themes improvements on Chrome Desktop&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>On Chrome 135 on Desktop, for users who newly sign in to Chrome or who have Sync enabled, settings, site shortcuts and themes synced to their Google Account will now be kept separate from the local ones, that is,&nbsp; settings from when they’re signed out or when Sync is turned off.</p>

    <p>This allows for strictly less data sharing than previously: local settings don’t get automatically uploaded when signing in or turning on Sync, and no settings from the account are left behind on the device when Sync is turned off.</p>

    <p>Existing enterprise policies <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncDisabled</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled </u></a>will continue to apply so admins can restrict or disable the Sync feature if they want to. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6309115" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Manage who can sync browser settings</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Note: This change is a follow-up to the launch of the new identity model on Chrome Desktop.&nbsp;</p>

  <li><strong>Third-party cookies always blocked in Incognito mode&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 135, users have third-party cookies blocked in Incognito mode with no way to globally re-enable them. Site-level controls for allowing third-party cookies will not be changed.&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrN135" name="chromeBrsrN135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Create service worker client and inherit service worker controller for srcdoc iframe&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Srcdoc context documents were previously not service worker clients and were not covered by their parent page’s service worker. This resulted in some discrepancies (for example, Resource Timing reports the URLs that these documents load, but the service worker doesn’t intercept them).&nbsp;</p>

    <p>To fix these discrepancies, Chrome 135 creates service worker clients for srcdoc iframes and makes them inherit the parent page's service worker controller.</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrO135" name="chromeBrsrO135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>HSTS tracking prevention&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p><a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6797" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)</u></a> allows sites to declare themselves accessible through secure connections only.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>In Chrome 135, HSTS tracking prevention mitigates user tracking by third-parties using the HSTS cache. It only allows HSTS upgrades for top-level navigations and blocks HSTS upgrades for sub-resource requests. This prevents third-party sites using the HSTS cache to track users across the web. For more information, see this HSTS Tracking Prevention explainer on <a href="https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/HSTS-Tracking-Prevention" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrP135" name="chromeBrsrP135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove deprecated navigator.xr.supportsSession method&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 135 removes the <code>navigator.xr.supportsSession</code> method, which was replaced in the <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebXR spec</u></a> by the <code>navigator.xr.isSessionSupported</code> method in September of 2019 after receiving feedback on the API shape from the TAG. It has been marked as deprecated in Chromium since then, producing a console warning redirecting developers to the updated API.</p>

    <p>Usage of the call is very low, as shown by <a href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/2416" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Status usage metrics</u></a>. Additionally, all major frameworks that are used to build WebXR content have been confirmed to have been updated to use the newer call.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrPP135" name="chromeBrsrPP135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove --load-extension command line switch in Google Chrome&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 137, to enhance the security and stability of the Chrome browser for our users, official Chrome branded builds will be deprecating the ability to load extensions via the <code>--load-extension</code> command-line flag. This change aims to mitigate the risks associated with harmful and unwanted extensions.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>With developer mode enabled, you can load unpacked extensions using the <strong>Load Unpacked</strong> button on the extension management page (<code>chrome://extensions/</code>). Developers can still use the --<a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>load-extension switch</u></a> in non-branded builds such as Chromium and Chrome For Testing.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS</strong></li>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome browser changes</h4>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrA135" name="upChromeBrsrA135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remote debugging port custom data directory requirement</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Remote debugging via a TCP port or a pipe will no longer be possible in Google Chrome with the default data directory on Windows, Linux and macOS.</p>

    <p>A custom data directory must be specified to remotely debug Google Chrome using the <code>--user-data-dir </code>switch, when using the <code>--remote-debugging-pipe</code> or <code>--remote-debugging-port</code> switches.</p>

    <p>The motivation for this change is because these remote debugging switches are being abused by infostealers and malware to extract data from Google Chrome. A custom user data directory uses a different encryption key and so it becomes no longer possible for malware to steal encrypted data such as cookies.</p>

    <p>This change does not affect Chrome for Testing and Chromium.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 136 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrB135" name="upChromeBrsrB135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Blob URL Partitioning: Fetching/Navigation</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As a continuation of Storage Partitioning, Chromium will implement partitioning of <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Blob URL</u></a> access by Storage Key (top-level site, frame origin, and the has-cross-site-ancestor boolean), with the exception of top-level navigations which will remain partitioned only by frame origin. This behavior is similar to what’s currently implemented by both Firefox and Safari, and aligns Blob URL usage with the partitioning scheme used by other storage APIs as part of Storage Partitioning. In addition, Chromium will enforce noopener on renderer-initiated top-level navigations to Blob URLs where the corresponding site is cross-site to the top-level site performing the navigation. This aligns Chromium with similar behavior in Safari, and the relevant specs have been updated to reflect these changes.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This change can be temporarily reverted by setting the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PartitionedBlobUrlUsage" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PartitionedBlobURLUsage</u></a><strong> </strong>policy. The policy will be deprecated when the other storage partitioning related enterprise policies are deprecated.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 136 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrC135" name="upChromeBrsrC135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate getters of Intl Locale Info API</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Intl Locale Info API is a Stage 3 ECMAScript <a href="https://github.com/tc39/proposal-intl-locale-info" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TC39 proposal</u></a> to enhance the Intl.Locale object by exposing locale information, such as week data (first day in a week, weekend start day, weekend end day, minimum day in the first week), and text direction hour cycle used in the locale.</p>

    <p>We shipped our implementation in <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5566859262820352" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome 99</u></a> but later on the proposal made some changes in Stage 3 and moved several getters to functions. We plan to remove the deprecated getters and relaunch the renamed functions.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 136 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrD135" name="upChromeBrsrD135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>FedCM updates</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As early as Chrome 136, Federated Credential Management API (<a href="https://developers.google.com/privacy-sandbox/cookies/fedcm" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>FedCM</u></a>) will be able to show multiple identity providers in the same dialog. This will provide developers with a convenient way to present all supported identity providers to users. We are planning to first tackle the simple case of having all providers in the same get() call.</p>

    <p>We plan to remove support for adding another account in FedCM passive mode. This feature allows showing a <strong>Use another account</strong> button alongside other IdP accounts in the chooser. The feature is currently unused, and UX conversations indicate that supporting this leads to a more complicated flow without much benefit. This feature will still work in FedCM active mode.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 136 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrE135" name="upChromeBrsrE135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Partitioning :visited links history</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To eliminate user browsing history leaks, anchor elements are styled as <code>:visited</code> only if they have been clicked from this top-level site and frame origin before. On the browser-side, this means that the VisitedLinks hashtable is now partitioned by triple-keying, or by storing the following for each visited link: &lt;link URL, top-level site, frame origin&gt;. By only styling links that have been clicked on this site and frame before, the many side-channel attacks that have been developed to obtain <code>:visited</code> links styling information are now obsolete, as they no longer provide sites with new information about users.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>There is an exception for <em>self-links</em>, where links to a site's own pages can be styled as <code>:visited</code> even if they have not been clicked on in this exact top-level site and frame origin before. This exemption is only enabled in top-level frames or subframes, which are same-origin with the top-level frame. The privacy benefits above are still achieved because sites already know which of its subpages a user has visited, so no new information is exposed. This was a community-requested exception that improves user experience as well.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 136 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrF135" name="upChromeBrsrF135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Strict Same Origin Policy for Storage Access API</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 136&nbsp;will adjust Storage Access API semantics to strictly follow the Same Origin policy, to enhance security. This means that using <code>document.requestStorageAccess()</code> in a frame will only attach cookies to requests to the iframe's origin (not site) by default.</p>

    <p>Note: the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a> policy or Storage Access headers can still be used to unblock cross-site cookies.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 136 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrG135" name="upChromeBrsrG135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove SwiftShader fallback</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As early as Chrome 137, we plan to deprecate automatic fallback to WebGL backed by SwiftShader. WebGL context creation will fail instead of falling back to SwiftShader. We plan to remove SwiftShader fallback&nbsp;for two primary reasons:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process.</li>
      <li>Users have a poor experience when falling back from a high-performance GPU-backed WebGL to a CPU-backed implementation. Users have no control over this behavior and it is difficult to describe in bug reports.</li>
    </ol>

    <p><a href="https://github.com/google/swiftshader" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SwiftShader</u></a> is a useful tool for web developers to test their sites on systems that are headless or do not have a supported GPU. This use case will still be supported by opting in but is not intended for running untrusted content.</p>

    <p>To opt in to lower security guarantees and allow SwiftShader for WebGL, run the chrome executable with the <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> command-line switch.</p>

    <p>During the deprecation period, a warning will appear in the JavaScript console when a WebGL context is created and backed with SwiftShader. Passing <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> will remove this warning message.</p>

    <p>Chromium and other browsers do not guarantee WebGL availability. You can test and handle WebGL context creation failure and fall back to other web APIs such as Canvas2D or an appropriate message to the user.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH135" name="upChromeBrsrH135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL host</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As stated in the <a href="http://whatwg.org" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WhatWG.org</u></a> spec, <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL hosts</u></a> cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host.</p>

    <p>This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 'HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a>' and URL <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>focus areas</u></a>.</p>

    <p>To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows <code>file://</code> URLs. To read more, see the discussion on <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>.</p>

    <p>This feature will be part of the ongoing work to bring Chromium closer to spec compliance by forbidding spaces in non-file URLs only.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrHH135" name="upChromeBrsrHH135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome will remove support for macOS 11</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

<p>Chrome 138 will be the last release to support macOS 11; Chrome 139+ will no longer support macOS 11, which is outside of its support window with Apple. Running on a supported operating system is essential to maintaining security.</p>

<p>On Macs running macOS 11, Chrome will continue to work, showing a warning infobar, but will not update any further. If a user wishes to have their Chrome be updated, they need to update their computer to a support version of macOS.</p>

<p>For new installations of Chrome 139+, macOS 12+ will be required.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome 139 on Windows, macOS</strong></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>


<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrI135" name="upChromeBrsrI135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Isolated Web Apps</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Isolated Web Apps (IWAs) are an extension of existing work on PWA installation and Web Packaging that provide stronger protections against server compromise and other tampering, which is necessary for developers of security-sensitive applications.</p>

    <p>Rather than being hosted on live web servers and fetched over HTTPS, these applications are packaged into Web Bundles, signed by their developer, and distributed to end-users through one or more of the potential methods described in <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/tutorials/getting-started-with-isolated-web-apps" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Getting started with Isolated Web Apps</u></a>.</p>

    <p>In the initial release, IWAs will only be installable through a policy on enterprise-managed ChromeOS devices.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows</strong>

        <p>This rollout adds support for Isolated Web Apps in enterprise-managed browser configurations on Windows.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ135" name="upChromeBrsrJ135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 to v5 migration</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the v5 API instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5.</p>

    <p>If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4*</code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead: <code>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</code>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 145 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows</strong>

        <p>This will be a gradual rollout.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK135" name="upChromeBrsrK135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome started directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Admins might use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, available from Chrome 125, to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 136, and will be removed in Chrome 137. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that admins can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise admins may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt-in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt-out through Chrome 136.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 147 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise is enhancing its security monitoring and incident response capabilities by collecting and reporting local and remote IP addresses and sending those IP addresses to the Security Investigation Logs (SIT). In addition, Chrome Enterprise will allow admins to optionally send the IP addresses to both in-house and third-party Security and Information Event Management (SIEM) providers via the Chrome Enterprise Reporting connector.</p>

    <p>This will be available for Chrome Enterprise Core customers.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeECE135" name="upChromeECE135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Inactive profile deletion in Chrome Enterprise Core</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In April 2025 (Chrome 136), the inactive period for profile deletion policy will start rolling out. In June 2025 (Chrome 138), the policy will begin to automatically delete managed profiles in the Admin console that have been inactive for more than the defined inactivity period. When releasing the policy, the inactivity period of time has a default value of 90 days. Meaning that by default, all managed profiles that have been inactive for more than 90 days are deleted from your account. Administrators can change the inactive period value using this policy. The maximum value to determine the profile inactivity period is 730 days and the minimum value is 28 days.</p>

    <p>If you lower the set policy value, it might have a global impact on any currently managed profiles. All impacted profiles will be considered inactive and, therefore, be deleted. This does not delete the user account. If an inactive profile is re-activated on a device, that profile will reappear in the console.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>

        <p>Policy will roll out in April (Chrome 136). Deletion will start in June (Chrome 138) and the initial wave of deletion will complete by the end of July (Chrome 139). After the initial deletion rollout, inactive profiles will continue to be deleted once they have reached their inactivity period.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>ChromeOS updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeOSA135" name="chromeOSA135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS policy for battery longevity&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 135 introduces a new battery charge limit policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DevicePowerBatteryChargingOptimization" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DevicePowerBatteryChargingOptimization</u></a> , which offers more optimization options. Battery charging optimization helps extend the lifespan of Chromebooks.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Administrators can set a maximum charge limit, with 100% as the default, to minimize battery degradation and improve long-term reliability.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>The new policy benefits both administrators managing fleets of devices, such as in educational settings, and individual users seeking to maximize their Chromebook's longevity. This policy does not require user interaction though administrators may wish to inform end users of the change to charging limits.</p>

    <p><img height="130" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXc7r6I46hwAOzvtjzm121Id7PRlH3WhWfMIRvmovIhRDDR3t9o4yqm1NfviQtqSWD1kKB_v4jpvbBYrNtjGPbpaPBcstpgA3MCVgGSSNGthy3zP6q2vm-rBxZ3-p0wNImD0yk18uG_3SOFSPCzmBGDVffdy1CB2KhJ6wphxn8gsWySq?key=QhRBJ0Uasz4gTHj_ACtMQnQO" width="364"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB135" name="chromeOSB135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Android Bluetooth stack, Fluoride, on ChromeOS Flex&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 122, we started rolling out Fluoride on ChromeOS devices and&nbsp; now it's being brought to ChromeOS Flex. The transition will happen seamlessly on login, preserving existing paired devices, and should work with Bluetooth devices today with no interruptions. For more details, see <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/androids-bluetooth-stack-fluoride-comes-to-chromeos" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Android’s Bluetooth stack, Fluoride, comes to ChromeOS</u></a>.</p>

    <p>If you experience issues, please file feedback and, if necessary, disable the new stack via <code>chrome://flags/#bluetooth-use-floss</code>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSC135" name="chromeOSC135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>External storage allowlist policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS policy to specify devices to be exempt from external storage restrictions. The new <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExternalStorageAllowlist" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExternalStorageAllowlist</u></a> policy lets administrators specify certain devices that will be exempt from previously-set external storage restrictions. By setting the policy, administrators can now restrict access to all external storage, but still allow trusted devices to have read/write access.</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/aySwEmb3o5l9vC6INSzM7W-LRUGsbgVxbCSMK6cvWuV_0qOvntv2AFPUMPA27vSbOSty=w895" width="947" height="679" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/aySwEmb3o5l9vC6INSzM7W-LRUGsbgVxbCSMK6cvWuV_0qOvntv2AFPUMPA27vSbOSty"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSD135" name="chromeOSD135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Image content search&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Instead of searching by file names, users can now search by the content of their images in Launcher.</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/YEso5PrbVRmfjqFQfoMirW4-zKxy6JAG44OKIlHKPXfuOglS-Lz_8o0t4WYxdaUyjkxW=w820" width="820" height="375" alt="&quot; &quot;" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/YEso5PrbVRmfjqFQfoMirW4-zKxy6JAG44OKIlHKPXfuOglS-Lz_8o0t4WYxdaUyjkxW">
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSE135" name="chromeOSE135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Fast Pair for mice on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Fast Pair is now available for mice on ChromeOS. You can now bring a Fast Pair-compatible mouse close to your ChromeOS device, and be prompted to pair it with one click. For details, see<a href="https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/2587653?hl=en"> </a><a href="https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/2587653" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Connect Chromebook to Bluetooth devices</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSF135" name="chromeOSF135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Mouse Keys on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Mouse Keys is an accessibility feature that allows customers to control their mouse pointer using the keyboard. This is helpful for people who have difficulty or pain using a traditional mouse.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSG135" name="chromeOSG135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Face control enhancements&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>We've made it clearer when <strong>Face control</strong> is active and simplified the process of turning it off. You'll now see a prominent <strong>Face control active</strong>&nbsp;message with a convenient close button directly in the UI. Additionally, you’ll see a notification to inform you when <strong>Face control</strong> is turned on.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>To reduce unintended session transitions, we have removed <strong>Face control</strong> accessibility settings on the login screen for managed devices.</p>

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/HKxWIoBtLaTePGcyQW25iHEx_6Hrh2nI93VJg1hQeT6NulHZAbdsPR5fVKEOWBdXt70=w895" width="919" height="362" alt="&quot; &quot;" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/HKxWIoBtLaTePGcyQW25iHEx_6Hrh2nI93VJg1hQeT6NulHZAbdsPR5fVKEOWBdXt70"></p>

    <p>&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA135" name="upChromeOSA135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Upcoming deprecation of user-installed Chrome apps&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 139 (currently planned for stable release on August 19th), user-installed Chrome apps will stop working. Starting in ChromeOS M135, a notification displays to remind users of the upcoming deprecation. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15950395" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>End of support for Chrome apps</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB135" name="upChromeOSB135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS freeform wallpapers&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 136, freeform wallpapers will offer an unrestricted input field that empowers users to express their individuality, creativity, and passions by turning their background into a personal canvas. Users will be able to generate wallpapers by inputting different prompts in the text field, or use the <strong>Inspire me</strong> feature, which will generate random prompts and wallpapers until you find one you like. This feature will be available on Chromebook Plus devices only. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15966259" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Wallpaper settings</u></a> .</p>

    <p>Admins can control this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAIWallpaperSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAIWallpaperSettings</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>For 18+ consumers, the default is <em>Allow with data collection</em>. Users under 13 cannot access the feature.</li>
      <li>For 18+ managed users, the default is <em>Allow without data collection</em>.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>Users under 18 cannot access the feature.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSC135" name="upChromeOSC135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Quick Share enhancements&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 136, Quick Share extends <strong>Visible to everyone</strong> mode duration to a maximum of 10 minutes from 5. This feature allows your device to share files with and receive files from Android devices and other Chromebooks. Users can set device visibility, enter <strong>Visible to everyone</strong> mode, toggle Quick Share, and go to the Quick Share settings page all from quick settings.</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/XPTXsrvRkc7SptdRZl0upz4oHcqBXADP05nwYfbSotV67pZC94kJksdhlso_tJAEq1Q=w895" width="1366" height="768" alt="" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/XPTXsrvRkc7SptdRZl0upz4oHcqBXADP05nwYfbSotV67pZC94kJksdhlso_tJAEq1Q"></li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSD135" name="upChromeOSD135"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Event-based device log collection for troubleshooting (Admin console)&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>To help troubleshoot device issues (like crashes or failed OS updates), ChromeOS automatically collects and uploads device logs. This happens when these specific settings are turned on:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Enable device system log upload: turns on the overall log collection</li>
      <li>Report device OS information -&gt; OS update status: collects data about OS updates</li>
      <li>Report device telemetry -&gt; Crash information: gathers fatal crash information</li>
    </ul>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 136, when a problem occurs, IT admins will see a notification with a direct link to the uploaded logs on the ChromeOS device's details page in the Admin console. You can also see a history of device events. Log uploads happen a maximum of two times a day, and each file is typically 400KB to 1MB in size.</p>

    <p>For details, see these articles in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13739279?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Remote log collection for ChromeOS devices</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1698333?hl=en#zippy=%2Cview-device-details" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>View ChromeOS Device List and Details&nbsp;</u></a></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>
