<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes</h2>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA134" name="chromeBrsrA134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Search your screen with Google Lens on Desktop and iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Admins can control all elements of this feature through a policy called <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a>. To perform the search, a screenshot of the screen is sent to Google servers but it is not linked to any IDs or accounts, it is not viewed by any human, and data about its contents is not logged. To contextualize the search to the document or website the user is viewing, the PDF bytes or website HTML is sent to Google servers but is not linked to any IDs or accounts, not viewable by any human, and the data or data generated about its contents is not logged.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>Desktop</u></p>

    <p>Since Chrome 126, users can search any images or text they see on their Desktop screen with Google Lens. To use this feature, go to a website and click the <strong>Google Lens</strong> chip on the on-focus omnibox or right-click an image and select <strong>Search with Google Lens</strong>. Users can select anywhere on the screen to search its contents, and refine their search by adding questions to the search box. Starting in Chrome 132, users can also ask questions about entire web pages or PDF documents and answers will reference their current document and the web. To use this feature, invoke <strong>Search with Google Lens</strong> as described above and enter queries into the search box on the top right corner of the Chrome window. A side panel will open on the right side of the browser window with search results.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>iOS</u></p>

    <p>Since Chrome 131, users can search any images or text they see on their iOS Chrome screen with Google Lens. To use this feature, go to a website and click on the <strong>3-dot menu &gt; Search with Google Lens</strong>. Starting in Chrome 134, users can also invoke this feature by clicking the <strong>Google Lens </strong>icon on the left side of the omnibox. Users can click, highlight, or drag anywhere on the screen to search its contents, and refine their search by adding keywords or questions to the search box.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>Rollout details:</u></p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 126 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout of the feature to 1% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 127 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout to 100% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 131 on iOS: Rollout of the feature to 1% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout of the expanded feature to 1% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 133 on iOS: Rollout to 100% Stable</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on iOS: Rollout of the expanded feature to 100% Stable</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB134" name="chromeBrsrB134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Security &amp; Privacy panel in Chrome DevTools&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 134, developers can use the new <strong>Security &amp; Privacy</strong> panel in Chrome DevTools to test how their site behaves when third-party cookies are limited. Developers can temporarily limit third-party cookies, observe how their site behaves, and review the status of third-party cookies on their site.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="451" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdhl9MsXJ3T_pLY-2AelrG0uXqkahqgsjiD7nHNb7AjaDhJMh4sLlulNhvzlDb44tn2xudwJV2VV7MS-ESMUMcttp-hama6Yuf1haNk8dUjZM302oTaPTniiTEOIdyMhH3YPdvx6w?key=5JVmW3enG4IRe0gEech3IQ_g" width="687"></p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>This feature does not make any permanent changes to existing enterprise policies, but it lets third-party cookie related enterprise policies (that is, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BlockThirdPartyCookies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BlockThirdPartyCookies</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a>) be temporarily overridden, to test enhanced restrictions. If your enterprise policy already blocks third-party cookies using <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BlockThirdPartyCookies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BlockThirdPartyCookies</u></a>, this feature will be disabled.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>The new <strong>Security &amp; Privacy</strong> panel replaces the existing <strong>Security</strong> panel. TLS connection and certificate information continue to be available on the <strong>Security</strong> menu on the left, within the <strong>Security &amp; Privacy</strong> panel.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC134" name="chromeBrsrC134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Better password form detection with ML&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 134 introduces a new client-side Machine Learning (ML) model to better parse password forms on the web to increase detection and filling accuracy. You can control this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PasswordManagerEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PasswordManagerEnabled</u></a> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD134" name="chromeBrsrD134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Client’s LLM assistance in mitigating scams&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Users on the webs are facing enormous amounts of several kinds of scams a day. To combat these scams, Chrome will leverage on-device Large Language Model (LLM) to identify scam websites for Enhanced Safe Browsing&nbsp;users. Chrome will send the page content to an on-device LLM to infer security-related signals of the page and send these signals to Safe Browsing server side for a final verdict. When enabled, Chrome may consume more bandwidth to download the LLM.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>An enterprise policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel</u></a> is available to control safe browsing and the mode it operates in.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>

        <p>Gather the brand name and intent summary of the page that requested keyboard lock API to identify scam websites.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE134" name="chromeBrsrE134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>LLM-powered on-device detection of abusive notifications on Android&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This launch aims to hide the contents of notifications that are suspected to be abusive. The user then has the options to dismiss, show the notification, or unsubscribe from the origin. This detection is to be done by an on-device model.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrF134" name="chromeBrsrF134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Customizing managed profiles with custom logo and label&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>New toolbar and profile menu customizations that help users easily identify if their Chrome profile is managed, whether they're on a work or personal device. This is especially useful for scenarios where employees use their own devices with managed accounts.</p>

    <p>To help tailor this experience, we're adding three new policies:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseCustomLabel" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseCustomLabel:</u></a> Customize the text displayed on the toolbar element to match your organization's branding.</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseLogoUrl" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseLogoUrl</u></a>: Add your company logo to the profile menu.</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings</u></a>: This policy can disable the default label for a managed profile in the Chrome toolbar.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>In Chrome 134, these policies will be available to customize the logo and label shown on a managed profile. The policies will take effect on user’s managed profiles.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>Starting Chrome 135, there will be updates to the default behavior of the profile label and icon overlaid on the account avatar. Managed profiles will show a <em>work</em> or <em>school</em> label in addition to the profile disk. In the profile menu, there will be a building icon overlaid on the account avatar. The expanded profile disk can be disabled via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings.</u></a></p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on macOS, Windows, Linux</strong>

        <p>Policies to customize the toolbar label and icon (in profile menu) are available in the Admin console. If policies have already been set, the user will see the customized logo and label.</p>
      </li>
      <li>Chrome 135: Starting rollout of defaults including:&nbsp;
        <ul>
          <li>1) <em>work</em> or <em>school</em> label shown in toolbar, next to user avatar&nbsp;</li>
          <li>2) A building icon overlayed on the user's account photo in the profile menu. The label can be turned off via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings</u></a>. Starting with 1% and gradual slow rollout thereafter.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="374" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdCApmajFJeed4Tap8qwyjXxsFFa5QvjjnPN5Z4sDKWMPOC4VZYdokgt8qPX6WbrCFCH-CjhR0rWg9ipX6EEppqwq91Vo9zeUntZbDSgI06jMmST5y1LE0zktUQcA1VS3292C9s11M?key=5JVmW3enG4IRe0gEech3IQ_g" width="660"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrG134" name="chromeBrsrG134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Device Bound Session Credentials google.com prototype&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The <a href="https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-dbsc/blob/main/README.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Device Bound Session Credentials</u></a> (DBSC) project is intended to move the web away from long-lived bearer credentials like cookies, which can be stolen and reused, to credentials which are either short-lived or cryptographically bound to a device.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>The feature aims at protecting users against credential theft which is typically performed by malware running on the user's device.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>The current launch is a proof-of-concept targeting the <strong>google.com</strong> website. In the future, we plan to standardize this approach for other websites and web browsers.</p>

    <p>Enterprise admins can control the feature state using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BoundSessionCredentialsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BoundSessionCredentialsEnabled</u></a> boolean policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 124 on Windows
        <p>Planned 1% rollout on Chrome stable for google.com cookie binding for the general population.</p>
      </li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows</strong>
        <p>Added binding support for OAuth2.0 refresh tokens that are used for Chrome sign-in.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrH134" name="chromeBrsrH134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Password change&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature gives users the option to change leaked credentials immediately. The feature can only be triggered from the <strong>Check your Password</strong> dialog. When users see a warning for an eligible website, they can change the password there and then.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="431" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfq9wFkb9VCrCQBZbIjR7MGFwm59ZJdGzfbt37czrbkffQu_xhlOdpKw98ntn6pfCEGH1aPneMINnYBnEjzkxT0yhXOdXHOJ9SBX3bCKNVOf5C8imhTLBmMmjB3fKdjLM-9aGQO-3M?key=5JVmW3enG4IRe0gEech3IQ_g" width="581"></p>

Reading mode now includes a <strong>Read aloud</strong> feature that allows users to hear the text they are reading spoken out loud. You can choose different natural voices and speeds, and see visual highlights as the text is spoken.&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrJ134" name="chromeBrsrJ134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Restrict unpacked extensions to developer mode&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 134, unpacked extensions loaded from the <code>chrome://extensions</code> page will only be enabled if the developer mode switch is turned on. This change is intended to improve security by mitigating the risks associated with harmful unpacked extensions and developer mode tampering exploitation. An enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensionDeveloperModeSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ExtensionDeveloperModeSettings</u></a>, is available to gate the existing developer mode switch.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        The feature will roll out to 100% of users on Chrome 134.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrK134" name="chromeBrsrK134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Show enterprise settings for AI features&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Previously, AI features were hidden from settings when they are disabled by enterprise policy. Now, we will keep showing the features and show a <em>Disabled by your organization</em> notice, similar to other settings when they are disabled by policy.</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrL134" name="chromeBrsrL134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Customizable &lt;select&gt; element&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Customizable <code>&lt;select&gt;</code> allows developers to take complete control of the rendering of <code>&lt;select&gt;</code> elements by adding the <code>appearance:base-select</code> CSS property.</p>

    <p>This feature relies on the <code>SelectParserRelaxation</code> flag, which changes the HTML parser to allow more tags within the <code>&lt;select&gt;</code> tag. Sites that include additional tags inside <code>&lt;select&gt;</code>, which were getting removed before, such as <code>&lt;span&gt;</code> tags, or sites that include an extremely large number of <code>&lt;option&gt;</code> tags in their <code>&lt;select&gt;</code>, might be affected by <code>SelectParserRelaxation</code>. This feature and <code>SelectParserRelaxation</code> can be controlled with the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SelectParserRelaxationEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SelectParserRelaxation</u></a> enterprise policy. Some issues that have come up in prior launches of <code>SelectParserRelaxation</code> include <code>&lt;select&gt;</code> elements taking a very long time to open or <code>&lt;option&gt;</code> tags not showing up anymore.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrM134" name="chromeBrsrM134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>HTML parser relaxation for &lt;select&gt;&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In Chrome 134, the HTML parser allows more tags in <code>&lt;select&gt;</code> in addition to <code>&lt;option&gt;</code>, <code>&lt;optgroup&gt;</code>, and <code>&lt;hr&gt;</code>.</p>

    <p>This supports the customizable <code>&lt;select&gt;</code> feature but is being shipped first because it can be done separately and has some compatibility risk.</p>

    <p>This feature is gated by the temporary policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SelectParserRelaxationEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SelectParserRelaxationEnabled</u></a>. This is a temporary transition period, and the policy will stop working by Chrome 141.</p>

    <p>For more details, see the <a href="https://open-ui.org/components/customizableselect/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Customizable Select Element (Explainer)</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrN134" name="chromeBrsrN134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove nonstandard getUserMedia audio constraints&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 134 removes a number of nonstandard goog-prefixed <a href="https://www.webrtc-developers.com/getusermedia-constraints-explained/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>constraints for </u><u>getUserMedia</u></a>, which existed before audio constraints were properly standardized.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>Usage has gone down significantly ~0.000001% to 0.0009% (depending on the constraint) and some of them do not even have an effect due to changes in the Chromium audio-capture stack. Soon none of them will have any effect due to other upcoming changes.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>We do not expect any major regressions due to this change. Applications using these constraints will continue to work, but will get audio with default settings (as if no constraints were passed). They can easily migrate to standard constraints.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrP134" name="chromeBrsrP134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New tab page cards for Microsoft Outlook and Sharepoint&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Enterprise users with Outlook or Sharepoint can now access their upcoming meetings or suggested files directly from the <strong>New tab</strong> page. This streamlined experience eliminates the need to switch tabs or waste time searching for your next meeting, allowing you to focus on what matters most. Admins who are interested in testing out this feature can <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/engage/trusted-testers/sign-up/?_ga=2.146701236.-163299450.1697557917&amp;_gl=1*96nbfd*_ga*MTYzMjk5NDUwLjE2OTc1NTc5MTc.*_ga_WH2QY8WWF5*MTY5NzU1NzkxNi4xLjEuMTY5NzU1ODIyMy4wLjAuMA.." rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Sign up to become a Trusted Tester</u></a>.</p>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome browser changes</h4>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrA134" name="upChromeBrsrA134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate mutation events</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Synchronous mutation events, including <code>DOMSubtreeModified</code>, <code>DOMNodeInserted</code>, <code>DOMNodeRemoved</code>, <code>DOMNodeRemovedFromDocument</code>, <code>DOMNodeInsertedIntoDocument</code>, and <code>DOMCharacterDataModified</code>, negatively affect page performance, and also significantly increase the complexity of adding new features to the Web. These APIs were deprecated from the spec in 2011, and were replaced (in 2012) by the much better-behaved Mutation Observer API. Usage of the obsolete mutation events must be removed or migrated to Mutation Observer.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Since Chrome 124, a temporary enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a>, is available to re-enable deprecated or removed mutation events. To read more, see this <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/mutation-events-deprecation" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome for Developers</u></a> blog post. If you encounter any issues, you can file a <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium bug</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Mutation event support is disabled by default, since Chrome 127, or around July 30, 2024. Code should have been migrated before that date to avoid site breakage. If more time is needed, there are a few options:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/origintrials/#/view_trial/919297273937002497" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Mutation Events Deprecation Trial</u></a> can be used to re-enable the feature for a limited time on a given site. This can be used up until Chrome 134, ending March 25, 2025.</li>
      <li>A <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy can also be used for the same purpose, also through Chrome 134.</li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy will be deprecated.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrB134" name="upChromeBrsrB134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Extension&nbsp;improvements on Chrome Desktop</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>On Chrome 135 on Desktop, some users who sign in to Chrome when installing a new extension can now use and save extensions in their Google Account.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Relevant enterprise policies controlling extensions, as well as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncDisabled</u></a> or <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a>, will continue to work as before, so admins can configure whether users can use and save items in their Google Account.</p>

    <p>For more information about how to use extensions on any computer, see&nbsp; <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome_webstore/answer/2664769" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Install and manage extensions</u></a> in the Chrome Web Store help center.</p>

    <p>Note: this change is a follow-up to the launch of the new identity model on Chrome Desktop.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrC134" name="upChromeBrsrC134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Removal of Private Network Access enterprise policies</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Private Network Access (PNA 1.0) is an unshipped security feature designed to limit website access to local networks. Due to deployability concerns, PNA 1.0 was never able to ship by default, as it was incompatible with too many existing devices.</p>

    <p>PNA 1.0 required changes to devices on local networks. Instead, Chrome is implementing an updated proposal, Private Network Access 2.0 (PNA 2.0). PNA 2.0 only requires changes to sites that need to access the local network, rather than requiring changes to devices on the local network. Sites are much easier to update than devices, and so this approach should be much more straightforward to roll out.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>The only way to enforce PNA 1.0 is via enterprise policy. To avoid regressing security for enterprise customers opting-in to PNA 1.0 prior to shipping PNA 2.0, we will maintain the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled</u></a> policy, which causes Chrome to send special preflight messages, until such time that it becomes incompatible with PNA 2.0.</p>

    <p>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed</u></a> policies, which loosen PNA 1.0 restrictions, will be removed in Chrome 135. These policies currently have no effect, since PNA 1.0 is not shipped, and they will have no meaning once PNA 1.0 is removed.</p>

    <p>PNA 2.0 is described in this <a href="https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/local-network-access" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>explainer on GitHub</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong>

        <p>Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowedForUrls</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecurePrivateNetworkRequestsAllowed</u></a> policies.</p>
      </li>
      <li>Chrome 137 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia
        <p>Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PrivateNetworkAccessRestrictionsEnabled</u></a>.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrE134" name="upChromeBrsrE134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Settings, site shortcuts, and themes improvements on Chrome Desktop</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>On Chrome 135 on Desktop, for users who newly sign in to Chrome or who have Sync enabled, settings, site shortcuts and themes synced to their Google Account will now be kept separate from the local ones, that is,&nbsp; settings from when they’re signed out or when Sync is turned off.</p>

    <p>This allows for strictly less data sharing than previously: local settings don’t get automatically uploaded when signing in or turning on Sync, and no settings from the account are left behind on the device when Sync is turned off.</p>

    <p>Existing enterprise policies <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncDisabled</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled </u></a>will continue to apply so admins can restrict or disable the Sync feature if they want to.</p>

    <p>Note: This change is a follow-up to the launch of the new identity model on Chrome Desktop. For more details, see <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5872905144238080" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Platform Status</u></a>.</p>

  <li><strong>Third-party cookies always blocked in Incognito mode</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

There will be no changes when the policy is true or unset. There will also be no changes to the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookieAllowedForUrls</u></a> policy, which will continue to apply in both regular and Incognito modes, as it applies at the site level and not globally.</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH134" name="upChromeBrsrH134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Blob URL Partitioning: Fetching/Navigation</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As a continuation of Storage Partitioning, Chromium will implement partitioning of <a href="https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Blob URL</u></a> access by Storage Key (top-level site, frame origin, and the has-cross-site-ancestor boolean), with the exception of top-level navigations which will remain partitioned only by frame origin. This behavior is similar to what’s currently implemented by both Firefox and Safari, and aligns Blob URL usage with the partitioning scheme used by other storage APIs as part of Storage Partitioning. In addition, Chromium will enforce noopener on renderer-initiated top-level navigations to Blob URLs where the corresponding site is cross-site to the top-level site performing the navigation. This aligns Chromium with similar behavior in Safari, and the relevant specs have been updated to reflect these changes.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This change can be temporarily reverted by setting the <strong>PartitionedBlobURLUsage </strong>policy. The policy will be deprecated when the other storage partitioning related enterprise policies are deprecated.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrI134" name="upChromeBrsrI134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Create service worker client and inherit service worker controller for srcdoc iframe</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Srcdoc context documents are currently not service worker clients and are not covered by their parent page’s service worker. This results in some discrepancies (for example, Resource Timing reports the URLs that these documents load, but the service worker doesn’t intercept them). We aim&nbsp; to fix the discrepancies by creating service worker clients for <code>srcdoc</code> iframes and make them inherit the parent page's service worker controller.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ134" name="upChromeBrsrJ134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate getters of Intl Locale Info API</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Intl Locale Info API is a Stage 3 ECMAScript <a href="https://github.com/tc39/proposal-intl-locale-info" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TC39 proposal</u></a> to enhance the <code>Intl.Locale</code> object by exposing locale information, such as week data (first day in a week, weekend start day, weekend end day, minimum day in the first week), and text direction hour cycle used in the locale.</p>

    <p>We shipped our implementation in <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5566859262820352" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome 99</u></a> but later on the proposal made some changes in Stage 3 and moved several getters to functions. We need to remove the deprecated getters and relaunch the renamed functions.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK134" name="upChromeBrsrK134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Partitioning :visited links history</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To eliminate user browsing history leaks, anchor elements are styled as <code>:visited</code> only if they have been clicked from this top-level site and frame origin before. On the browser-side, this means that the VisitedLinks hashtable is now partitioned by triple-keying, or by storing the following for each visited link: <code>&lt;link URL, top-level site, frame origin&gt;</code>. By only styling links that have been clicked on this site and frame before, the many side-channel attacks that have been developed to obtain <code>:visited </code>links styling information are now obsolete, as they no longer provide sites with new information about users.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>There is an exception for <em>self-links</em>, where links to a site's own pages can be styled as :visited even if they have not been clicked on in this exact top-level site and frame origin before. This exemption is only enabled in top-level frames or subframes, which are same-origin with the top-level frame. The privacy benefits above are still achieved because sites already know which of its subpages a user has visited, so no new information is exposed. This was a community-requested exception that improves user experience as well.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrLL134" name="upChromeBrsrLL134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>HSTS tracking prevention</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p><a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6797" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)</u></a> allows sites to declare themselves accessible through secure connections only. As early as Chrome 135, HSTS tracking prevention will mitigate&nbsp;user tracking by third-parties using&nbsp;the HSTS cache. It only allows HSTS upgrades for top-level navigations and blocks HSTS upgrades for sub-resource requests. This will prevent&nbsp;third-party sites using&nbsp;the HSTS cache to track users across the web. For more information, see this HSTS tracking prevention <a href="https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/HSTS-Tracking-Prevention" rel="noopener" target="_blank">explainer on Github</a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL134" name="upChromeBrsrL134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove deprecated navigator.xr.supportsSession method</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p><code>navigator.xr.supportsSession</code> was replaced in the WebXR spec by the <code>navigator.xr.isSessionSupported</code> method in September of 2019 after receiving feedback on the API shape from the TAG. It has been marked as deprecated in Chromium since then, producing a console warning redirecting developers to the updated API.</p>

    <p>Usage of the call is very low, as shown by <a href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/2416" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Status usage metrics</u></a>. Additionally, all major frameworks that are used to build WebXR content have been confirmed to have been updated to use the newer call.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrM134" name="upChromeBrsrM134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Strict Same Origin policy for Storage Access API</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 135 will adjust Storage Access API semantics to strictly follow the Same Origin policy, to enhance security. This means that using <code>document.requestStorageAccess()</code> in a frame will only attach cookies to requests to the iframe's origin (not site) by default.</p>

    <p>Note: the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a> policy or Storage Access headers can still be used to unblock cross-site cookies.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrN134" name="upChromeBrsrN134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome started directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Admins might use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, available from Chrome 125, to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 136, and will be removed in Chrome 137. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that admins can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise admins may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt-in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt-out through Chrome 136.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrO134" name="upChromeBrsrO134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove SwiftShader fallback</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As early as Chrome 137, we plan to deprecate automatic fallback to WebGL backed by SwiftShader. WebGL context creation will fail instead of falling back to SwiftShader. We plan to remove SwiftShader fallback&nbsp; for two primary reasons:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process.</li>
      <li>Users have a poor experience when falling back from a high-performance GPU-backed WebGL to a CPU-backed implementation. Users have no control over this behavior and it is difficult to describe in bug reports.</li>
    </ol>

    <p><a href="https://github.com/google/swiftshader" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SwiftShader</u></a> is a useful tool for web developers to test their sites on systems that are headless or do not have a supported GPU. This use case will still be supported by opting in but is not intended for running untrusted content.</p>

    <p>To opt-in to lower security guarantees and allow SwiftShader for WebGL, run the chrome executable with the <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> command-line switch.</p>

    <p>During the deprecation period, a warning will appear in the JavaScript console when a WebGL context is created and backed with SwiftShader. Passing <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> will remove this warning message.</p>

    <p>Chromium and other browsers do not guarantee WebGL availability. You can test and handle WebGL context creation failure and fall back to other web APIs such as Canvas2D or an appropriate message to the user.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrP134" name="upChromeBrsrP134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL host</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As stated in the <a href="http://whatwg.org" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WhatWG.org</u></a> spec, <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL hosts</u></a> cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host.</p>

    <p>This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a>&nbsp;and URL <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>focus areas</u></a>.</p>

    <p>To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows <code>file:// </code>URLs. To read more, see the discussion on <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>.</p>

    <p>This feature will be part of the ongoing work to bring Chromium closer to spec compliance by forbidding spaces in non-file URLs only.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 138 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrQ134" name="upChromeBrsrQ134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 to v5 migration</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the v5 API instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5.</p>

    <p>If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4*</code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead: <code>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</code>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 145 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows</strong>

        <p>This will be a gradual roll-out.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h4>Upcoming Chrome Enterprise Core changes</h4>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeECA134" name="upChromeECA134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Apple Extensible SSO support for Chrome on macOS</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Chrome 135 on macOS will enable seamless authentication for identity providers that are enabled via an OS-configured Enterprise Single Sign On (SSO) extension. For this initial release, it will allow end users on managed browsers to sign in to any Microsoft Entra-authenticated resources without the need to enter any credentials. Extensible SSO needs to be pre-configured in your environment and deployed with its respective enterprise device management solution. Additional identity providers might be supported in the near future.</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeECB134" name="upChromeECB134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Isolated Web Apps</strong>&nbsp;<a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Isolated Web Apps (IWAs) are an extension of existing work on PWA installation and Web Packaging that provide stronger protections against server compromise and other tampering, which is necessary for developers of security-sensitive applications.</p>

    <p>Rather than being hosted on live web servers and fetched over HTTPS, these applications are packaged into Web Bundles, signed by their developer, and distributed to end-users through one or more of the potential methods described in <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/tutorials/getting-started-with-isolated-web-apps" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Getting started with Isolated Web Apps</u></a>.</p>

    <p>In the initial release, IWAs will only be installable through a policy on enterprise-managed ChromeOS devices.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 140 on Windows</strong>

        <p>This rollout adds support for Isolated Web Apps in enterprise-managed browser configurations on Windows.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>ChromeOS updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeOSA134" name="chromeOSA134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Isolated Web Apps in ChromeOS kiosk mode&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 134, ChromeOS kiosk mode supports <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/web/isolated-web-apps" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Isolated Web Apps</u></a>, a more secure and versatile app solution with access to deep system integrations and powerful capabilities. Administrators can configure IWAs for kiosk and digital signage deployments on <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise⁠</u></a> managed devices through the <a href="https://workspace.google.com/products/admin/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Admin console⁠</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB134" name="chromeOSB134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Migrate data for graduating students&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>As early as March 2025, the new content transfer tool will guide graduating students or other EDU-managed users who want to migrate their data through an updated data transfer process. This will allow them to take their Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Gmail content to a Gmail account of their choice.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This new application allows school administrators to pin an icon to the shelf, notify students and faculty on their Chromebooks, and set dates to trigger these nudges to encourage them to use content transfer.</p>

    <p>For more details, see our&nbsp;article describing how to <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16100326" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Allow data transfer in schools</a> in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="432" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeYuh_keTQ9O6Jz4A1XUUmrvUT8te5j7kBPhUY9VL3ASujWgZGLpqFRJzYuN6juDF29q3QvU-bKXSudkxjDdgfhueidz9yejxDP75wYINzqRjWlWwADdwosFHcTgDpPSs9rA0ES4kLl8Znk5wbhG-OdxpoTyFZaSUKNBfyjBB7GD_rs?key=MD3rNYdxfGkXzGY2QuxNiT1d" width="648"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="chromeOSC134" name="chromeOSC134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Slow Keys&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Slow Keys is an accessibility feature designed to assist individuals with limited dexterity in typing more accurately. This feature is particularly helpful for those who have conditions such as tremors, arthritis, or numbness in their fingertips, which can make it difficult to press keys with precision.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Slow Keys works by introducing a delay, requiring keys to be held down for a set amount of time before they are registered. This will prevent unintended keystrokes from being pressed.&nbsp;</p>

    <p><img height="427" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeyonZJos0_52w4guVaIlFIW9_EgJzNbAd0mrOz8wHo7MkR3ILUPH7e6X5KPW8LWlY93Cu11tu4zCBGYh_VmTYQgbhlJtbJZrzVXhehFXesY-SqnAjqaz2IOc3cjJv6Eakc5p-HH3BP3xaQ3EYlURAGQvW2Ufftslg2okJq5-fQ3qLb?key=MD3rNYdxfGkXzGY2QuxNiT1d" width="624"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSD134" name="chromeOSD134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>GIFs with Quick Insert&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Quick Insert will soon support direct GIF insertion! Quickly add GIFs to your messages and documents without leaving the Quick Insert menu. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/15481991" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Use Quick Insert to add &amp; create content</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA134" name="upChromeOSA134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS policy for battery longevity&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 135 introduces a new battery charge limit policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DevicePowerBatteryChargingOptimization" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DevicePowerBatteryChargingOptimization</u></a> , which offers more optimization options. Battery charging optimization helps extend the lifespan of Chromebooks.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Administrators can still set a maximum charge limit, with 100% as the default, to minimize battery degradation and improve long-term reliability.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>The new policy benefits both administrators managing fleets of devices, such as in educational settings, and individual users seeking to maximize their Chromebook's longevity. This policy automatically applies and requires no user interaction.</p>

    <p><img height="130" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeMktQW3AD2VD5mj7Dj_uOp7hT6qTHLiOMNoxNsScl0FdlbvZm2ZZ07QqQ4EjI7vqwZE9x2_n0122Ts1nfrdS-esZuhJKTbJjPuF-KuMHfFikhy3Onzcr3ayWvws1_IzyP4aaDsDWNcyA6ZmIEnmSjZWiBbdS3tqur0sZM6Bc3L6Vwl?key=MD3rNYdxfGkXzGY2QuxNiT1d" width="364"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB134" name="upChromeOSB134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Kiosk Heartbeat change&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>Last summer, we sent out an MSA to inform the customer about a migration of the Kiosk Heartbeat API that ultimately needs an update to ChromeOS 126.</p>

    <p>If your organization is running a version older than ChromeOS 126, you need to update your device fleet. This kiosk heartbeat change requires an update to ChromeOS 126 or ChromeOS LTS 126 or to update to the current stable ChromeOS release.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>What do you need to do?</strong>

        <p>Please ensure you have activated (value: 0) DeviceChromeVariation for your organization until all devices have been updated to ChromeOS LTS 132. Once all devices are on ChromeOS LTS 132,&nbsp; DeviceChromeVariation is not needed anymore and can be changed to any value.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>What happens when DeviceChromeVariation is deactivated?</strong>

        <p>Devices on LTS versions older than ChromeOS LTS 132 will keep using the old Kiosk Heartbeat infrastructure until April 7th, 2025.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <p>Starting April 8th, 2025, all devices on LTS versions older than ChromeOS LTS 132 will stop sending device heartbeats.&nbsp;For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6179663" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Monitor kiosk health</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSC134" name="upChromeOSC134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Event-based device log collection for troubleshooting (Admin console)&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 135, to help troubleshoot device issues (like crashes or failed OS updates), our system will automatically be able to collect and upload device logs. This will happen when these specific settings are turned on:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Enable device system log upload: turns on the overall log collection</li>
      <li>Report device OS information -&gt; OS update status: collects data about OS updates</li>
      <li>Report device telemetry -&gt; Crash information : gathers fatal crash information</li>
    </ul>

    <p>When a problem occurs, IT admins will see a notification with a direct link to the uploaded logs on the ChromeOS device's details page in the Admin console. You can also see a history of device events. Log uploads happen a maximum of two times a day, and each file is typically 400KB to 1MB in size.</p>

    <p>For more details, see these articles in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13739279?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Remote log collection for ChromeOS devices</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1698333?hl=en#zippy=%2Cview-device-details" rel="noopener" target="_blank">View ChromeOS device list and details&nbsp;</a></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSD134" name="upChromeOSD134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>AI wallpapers and backgrounds&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 136, we plan to introduce high-resolution, generative AI wallpapers and video call backgrounds on ChromeOS. With this feature, you can unleash your creativity and turn your Chromebook into a canvas of personal expression. Choose from a diverse collection of templates and, in just a few clicks, infuse your Chromebook with your unique personality, mood, or interest.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Two new policies will be available to control these features; <strong>GenAIVcBackgroundSettings</strong> and <strong>GenAIWallpaperSettings</strong>. This feature will be available on <a href="https://www.google.com/chromebook/discover/chromebookplus/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromebook Plus devices</u></a> only.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSE134" name="upChromeOSE134"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Deprecating Chrome Apps support on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In 2016, we announced the deprecation of Chrome Apps in favor of web apps, and in 2021, we <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2021/10/extending-chrome-app-support-on-chrome.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>announced on the Chromium Blog</u></a> that support for Chrome Apps for ChromeOS Enterprise and Education customers and developers on ChromeOS would be extended until at least January 2025. With the majority of our customers having migrated off of Chrome Apps (including <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#packaged-app-legacy" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Legacy (v1) packaged apps</u></a> and <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#hosted-app" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Hosted apps</u></a>), we can confirm the following updates about Chrome Apps discontinuation dates.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>July 2025: End of support for user-installed Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M139).</strong>

        <ul>
          <li>Chrome Apps that are force-installed through the admin console will continue to be supported.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>July 2026: Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode (scheduled for ChromeOS M150).
        <ul>
          <li>Devices on the LTS channel with Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode will receive support until April 2027.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>February 2028: Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M168), marking the end of life for all Chrome Apps.
        <ul>
          <li>Devices on the LTS channel can continue to use Chrome Apps until October 2028.</li>
          <li>No exceptions will be granted.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>These deprecation timelines also apply to self-hosted Chrome Apps.</p>

    <p>While no new Chrome Apps can be added to the Chrome Web Store, existing Chrome Apps can continue to be updated through October 2028 when they will reach end of life on ChromeOS. After this date, Chrome Apps will be removed from the Chrome Web Store.</p>

    <p>If your organization has developed in-house Chrome Apps and you need assistance, please refer to <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/apps/migration/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Transition from Chrome Apps</u></a> guide. You can also join us in the <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/join-us-in-the-chromeos-developer-community-on-discord" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS developer community on Discord</u></a>, or reach out to us through the form at <a href="https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us" rel="noopener" target="_blank">https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us</a>. Refer to the <a href="https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS release schedule</u></a> for release dates and updates.</p>

    <p>In the coming weeks, additional detailed information will be sent to all remaining Chrome App developers and all ChromeOS Administrators.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes</h2>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA133" name="chromeBrsrAA133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Search with Google Lens on Desktop and iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Admins can control all elements of this feature through a policy called <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a>. To perform the search, a screenshot of the screen is sent to Google servers but it is not linked to any IDs or accounts, it is not viewed by any human, and data about its contents is not logged. To contextualize the search to the document or website the user is viewing, the PDF bytes or website HTML is sent to Google servers but is not linked to any IDs or accounts, not viewable by any human, and the data or data generated about its contents is not logged.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>Desktop</u></p>

    <p>Since Chrome 126, users can search any images or text they see on their Desktop screen with Google Lens. To use this feature, go to a website and click the <strong>Google Lens</strong> chip on the on-focus omnibox or by right-clicking on an image and selecting <strong>Search with Google Lens</strong>. Users can select anywhere on the screen to search its contents, and refine their search by adding questions to the search box. Starting in Chrome 132, users can also ask questions about entire web pages or PDF documents and answers will reference their current document and the web. To use this feature, invoke <strong>Search with Google Lens</strong> as described above and enter queries into the search box on the top right corner of the Chrome window. A side panel will open on the right side of the browser window with search results.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>iOS</u></p>

    <p>Since Chrome 131, users can search any images or text they see on their iOS Chrome screen with Google Lens. To use this feature, go to a website and click on the <strong>3-dot menu &gt; Search with Google Lens</strong>. Users can click, highlight, or drag anywhere on the screen to search its contents, and refine their search by adding keywords or questions to the search box.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>Rollout details:</u></p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 126 on ChromeOS, Linux, mac, Windows: Rollout of the feature at 1% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 127 on ChromeOS, Linux, mac, Windows: Rollout to 100% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 131 on iOS: Rollout of the feature at 1% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, mac, Windows: Rollout of the expanded feature at 1% Stable</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on iOS: Rollout to 100% Stable</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a name="chromeBrsrA133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Ad-hoc code signatures for PWA shims on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Code signatures for the application shims that are created when installing a Progressive Web App (PWA) on macOS are changing to use ad-hoc code signatures that are created when the application is installed. The code signature is used by macOS as part of the application's identity. These ad-hoc signatures result in each PWA shim having a unique identity to macOS, where previously every PWA looked like the same application to macOS.</p>

    <p>This update addresses problems when attempting to include multiple PWAs in the <strong>Open at Login</strong> preference pane on macOS, and permits future improvements to handling of user notifications within PWAs on macOS.</p>

    <p>Admins should test for compatibility with any endpoint security or binary authorization tools they use (such as Santa). The feature can be enabled for this testing using <code>chrome://flags/#use-adhoc-signing-for-web-app-shims</code>. They can then install a Progressive Web App and ensure that it launches as expected.</p>

    <p>If there is an incompatibility between the feature and their current security policies, the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AdHocCodeSigningForPWAsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AdHocCodeSigningForPWAsEnabled</u></a> policy can be used to disable the feature while they deploy an updated endpoint security policy. The enterprise policy is intended to be used to disable the feature only until endpoint security policies have been updated, at which point it should be unset.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 129 on macOS<br>
        Feature disabled behind a flag (<code>chrome://flags/#use-adhoc-signing-for-web-app-shims</code>) so that enterprises can test for compatibility with their endpoint security tools, such as <a href="https://santa.dev/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Santa</u></a>. If it is not currently compatible they can disable the feature via the enterprise policy while they update their endpoint security configurations. The enterprise policy is intended to be used to disable the feature only until endpoint security policies have been updated.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on macOS</strong>

        <p>Feature will begin to roll out to stable 100%.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB133" name="chromeBrsrB133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Sync stops support for Chrome versions more than four years old&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in February 2025, Chrome Sync (using and saving data in your Google Account) no longer supports Chrome versions that are more than four years old. To continue using Chrome Sync, you need to upgrade to a more recent version of Chrome. To read more, see this discussion: <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/thread/321051266" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Sync will be sunset on versions of Chrome that are more than four years old</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows</strong>

        <p>This change affects only the old versions of Chrome and will be rolled out server-side. Chrome 133 is specified only to reflect the timeline when the change will take&nbsp;effect.&nbsp;</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC133" name="chromeBrsrC133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New option in HttpsOnlyMode policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Ask Before HTTP (ABH), previously named HTTPS Only/First Modes, allows Chrome to ask for user consent before sending insecure HTTP content over the wire. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HttpsOnlyMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HttpsOnlyMode</u></a> policy allows force-enabling, or force-disabling, ABH.</p>

    <p>In Chrome 129, we added a new middle-ground variant of ABH called "balanced mode". This variant aims to reduce user inconvenience by working like (strict) ABH most of the time, but not asking when Chrome knows that an HTTPS connection isn't possible (such as when connecting to a single-label hostname like internal/).</p>

    <p>We are adding a force_balanced_enabled policy option to allow force-enabling this new variant. Setting force_balanced_enabled on browsers before Chrome 129 will result in the default behavior, which places no enterprise restrictions on the ABH setting.</p>

    <p>To avoid unexpected impact, if you have previously set force_enabled, we recommend not setting force_balanced_enabled until your entire fleet has upgraded to Chrome 129 or higher. If you are not migrating from force_enabled to force_balanced_enabled, you will be unaffected by this change.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 129 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD133" name="chromeBrsrD133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Tab freezing on Energy saver&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>When Energy saver is active, Chrome freezes a tab that has been hidden and silent for &gt;5 minutes and uses a lot of CPU, unless:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The tab provides audio- or video- conferencing functionality (detected via microphone, camera or screen/window/tab capture, or an RTCPeerConnection with an open RTCDataChannel or a live MediaStreamTrack).</li>
      <li>The tab controls an external device (detected via usage of Web USB, Web Bluetooth, Web HID or Web Serial).</li>
    </ul>

    <p>This will extend battery life and speed up Chrome through reduced CPU usage.<br>
      The feature can be tested using a flag,&nbsp; chrome://flags/#freezing-on-energy-saver. Alternatively, it can be tested with chrome://flags/#freezing-on-energy-saver-testing, which simulates Energy saver being active and all tabs using a lot of CPU; this allows you to verify whether tabs are eligible for freezing and would be frozen if using a lot of CPU.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        The feature will start rolling out to 1% of stable in Chrome 133.
        <p>Energy saver availability can be controlled via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BatterySaverModeAvailability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BatterySaverModeAvailability</u></a> policy (this change has no effect when Energy saver is inactive).</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE133" name="chromeBrsrE133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>V8 security setting on Android&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>V8 is Chrome’s JavaScript and WebAssembly engine used to improve site performance. To reduce the attack surface of Chrome, Chrome 133 on Android now includes a new setting on <code>chrome://settings/security</code> to disable the V8 Just-in-Time (JIT) optimizers. This maintains compatibility with Web Assembly. Admins can continue to control this feature using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DefaultJavaScriptJitSetting" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DefaultJavaScriptJitSetting</u></a> enterprise policy, and the associated <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#JavaScriptJitAllowedForSites" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>JavaScriptJitAllowedForSites</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#JavaScriptJitBlockedForSites" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>JavaScriptJitBlockedForSites</u></a> policies.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 122 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia<br>
        The setting rolls out in Chrome 121. The enterprise policies have been available since Chrome 93.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android</strong><br>
        The setting is available on Android in Chrome 133, under Site Settings. The enterprise policies are no longer marked experimental.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

    <p>We have removed the Chrome Welcome page from <code>initial_preferences</code> because that page is redundant with the First Run Experience that triggers on desktop platforms. <p><a id="chromeBrsrG133" name="chromeBrsrG133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support for non-special scheme URLs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Since Chrome 130, Chrome browser supports <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">non-special scheme URLs</a>, for example, <code>git://example.com/path</code>. Previously, the Chromium URL parser didn't support non-special URLs. The parser parses non-special URLs as if they had an opaque path, which is not aligned with the URL standard. In Chrome 133, the Chromium URL parser parses non-special URLs correctly, following the URL standard. For more details, see <a href="http://bit.ly/url-non-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">http://bit.ly/url-non-special</a>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</li>

      <li>Chrome 134 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android: Feature flag being removed</li>
    </ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrA133" name="upChromeBrsrA133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Privacy and security panel in Chrome DevTools&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 134, developers will be able to use the new <strong>Privacy and security</strong> panel in Chrome DevTools to test how their site will behave when third-party cookies are limited. Developers will be able to temporarily limit third-party cookies, observe how their site behaves, and review the status of third-party cookies on their site.</p>

    <p>This feature will not make any permanent changes to existing enterprise policies, but it will let third-party cookie related enterprise policies (that is, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BlockThirdPartyCookies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BlockThirdPartyCookies</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a>) be temporarily overridden to be more restrictive. If your enterprise policy already blocks third-party cookies using <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BlockThirdPartyCookies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BlockThirdPartyCookies</u></a>, this feature will be disabled.</p>

    <p>The new <strong>Privacy &amp; security</strong> panel will replace the existing <strong>Security</strong> panel. TLS connection and certificate information will continue to be available on the <strong>Security</strong> tab in the <strong>Privacy &amp; security</strong> panel.</p>

  <li><strong>Read aloud in Reading mode in Chrome 134&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

  </li>
