<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrD133" name="upChromeBrsrD133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Blob URL Partitioning: Fetching/Navigation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As a continuation of Storage Partitioning, Chromium will implement partitioning of Blob URL access by Storage Key (top-level site, frame origin, and the has-cross-site-ancestor boolean), with the exception of top-level navigations which will remain partitioned only by frame origin. This behavior is similar to what’s currently implemented by both Firefox and Safari, and aligns Blob URL usage with the partitioning scheme used by other storage APIs as part of Storage Partitioning. In addition, Chromium will enforce noopener on renderer-initiated top-level navigations to Blob URLs where the corresponding site is cross-site to the top-level site performing the navigation. This aligns Chromium with similar behavior in Safari, and the relevant specs have been updated to reflect these changes.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This change can be temporarily reverted by setting the <strong>PartitionedBlobURLUsage policy</strong>. The policy will be deprecated when the other storage partitioning related enterprise policies are deprecated.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrE133" name="upChromeBrsrE133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Create service worker client and inherit service worker controller for srcdoc iframe&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Srcdoc context documents are currently not service worker clients and are not covered by their parent page’s service worker. This results in some discrepancies (for example, Resource Timing reports the URLs that these documents load, but the service worker doesn’t intercept them). We aim&nbsp;to fix the discrepancies by creating service worker clients for srcdoc iframes and make them inherit the parent page's service worker controller.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrF133" name="upChromeBrsrF133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Fire error event instead of throwing exception for CSP blocked worker&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>When blocked by the Content Security Policy (<a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CSP" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSP</u></a>), Chromium currently throws a SecurityError exception from the&nbsp; "new Worker(url)" or "new SharedWorker(url)" constructors. According to the <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#fetch-integration" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSP specification</u></a>,&nbsp; the CSP check is performed as part of a fetch and an error event should fire after the object is returned. This update aims to make Chromium spec-conformant, by not throwing an exception from the constructor but instead firing an error event asynchronously.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrG133" name="upChromeBrsrG133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove nonstandard getUserMedia audio constraints&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Blink supports a number of nonstandard goog-prefixed constraints for getUserMedia from some time before constraints were properly standardized.</p>

    <p>Usage has gone down significantly ~0.000001% to 0.0009% (depending on the constraint) and some of them do not even have an effect due to changes in the Chromium audio-capture stack. Soon none of them will have any effect due to other upcoming changes.</p>

    <p>We do not expect any major regressions due to this change. Applications using these constraints will continue to work, but will get audio with default settings (as if no constraints were passed). They can easily migrate to standard constraints.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH133" name="upChromeBrsrH133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate mutation events&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Synchronous mutation events, including <code>DOMSubtreeModified</code>, <code>DOMNodeInserted</code>, <code>DOMNodeRemoved</code>, <code>DOMNodeRemovedFromDocument</code>, <code>DOMNodeInsertedIntoDocument</code>, and <code>DOMCharacterDataModified</code>, negatively affect page performance, and also significantly increase the complexity of adding new features to the Web. These APIs were deprecated from the spec in 2011, and were replaced (in 2012) by the much better-behaved Mutation Observer API. Usage of the obsolete mutation events must be removed or migrated to Mutation Observer.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Since Chrome 124, a temporary enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a>, is available to re-enable deprecated or removed mutation events. To read more, see <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/mutation-events-deprecation" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>this</u></a> blog post. If you encounter any issues, file a bug <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Mutation event support is disabled by default, since Chrome 127, or around July 30, 2024. Code should have been migrated before that date to avoid site breakage. If more time is needed, there are a few options:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/origintrials/#/view_trial/919297273937002497" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Mutation Events Deprecation Trial</u></a> can be used to re-enable the feature for a limited time on a given site. This can be used up until Chrome 134, ending March 25, 2025.</li>
      <li>A <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy can also be used for the same purpose, also through Chrome 134.</li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy will be deprecated.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrHH133" name="upChromeBrsrHH133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Cross-device synchronization of Chrome settings and themes on Desktop&nbsp;at sign-in&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Following the launch of the new identity model on Chrome Desktop, we plan to enable account settings, themes and site shortcuts to users at&nbsp;sign-in (rather than needing to sync).</p>

    <p>To do this, we will introduce&nbsp;local and account storage&nbsp;for each of these data types.</p>

    <p>This means:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>For Chrome users on Desktop who&nbsp;sign in to Chrome or who have Sync enabled, settings, site shortcuts and themes synced to their Google Account will&nbsp;be kept separate from the local ones, that is, settings from when they’re signed out or when Sync is turned off.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>This allows for strictly less data sharing than previously: local settings don’t get automatically uploaded when users sign&nbsp;in or turn&nbsp;on Sync, and no settings from their account storage are left behind on the device when Sync is turned off.</li>
      <li>
        <p>Existing Chrome policies <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncDisabled</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a> will continue to apply so admins can restrict or disable the Sync feature if they want to.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Linux, MacOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrI133" name="upChromeBrsrI133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL host&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As stated in the <a href="http://whatwg.org" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WhatWG.org</u></a> spec, <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL hosts</u></a> cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host.</p>

    <p>This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 'HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a>' and URL <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>focus areas</u></a>.</p>

    <p>To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows <code>file:// </code>URLs. To read more, see the discussion on <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>.</p>

    <p>This feature will be part of the ongoing work to bring Chromium closer to spec compliance by forbidding spaces for non-file URLs only.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ133" name="upChromeBrsrJ133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Due to unexpected issues, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled</u></a>&nbsp;will be removed in Chrome 135. If you have feedback about this removal, please file a bug <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/u/1/issues/377321453" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 132 on Windows<br>
        Deprecation of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled </u></a>policy</li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows</strong><br>
        Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled</u></a> policy</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK133" name="upChromeBrsrK133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate getters of Intl Locale Info API&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Intl Locale Info API is a Stage 3 ECMAScript <a href="https://github.com/tc39/proposal-intl-locale-info" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TC39 proposal</u></a> to enhance the Intl.Locale object by exposing locale information, such as week data (first day in a week, weekend start day, weekend end day, minimum day in the first week), and text direction hour cycle used in the locale.</p>

    <p>We shipped our implementation in <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5566859262820352" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome 99 </u></a>&nbsp;but later on the proposal made some changes in Stage 3 and moved several getters to functions. We need to remove the deprecated getters and relaunch the renamed functions.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL133" name="upChromeBrsrL133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove SwiftShader fallback&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Allowing automatic fallback to WebGL backed by SwiftShader is deprecated and WebGL context creation will fail instead of falling back to SwiftShader. This was done for two primary reasons:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process.</li>
      <li>Users have a poor experience when falling back from a high-performance GPU-backed WebGL to a CPU-backed implementation. Users have no control over this behavior and it is difficult to describe in bug reports.</li>
    </ol>

    <p>SwiftShader is a useful tool for web developers to test their sites on systems that are headless or do not have a supported GPU. This use case will still be supported by opting in but is not intended for running untrusted content.</p>

    <p>To opt-in to lower security guarantees and allow SwiftShader for WebGL, run the chrome executable with the --enable-unsafe-swiftshader command-line switch.</p>

    <p>During the deprecation period, a warning will appear in the JavaScript console when a WebGL context is created and backed with SwiftShader. Passing --enable-unsafe-swiftshader will remove this warning message.</p>

    <p>Chromium and other browsers do not guarantee WebGL availability. You can test and handle WebGL context creation failure and fall back to other web APIs such as Canvas2D or an appropriate message to the user.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Windows,&nbsp; macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrM133" name="upChromeBrsrM133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 to v5 migration&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the v5 API instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5.</p>

    <p>If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4*</code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead:<u> </u><a href="http://safebrowsing.googleapis.com" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</u></a>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux,&nbsp; macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>

    <p>This will be a gradual roll-out.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrN133" name="upChromeBrsrN133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome started directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Admins might use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, available from Chrome 125, to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 136, and will be removed in Chrome 137. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that admins can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise admins may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt-in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt-out through Chrome 136.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.&nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>ChromeOS updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeOSA133" name="chromeOSA133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Enhanced Office file handling for managed users&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Starting from ChromeOS 133, managed users can now seamlessly open and edit their Microsoft Office files (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), regardless of whether they use Office for the web in Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace.</p>

    <p>Organizations using Office for the web benefit from OneDrive integration into the <strong>Files</strong> app, Microsoft 365 PWA system integrations for a desktop-like experience, SSO for all required applications, and advanced policy controls for preconfiguration.</p>

    <p>For Google Workspace customers, the transition of local files to Google Workspace is optimized.</p>

    <p>For more information, see&nbsp;<a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15747781" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Set up Office file handling for managed users</a>&nbsp;in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center.</p>

    <p>New policies for Microsoft Office file handling include:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MicrosoftOneDriveMount" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MicrosoftOneDriveMount</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MicrosoftOneDriveAccountRestrictions" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MicrosoftOneDriveAccountRestrictions</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MicrosoftOfficeCloudUpload" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MicrosoftOfficeCloudUpload</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GoogleWorkspaceCloudUpload" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GoogleWorkspaceCloudUpload</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#QuickOfficeForceFileDownloadEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>QuickOfficeForceFileDownloadEnabled</u></a></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB133" name="chromeOSB133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Make cloud storage the sole data storage option on ChromeOS devices&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 133 introduces a true cloud-first experience, allowing admins to ensure that all files are stored on either Google Workspace or Microsoft OneDrive by blocking local storage. This feature prevents data loss, reduces security risks, supports legal hold requirements, and is particularly beneficial for shared devices.</p>

    <p>For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15788473" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Use cloud storage as sole storage option on ChromeOS devices</a>&nbsp;in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center.</p>

    <p>New policies for cloud storage include:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalUserFilesAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalUserFilesAllowed</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LocalUserFilesMigrationDestination" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LocalUserFilesMigrationDestination</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DownloadDirectory" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DownloadDirectory</u></a> (OneDrive support)</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ScreenCaptureLocation" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ScreenCaptureLocation</u></a></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSC133" name="chromeOSC133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Bounce Keys on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Bounce Keys is an accessibility feature designed to make computer use easier for individuals with limited dexterity or tremors. It works by ignoring repeated keystrokes within a short time interval, which you can customize to fit your needs. This prevents unintended characters being entered due to unintentional key presses.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="410" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf_KQXr5-gORQV8UwjsJ9wJg7a9q0EIiqPmPhQ_kiLmeXq7y5A9P0xV2LgyHJAUsti2KbY-oC9DhE6T8Pe89YuAavx8MGWtOlN9KhoDzKW6wtXhDxDXoSUTcSVNOdE83J7yVHFmaUw?key=cZlxCRpU63yiPVR8sOHX8jV8" width="702"></p>
    <br>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSD133" name="chromeOSD133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Enhanced Welcome Tour&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>New ChromeOS users are now greeted with a Welcome Tour immediately after device setup. Welcome Tour provides an interactive way for users to learn the basics and to get up and running on their new Chromebook quickly.</p>

    <p><img height="452" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcPRH9DlejEIKtINHCNOahndDk5mV6zYKjJLLwCj66rNWo5ehDUlnPtpY_1UPC6raQDDAFpD3Yy2fNYO7Kq4wcoJsRwbRrlpfTMnMqFql2A5twcGo3xSwcl5-ZY0q4lmNSh5BeJvyU?key=cZlxCRpU63yiPVR8sOHX8jV8" width="707"></p>
  </li>

<p><a id="chromeOSDD133" name="chromeOSDD133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>New ChromeOS policy for keyboard languages&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 133, a new <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AllowedInputMethodsForceEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AllowedInputMethodsForceEnabled</u></a> policy allows administrators to automatically install keyboard languages previously set by <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AllowedInputMethods" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AllowedInputMethods</u></a>. The user can not add new or remove selected keyboard languages when the policy is set.</p>
  </li>

<p><a id="chromeOSE133" name="chromeOSE133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Screencast language update&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Screencast now supports over 50 languages. To use Screencast, press the <strong>Launcher</strong> icon and search for <em>Screencast</em>. You can find the list of languages in the Help Center article: <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11972236" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Use the Screencast app to record and share on your ChromeOS devices</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="398" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXftETOfAoxyGDJZyaQLSBDYfUmC9PLxS6xVqgftowWMIP8gBcBm3WJhNMrpkShRK4pKv75iLABi6LV718zrgGCmWv83YfwMG_1MRGdFXLDhQZUYJD88rWONzSCsnnA7fjI1Zo8wWw?key=cZlxCRpU63yiPVR8sOHX8jV8" width="719"></p>

<p><a id="chromeOSF133" name="chromeOSF133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>

    <p><strong>New toggle for Bluetooth mic Super Resolution&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 133 adds a toggle to control <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/bluetooth-microphone-super-resolution-better-nbs-sound-quality-through-machine-learning" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Bluetooth mic Super Resolution</u></a>.     <p><strong>Health monitoring for Kiosk devices&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 133 improves status update latency for health monitoring for Kiosk devices. Under ideal conditions, status updates for Kiosk devices are now reported in about a minute. Offline status should now be sent or updated within 11 minutes. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6179663" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Monitor kiosk health</u></a> in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center.</p>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA133" name="upChromeOSA133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Kiosk Heartbeat change&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>Last summer, we sent out an MSA to inform the customer about a migration of the Kiosk Heartbeat API that ultimately needs an update to ChromeOS 126.</p>

    <p>If your organization is running a version older than ChromeOS 126, you need to update your device fleet. This kiosk heartbeat change requires an update to ChromeOS 126 or ChromeOS LTS 126 or to update to the current stable ChromeOS release.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>What do you need to do?</strong></li>
    </ul>

    <p>Please ensure you have activated (value: 0) DeviceChromeVariation for your organization until all devices have been updated to LTS132.</p>

    <p>Once all devices are on LTS132,&nbsp; DeviceChromeVariation is not needed anymore and can be changed to any value.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>What happens when DeviceChromeVariation is deactivated?</strong></li>
    </ul>

    <p>Devices on LTS versions older than LTS132 will keep using the old Kiosk Heartbeat infrastructure until April 7th, 2025.</p>

    <p>Starting April 8th, 2025, all devices on LTS versions older than ChromeOS LTS 132 will stop sending device heartbeats.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB133" name="upChromeOSB133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Isolated Web Apps in ChromeOS kiosk mode&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 134, ChromeOS kiosk mode will support <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/web/isolated-web-apps" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Isolated Web Apps</u></a>, a more secure and versatile app solution with access to deep system integrations and powerful capabilities. Administrators will be able to configure IWAs for kiosk and digital signage deployments on <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Enterprise⁠</u></a> managed devices through the <a href="https://workspace.google.com/products/admin/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Admin console⁠</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSC133" name="upChromeOSC133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Migrate data for graduating students&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as March 2025, the new content transfer tool will guide graduating students or other EDU-managed users who want to migrate their data through the updated <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13861235" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Google Takeout</u></a> transfer process. This will allow them to take their Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Gmail content to a Gmail account of their choice.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This new application allows school administrators to pin an icon to the shelf, notify students and faculty on their Chromebooks, and set dates to trigger these nudges to encourage them to use content transfer.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="432" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf-UqLwkaQ36lVvTDdjiuUsONsX3HFscjn57weDowe8rZFlH4fAm0SBeAaaL9x2l7KCVSv5qrqBWXedWX0ce1R7J7iLYLGquUM4oHVKL3f8uw0mELZdHUjMeDWl39IOmJI-QHJH8g?key=cZlxCRpU63yiPVR8sOHX8jV8" width="648"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSD133" name="upChromeOSD133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>New ChromeOS policy for battery longevity&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 134, we will introduce a new battery charge limit policy that will offer more optimization options, which will help extend the lifespan of Chromebooks. Administrators will still be able to set a maximum charge limit, with 100% as the default, to minimize battery degradation and improve long-term reliability. This new policy will benefit both administrators managing fleets of devices, such as in educational settings, and individual users seeking to maximize their Chromebook's longevity. This policy will automatically apply and will require no user interaction.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSE133" name="upChromeOSE133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Slow Keys&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>Slow Keys is an accessibility feature designed to assist individuals with limited dexterity in typing more accurately. This feature is particularly helpful for those who have conditions such as tremors, arthritis, or numbness in their fingertips, which can make it difficult to press keys with precision. Slow Keys will work by introducing a delay, requiring keys to be held down for a set amount of time before they are registered. This will prevent unintended keystrokes from being pressed.&nbsp;</p>

    <p><img height="427" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfOtyYjMz0JFvDrn_OSF756HNwuFSzQJKT-98KFOnP3Az96mzlQrIAaIJ3GlgZyjHegwAxn1-SRG3U-aY3onxrc628aalyXd2Tx4jp8McFCzOzKwD1IauKQAJUCohf9ZWI1_YpG5nc?key=cZlxCRpU63yiPVR8sOHX8jV8" width="624"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSF133" name="upChromeOSF133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>GIFs with Quick Insert&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>Quick Insert will soon support direct GIF insertion! Quickly add GIFs to your messages and documents without leaving the Quick Insert menu. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/15481991" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Use Quick Insert to add &amp; create content</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSG133" name="upChromeOSG133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>AI wallpapers and backgrounds&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 135, we plan to introduce high-resolution, generative AI wallpapers and video call backgrounds on ChromeOS. With this feature, you can unleash your creativity and turn your Chromebook into a canvas of personal expression. Choose from a diverse collection of templates and, in just a few clicks, infuse your Chromebook with your unique personality, mood, or interest.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Two new policies will be available to control these features; <strong>GenAIVcBackgroundSettings</strong> and <strong>GenAIWallpaperSettings</strong>. This feature will be available on <a href="https://www.google.com/chromebook/discover/chromebookplus/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromebook Plus devices</u></a> only.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSH133" name="upChromeOSH133"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Deprecating Chrome Apps support&nbsp;on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In 2016, we announced the deprecation of Chrome Apps in favor of web apps, and in 2021, we <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2021/10/extending-chrome-app-support-on-chrome.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>announced on the Chromium Blog</u></a> that support for Chrome Apps for ChromeOS Enterprise and Education customers and developers on ChromeOS would be extended until at least January 2025. With the majority of our customers having migrated off of Chrome Apps (including <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#packaged-app-legacy" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Legacy (v1) packaged apps</u></a> and <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#hosted-app" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Hosted apps</u></a>), we can confirm the following updates about Chrome Apps discontinuation dates.</p>

    <p>&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>July 2025: End of support for user-installed Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M138).</strong>

        <ul>
          <li>Chrome Apps that are force-installed through the Admin console will continue to be supported.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>July 2026: Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode (scheduled for ChromeOS M150).
        <ul>
          <li>Devices on the LTS channel with Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode will receive support until April 2027.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>February 2028: Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M168), marking the end of life for all Chrome Apps.
        <ul>
          <li>Devices on the LTS channel can continue to use Chrome Apps until October 2028.</li>
          <li>No exceptions will be granted.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <p>These deprecation timelines also apply to self-hosted Chrome Apps.</p>

    <p>While no new Chrome Apps can be added to the Chrome Web Store, existing Chrome Apps can continue to be updated through October 2028 when they will reach end of life on ChromeOS. After this date, Chrome Apps will be removed from the Chrome Web Store.</p>

    <p>If your organization has developed in-house Chrome Apps and you need assistance, please refer to <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/apps/migration/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Transition from Chrome Apps</u></a> guide. You can also join us in the <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/join-us-in-the-chromeos-developer-community-on-discord" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS developer community on Discord</u></a>, or reach out to us through the form at <a href="https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us" rel="noopener" target="_blank">https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us</a>. Refer to the <a href="https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS release schedule</u></a> for release dates and updates.</p>

    <p>In the coming weeks, additional detailed information will be sent to all remaining Chrome App developers and all ChromeOS Administrators.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes</h2>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA132" name="chromeBrsrA132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Search with Google Lens&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In Chrome 132, we begin to roll out this enhanced feature across all platforms. Admins can control all elements of this feature through a policy called <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a>. To perform the search, a screenshot of the screen is sent to Google servers but it is not linked to any IDs or accounts, it is not viewed by any human, and data about its contents is not logged. To contextualize the search to the document or website the user is viewing, the PDF bytes or website HTML is sent to Google servers but is not linked to any IDs or accounts, not viewable by any human, and the data or data generated about its contents is not logged.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>Desktop</u></p>

    <p>Since Chrome 126, users can search any images or text they see on their Desktop screen with Google Lens. To use this feature, go to a website and click the <strong>Google Lens</strong> chip on the on-focus omnibox or by right-clicking on an image and selecting <strong>Search with Google Lens</strong>. Users can select anywhere on the screen to search its contents, and refine their search by adding questions to the search box. Starting in Chrome 132, users can also ask questions about entire web pages or PDF documents and answers will reference their current document and the web. To use this feature, invoke <strong>Search with Google Lens</strong> as described above and enter queries into the search box on the top right corner of the Chrome window. A side panel will open on the right side of the browser window with search results.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>iOS</u></p>

    <p>Since Chrome 131, users can search any images or text they see on their iOS Chrome screen with Google Lens. To use this feature, go to a website and click on the <strong>3-dot menu &gt; Search with Google Lens</strong>. Users can click, highlight, or drag anywhere on the screen to search its contents, and refine their search by adding keywords or questions to the search box.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><u>Rollout details:</u></p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 126 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout of the feature at 1% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 127 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout to 100% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 131 on iOS: Rollout of the feature at 1% Stable</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows:</strong> Rollout of the expanded feature at 1% Stable</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB132" name="chromeBrsrB132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Network Service sandboxed on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>To improve security and reliability, the network service, already running in its own process, is now sandboxed on Windows. As part of this, third-party code that is currently able to tamper with the network service may be prevented from doing so. This might cause interoperability issues with software that injects code into Chrome's process space, such as Data Loss Prevention software. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#NetworkServiceSandboxEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>NetworkServiceSandboxEnabled</u></a> policy allows you to disable the sandbox if incompatibilities are discovered. You can test the sandbox in your environment using these <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Bk3Z8CUQucd8FP6ISKkT3Q9YYuP43574VIO_kyAISBU/view#heading=h.llygd223jffh" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>instructions</u></a>.</p>

    <p>You can <a href="https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/entry?template=Enterprise+Issue&amp;summary=Network+Sandbox+Issue+:&amp;comment=Chrome" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>report </u></a>any issues you encounter.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows</strong><br>
        Network Service sandboxed on Windows</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC132" name="chromeBrsrC132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Ad-hoc code signatures for Progressive Web App shims on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;

    <p>Code signatures for the application shims that are created when installing a Progressive Web App on macOS are changing to use ad-hoc code signatures that are created when the application is installed. The code signature is used by macOS as part of the application's identity. These ad-hoc signatures result in each PWA app shim having a unique identity to macOS, where previously every PWA looked like the same application to macOS.</p>

    <p>This update addresses problems when attempting to include multiple Progressive Web Applications in macOS's <strong>Open at Login</strong> preference pane, and permits future improvements to handling of user notifications within PWAs on macOS.</p>

    <p>Admins should test for compatibility with any endpoint security or binary authorization tools they use (such as <a href="https://santa.dev/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Santa</u></a>). The feature can be enabled for this testing using <code>chrome://flags/#use-adhoc-signing-for-web-app-shims</code>. They can then install a Progressive Web App and ensure that it launches as expected.</p>

    <p>If there is an incompatibility between the feature and their current security policies, the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AdHocCodeSigningForPWAsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AdHocCodeSigningForPWAsEnabled</u></a> policy can be used to disable the feature while they deploy an updated endpoint security policy. The enterprise policy is intended to be used to disable the feature only until endpoint security policies have been updated, at which point it should be unset.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 129 on macOS<br>
        Feature disabled behind a flag (<code>chrome://flags/#use-adhoc-signing-for-web-app-shims</code>) so that enterprises can test for compatibility with their endpoint security tools, such as <a href="https://santa.dev/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Santa</u></a>. If it is not currently compatible they can disable the feature via the enterprise policy while they update their endpoint security configurations. The enterprise policy is intended to be used to disable the feature only until endpoint security policies have been updated.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on macOS</strong><br>
        This feature will begin to roll out to stable, starting at 1% rollout.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD132" name="chromeBrsrD132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Batch upload&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Since Chrome 128, users have access to their passwords and addresses from their Google Account at the point of sign-in (in addition to their payment methods, which was an existing sign-in feature). These data-types have two distinct storages: local and account. With Chrome 132, we are providing users an opportunity to upload any local data they have to their Google Account. This will first be made available for passwords and addresses and will be expanded to include other data types in the future.</p>

    <p>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a> policy applies equally to sync and data upload. Therefore, if either passwords or addresses are disabled, they are not made available for upload in the batch uploader.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="318" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeZ03I-Bey5E0bka-JB07qB3X2fBjdAEgELrCJLupzpBS327J6R8-Ry9JAUzA1bpRiXdd8BqVIjCcjhBZzknxe2Hn8uqBf54yiNAKCvqoJ3S8GswAjhRZZJUm9XY3ltk4PuyPmiG2s?key=cjF-LTTEcICJMeqE5_7vuqd2" width="360"><img height="321" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdGhyYKwfzI_r4NUi0xP3_beL1f4ZkGN0YRftwWhSaCTXsHo44kymH8sMPhsrkvwizhFl3Xwt8QVDzFBk2zXWrKZnFKovthp7_22YihK1xim2J9NgLOqFI1ocir_kRObPaM-AKXDMQ?key=cjF-LTTEcICJMeqE5_7vuqd2" width="265"></p>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE132" name="chromeBrsrE132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Connectors Disclaimer workflow updates&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>We have made updates to our <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/terms/chrome-enterprise-core/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Terms of Service</u></a> for Chrome Enterprise Core that includes a section on 3rd party data-sharing. These updates improve the sign-up flow for Chrome browser Enterprise connectors.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrEE132" name="chromeBrsrEE132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>DownloadRestrictions is stricter on file type restrictions&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>You can control downloads within your organization using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DownloadRestrictions"><u>DownloadRestrictions</u></a> policy, with options to allow you select an appropriate level of file type restrictions:</p>

    <p>0 = No special restrictions. Default.<br>
      1 = Block malicious downloads and dangerous file types.<br>
      2 = Block malicious downloads, uncommon or unwanted downloads and dangerous file types.<br>
      3 = Block all downloads.<br>
      4 = Block malicious downloads. Recommended.</p>
    Where option value = 1, this means:

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome browser blocks malicious files flagged by the Safe Browsing server AND blocks all dangerous file types. Only recommended for OUs, browsers, or users that have a high tolerance for false positives.</li>
    </ul>

    <p>Where option value = 2, this means:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome browser blocks malicious files flagged by the Safe Browsing server AND blocks uncommon or unwanted files flagged by the Safe Browsing server AND blocks all dangerous file types. Only recommended for OUs, browsers, or users that have a high tolerance for false positives.</li>
    </ul>

    <p>Previously, the <em>dangerous file types</em>&nbsp;blocking was not being correctly applied by Chrome, and this has now been fixed. This means, however, that the policy is now much stricter on certain file types that could be dangerous to the user, like `<code>.exe</code>` or `<code>.msi</code>` files on Windows. If this induces too many false positives, you can leave the policy unset or set the policy value to 4.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrF132" name="chromeBrsrF132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Updates to Chrome Identity model on desktop&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Instead of having to set up Chrome sync on your device, you can now simply sign in to Chrome to access and save items to your Google Account. This new identity model on Desktop also includes an explicit sign-in to Chrome from a web sign-in.</p>

    <p>Signing into the web (using Gmail) prompts users to sign-in to Chrome. If they decline, they won’t be signed-in to Chrome, only to the web.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>If they accept, profile management (user-based policies), payments (already available today), passwords, addresses, bookmarks*, extensions*, search engine prefs*, themes* and PWAs* will be enabled.</li>
      <li>If they decline, Chrome can still use the sign-in credentials to facilitate a one-click sign-in to Chrome.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>Synchronizing history, Open tabs and tab groups still exist behind a separate opt-in for now.</li>
      <li>Invalidated credentials (e.g. signing out of the web or remote sign-out) will put Chrome in a ‘pending’ state, previously ‘sync paused’. Autofill data will not be available from the user’s Google Account. Users in this state will be prompted to “Verify it’s you” in the Chrome toolbar.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>*These data types will be enabled behind sign-in (instead of sync opt in) in upcoming Chrome milestones.</p>

    <p>Web sign-in intercepts can be controlled using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SigninInterceptionEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SigninInterceptionEnabled</u></a> policy. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11198768" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Force users to create a separate profile</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Linux, macOS, Windows </strong>Roll-out starts<br>
        &nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="145" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf_YIGQJqKMB77AW-RZC6Qf06TH-zA6fEu_RiJVgO0dc0HIR3V1VshEFLe3gAxPV2j4us26qYqoCu4BzlM9QMLgs3E-7GgxvxRwQPLpkiXp56ftpIMJaMYEEoW9aYWguQF16bc6XnQ?key=cjF-LTTEcICJMeqE5_7vuqd2" width="197"><img height="143" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcYGPmaqkclUxKh7cbA9pczVxAyRpyNlwW9Qy4ls0_aQbRbqSJCZMyQPki9MFFell5biQvMQcqPSGiYGDARAStby0yLFhcPywult_blATYYEHJywPCu61bjQ7fRkfdO_6NaDwi-ULE?key=cjF-LTTEcICJMeqE5_7vuqd2" width="195"><img height="142" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdamOX8Tnn9Hn01kB4ktZtXIit1YBQ5GzbWjq-QQSKChnEQsMqza5UcVBRO8G-AlJUWzY0VNbfohaKtKbFVy6KD3xipZ90GKa-CH9uJRfqFRDopNaMY4oFM9Jz0wNM9FZRxbX_yN4U?key=cjF-LTTEcICJMeqE5_7vuqd2" width="198"></p>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrG132" name="chromeBrsrG132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>HTTPS-First Mode for Typically Secure Users&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>HTTPS-First Mode (HFM) enables a default-HTTPS experience in Chrome by automatically upgrading sites to HTTPS. If a site doesn’t support HTTPS, HFM shows a warning before loading the HTTP version. HFM significantly improves the security guarantees of HTTPS by preventing loading of HTTP URLs without explicit user approval.</p>

    <p>HFM for typically secure users (this feature) is a heuristic that can automatically enable HFM for the user if the user has a typically secure browsing pattern. Typically secure browsing pattern is determined by keeping track of HTTPS-Upgrade fallbacks (failed HTTPS Upgrades, which would be HFM interstitials if the user manually enabled HFM) and a few other factors such as profile age and overall site engagement score.</p>

    <p>If these signals indicate that the user mostly visits secure sites, the heuristic will automatically enable HFM setting. HFM interstitials caused by this heuristic will display a custom message. The user can disable HFM by simply turning off the UI setting and the heuristic will never kick in again.</p>

    <p>This feature can be controlled using the existing enterprise policies <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HttpsOnlyMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HttpsOnlyMode</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HttpAllowlist" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HttpAllowlist.</u></a></p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrH132" name="chromeBrsrH132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Passkeys on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Passkeys are a more secure alternative to passwords. Unlike passwords, which can be phished or guessed, passkeys let users authenticate to sites and apps using public-key cryptography, as defined in the Webauthn standard.</p>

    <p>Google Password Manager passkeys are already available in Chrome on other platforms; this launch brings them to the iOS platform, through enhancements to Chrome's existing Credential Provider Extension ("Passwords in Other Apps"). Using the Extension, Google Password Manager passkeys can be used to sign in to pages in Chrome and other browsers, as well as to native apps.</p>

    <p>Passkeys are saved to a user's Google Account and available whenever the user is signed in to Chrome. Relevant enterprise policies such as <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a>, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PasswordManagerEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PasswordManagerEnabled</u></a> will continue to work as before and can be used to configure whether users can use and save passwords in their Google Account.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on iOS</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

    <p>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PasswordLeakDetectionEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PasswordLeakDetectionEnabled</u></a> toggle that was originally found on <code>chrome://settings/security</code> is moving from under the standard protection heading to further down on the page under the <strong>Advanced</strong> section.&nbsp;</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrM132" name="chromeBrsrM132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support non-special scheme URLs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 130 supports <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">non-special scheme URLs</a>, for example, <u>git://example.com/path</u>. Previously, the Chromium URL parser didn't support non-special URLs. The parser parses non-special URLs as if they had an opaque path, which is not aligned with the URL standard. Now, the Chromium URL parser parses non-special URLs correctly, following the URL standard. For more details, see <a href="http://bit.ly/url-non-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">http://bit.ly/url-non-special</a>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>

The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/?policy=LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a> enterprise policy is in place allowing you&nbsp;to turn the feature on or off.</p>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrO132" name="chromeBrsrO132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>User Link capturing on PWAs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Web links automatically direct users to installed web apps. To better align with users' expectations around installed web apps, Chrome makes it easier to move between the browser and installed web apps. When the user clicks a link that could be handled by an installed web app, Chrome adds a chip in the address bar to suggest switching over to the app. When the user clicks the chip, this either launches the app directly, or opens a grid of apps that can support that link. For some users, clicking a link always automatically opens the app.<br>
      When some users click a link, it always opens in an installed PWA, while some users see the link open in a new tab with a chip in the address bar and clicking the chip launches the app. A flag is available to control this feature: <code>chrome://flags/#enable-user-link-capturing-pwa</code>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        Launch to 100% of Stable with either a default on (always launch apps on link clicks) or a default off (always open in a tab, only launch if the user clicks on chip on address bar).</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><strong><img height="374" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdxprtppr2g-VIrtg0ZvRiMylo7j3hvVG1QHqMcAGpnQWGzj9QNmdoLWKLUf_m9vjPqM832D1w7np8ieC7zQHkYx4SsMcNfsPo5yLIswZfEugJIRHjvGfhaGg8NqgZALsl2oDOUAnc?key=cjF-LTTEcICJMeqE5_7vuqd2" width="658"></strong></p>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrP132" name="chromeBrsrP132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Keyboard-focusable scroll containers&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Improves accessibility by making scroll containers focusable using sequential focus navigation. Today, the tab key doesn't focus scrollers unless tabIndex is explicitly set to 0 or more.</p>

    <p>By making scrollers focusable by default, users who can't (or don't want to) use a mouse will be able to focus clipped content using a keyboard's tab and arrow keys. This behavior is enabled only if the scroller does not contain any keyboard focusable children. This logic is necessary so we don't cause regressions for existing focusable elements that might exist within a scroller like a &lt;textarea&gt;.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><strong>Note:</strong> The previous rollout of this feature (started first in Chrome 127 and again in Chrome 130) was stopped due to an accessibility regression, which should be fixed in the current implementation shipping in Chrome 132.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrQ132" name="chromeBrsrQ132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove Prefixed HTMLVideoElement Fullscreen APIs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The prefixed HTMLVideoElement-specific fullscreen APIs have been deprecated since Chrome 38. They were replaced by the Element.requestFullscreen() API, which first shipped un-prefixed in Chrome 71, in 2018. As of 2024, most browsers have had support for the un-prefixed APIs for a few years now.</p>

    <p>This feature tracks removing the following APIs from HTMLVideoElement:</p>

    <p>- readonly attribute boolean webkitSupportsFullscreen;</p>

    <p>- readonly attribute boolean webkitDisplayingFullscreen;</p>

    <p>- void webkitEnterFullscreen();</p>

    <p>- void webkitExitFullscreen();</p>

    <p>// Note the different capitalization of the "S" in FullScreen.</p>

    <p>- void webkitEnterFullScreen();&nbsp;</p>

    <p>- void webkitExitFullScreen();</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>These methods are now only aliases for the modern API. Their use has declined steadily over the years.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrR132" name="chromeBrsrR132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Throw exception for popovers or dialogs in non-active documents&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This is a corner case change that does not impact developers. Previously calling `showPopover()` or `showModal()` on a popover or dialog that resides within an inactive document would silently fail. This means that no exception would be thrown, but since the document is inactive, no popover or dialog would be shown. These situations now throw InvalidStateError. For more information, see the relevant <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10705" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>spec</u> </a>pull request on Github.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>

<h2>Chrome Enterprise Core changes</h2>

<p><a id="chromeECA132" name="chromeECA132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Customized Chrome Web Store for enterprises&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Admins can leverage new settings to customize the Chrome Web Store for their managed users, which includes the ability to:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Add company logos</li>
      <li>Add hero banners and custom announcements</li>
      <li>Curate extension collections</li>
      <li>Hide extension categories</li>
    </ul>

    <p>These settings are configurable via the Admin console (<a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15469659" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>learn more</u></a>) and are available to all signed-in managed users (users signed-in to the Chrome Web Store with a managed Google Account).&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Additionally, all managed users who sign in to the Chrome Web Store will see the following changes:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>New tags for items “Blocked by their admin” when searching for an item</li>
      <li>Private domain item search and advanced filtering capabilities</li>
      <li>Private items and recommended items are relocated to the “Extensions” tab&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>Enrolled browsers (without the need to sign in) will be supported later in 2025.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="466" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdmQFTXIkGL0J7pFB797sdpFGWyMCeEQyBERd9hEvDJklImhTldZ0K0d64OkIy2r841vUyrHnWrXL--6_UsvaPXayzAcTC0rrevI4Lez2BhSmT3ViUwZbE2blBjqHd9eMjdI2dLRuI?key=cjF-LTTEcICJMeqE5_7vuqd2" width="718"></p>

<p><a id="chromeECB132" name="chromeECB132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New Chrome user management capabilities in the Admin console&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Admins can now get more visibility into Chrome user profiles in their organization with a new profile list and reporting features for signed-in Google Accounts. This centralized view in the Google Admin console provides detailed reports about user profiles in your organization, including profile information, browser version, applied policies and installed extensions. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14707830" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>View Chrome browser profile details</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>To get started, IT administrators can simply turn on the new Chrome <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/2657289?hl=en#zippy=%2Cmanaged-profile-reporting" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Managed profile reporting policy</u></a> to view the reporting information about managed profiles.&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome Enterprise Premium changes</h2>
&nbsp; &nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeEPA132" name="chromeEPA132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>File download encryption for DLP Rules&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>When a file downloaded Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rule is triggered, the file is now encrypted on the fly to ensure that end users cannot access that file when a verdict is being returned. This means that users can no longer bypass the rule by moving or renaming the file.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This feature is gated by the existing policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector</u></a> and is only available to Chrome Enterprise Premium users.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome browser changes</h4>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrA132" name="upChromeBrsrA132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL hosts&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As stated in the <a href="http://whatwg.org" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WhatWG.org</u></a> spec, <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL hosts</u></a> cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host.</p>

    <p>This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 'HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a>' and URL <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>focus areas</u></a>.</p>

    <p>To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows <code>file://</code> URLs (see the discussion on <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>).</p>

    <p>This feature will be part of the ongoing work to bring Chromium closer to spec compliance by forbidding spaces for non-file URLs only.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrB132" name="upChromeBrsrB132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Read aloud in Reading mode in Chrome 133&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Reading mode is a side-panel feature that provides a simplified view of text-dense web pages. Reading mode will include a Read aloud feature which will allow users to hear the text they are reading spoken out loud. Users will be able to choose different natural voices and speeds, and see visual highlights.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrC132" name="upChromeBrsrC132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Tab freezing on Energy saver&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>When Energy saver is active, Chrome will freeze a tab that has been hidden and silent for &gt;5 minutes and uses a lot of CPU, unless:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The tab provides audio- or video- conferencing functionality (detected via microphone, camera or screen/window/tab capture, or an RTCPeerConnection with an open RTCDataChannel or a live MediaStreamTrack).</li>
      <li>The tab controls an external device (detected via usage of Web USB, Web Bluetooth, Web HID or Web Serial).</li>
    </ul>

    <p>This will extend battery life and speed up Chrome through reduced CPU usage.<br>
      The feature can be tested in Chrome 131 via c<code>hrome://flags/#freezing-on-energy-saver</code>. Alternatively, it can be tested with <code>chrome://flags/#freezing-on-energy-saver-testing</code>, which simulates Energy saver being active and all tabs using a lot of CPU; this allows you to verify whether tabs are eligible for freezing and would be frozen if using a lot of CPU.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Energy saver availability can be controlled via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BatterySaverModeAvailability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BatterySaverModeAvailability</u></a> policy (this change has no effect when Energy saver is inactive).</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        The feature will start rolling out to 1% of stable in Chrome 133.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrD132" name="upChromeBrsrD132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate getters of Intl Locale Info&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Intl Locale Info API is a Stage 3 ECMAScript <a href="https://github.com/tc39/proposal-intl-locale-info" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TC39 proposal</u></a> to enhance the Intl.Locale object by exposing Locale information, such as week data (first day in a week, weekend start day, weekend end day, minimum day in the first week), and text direction hour cycle used in the locale.</p>

    <p>We shipped our implementation in <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5566859262820352" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome 99 </u></a>&nbsp;but later on the proposal made some changes in Stage 3 and moved several getters to functions. We need to remove the deprecated getters and relaunch the renamed functions.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrE132" name="upChromeBrsrE132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Popover invoker and anchor positioning improvements&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This update represents the following related set of changes, which were <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9144#issuecomment-2195095228" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>resolved</u></a>&nbsp; and <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10728" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>landed</u></a>&nbsp;</p>

    <p>1. add an imperative way to set invoker relationships between popovers:&nbsp;</p>

    <p>&nbsp; &nbsp; <code>popover.showPopover({source})</code></p>

    <p>2. invoker relationships create implicit anchor element references.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove Chrome Welcome page triggering via initial prefs first run tabs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>For more details about the context of the initial_preferences file, see <a href="https://www.chromium.org/administrators/configuring-other-preferences" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Configuring Other Preferences</u></a>.</p>

    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
