<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrG132" name="upChromeBrsrG132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove nonstandard getUserMedia audio constraints&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Blink supports a number of nonstandard goog-prefixed constraints for getUserMedia from some time before constraints were properly standardized.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Usage has gone down significantly ~0.000001% to 0.0009% (depending on the constraint) and some of them do not even have an effect due to changes in the Chromium audio-capture stack. Soon none of them will have any effect due to other upcoming changes.</p>

    <p>We do not expect any major regressions due to this change. Applications using these constraints will continue to work, but will get audio with default settings (as if no constraints were passed). They can easily migrate to standard constraints.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH132" name="upChromeBrsrH132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove SwiftShader fallback&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Allowing automatic fallback to WebGL backed by SwiftShader is deprecated and WebGL context creation will fail instead of falling back to SwiftShader. This was done for two primary reasons:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process.</li>
      <li>Users have a poor experience when falling back from a high-performance GPU-backed WebGL to a CPU-backed implementation. Users have no control over this behavior and it is difficult to describe in bug reports.</li>
    </ol>
    &nbsp;

    <p>SwiftShader is a useful tool for web developers to test their sites on systems that are headless or do not have a supported GPU. This use case will still be supported by opting in but is not intended for running untrusted content.</p>

    <p>To opt-in to lower security guarantees and allow SwiftShader for WebGL, run the chrome executable with the --enable-unsafe-swiftshader command-line switch.</p>

    <p>During the deprecation period, a warning will appear in the JavaScript console when a WebGL context is created and backed with SwiftShader. Passing <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader </code>will remove this warning message.</p>

    <p>Chromium and other browsers do not guarantee WebGL availability. You can test and handle WebGL context creation failure and fall back to other web APIs such as Canvas2D or an appropriate message to the user.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrI132" name="upChromeBrsrI132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Privacy &amp; security panel in Chrome DevTools&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 133, developers will be able to use the new <strong>Privacy &amp; security</strong> panel in Chrome DevTools to test how their site will behave when third-party cookies are limited. Developers will be able to temporarily limit third-party cookies, observe how their site behaves, and review the status of third-party cookies on their site.</p>

    <p>This feature will not make any permanent changes to existing enterprise policies, but it will let third-party cookie related enterprise policies (that is, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BlockThirdPartyCookies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BlockThirdPartyCookies</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a>) be temporarily overridden to be more restrictive. If your enterprise policy already blocks third-party cookies using <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BlockThirdPartyCookies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BlockThirdPartyCookies</u></a>, this feature will be disabled.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>The new <strong>Privacy &amp; security</strong> panel will replace the existing <strong>Security</strong> panel. TLS connection and certificate information will continue to be available on the <strong>Security</strong> tab in the <strong>Privacy &amp; security</strong> panel.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ132" name="upChromeBrsrJ132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Sync to end support for Chrome versions more than four years old&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in February 2025, Chrome Sync (using and saving data in your Google Account) will no longer support Chrome versions that are more than four years old. You need to upgrade to a more recent version of Chrome if you want to continue using Chrome Sync.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>

    <p>This change affects only the old versions of Chrome and will be rolled out server-side. Chrome 133 is specified only to reflect the timeline when the change will make an effect.</p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK132" name="upChromeBrsrK132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>V8 Security Setting&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Add a setting on <code>chrome://settings/security </code>to disable the V8 JIT optimizers, in order to reduce the attack surface of Chrome. This maintains compatibility with Web Assembly. This behavior continues to be controlled by the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DefaultJavaScriptJitSetting" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DefaultJavaScriptJitSetting</u></a> enterprise policy, and the associated <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#JavaScriptJitAllowedForSites" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>JavaScriptJitAllowedForSites</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#JavaScriptJitBlockedForSites" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>JavaScriptJitBlockedForSites</u></a> policies.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 122 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia<br>
        The setting rolls out in Chrome 121. The enterprise policies have been available since Chrome 93.</li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android</strong><br>
        The setting is available on Android in Chrome 133, under Site Settings. The enterprise policies are no longer marked experimental.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL132" name="upChromeBrsrL132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New option in HttpsOnlyMode policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Ask Before HTTP (ABH, formerly HTTPS Only/First Modes) is a setting that tells Chrome to ask for user consent before sending insecure HTTP content over the wire. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HttpsOnlyMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HttpsOnlyMod</u></a> policy allows force-enabling, or force-disabling, ABH.</p>

    <p>In Chrome 129, we are adding a new middle-ground variant of ABH called "balanced mode". This variant aims to reduce user inconvenience by working like (strict) ABH most of the time, but not asking when Chrome knows that an HTTPS connection isn't possible (such as when connecting to a single-label hostname like internal/).</p>

    <p>We are adding a force_balanced_enabled policy option to allow force-enabling this new variant. Setting force_balanced_enabled on browsers before Chrome 129 will result in the default behavior, which places no enterprise restrictions on the ABH setting.</p>

    <p>To avoid unexpected impact, if you have previously set force_enabled, we recommend not setting force_balanced_enabled until your entire fleet has upgraded to Chrome 129 or higher. If you are not migrating from force_enabled to force_balanced_enabled, you will be unaffected by this change.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 129 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrM132" name="upChromeBrsrM132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 to v5 migration&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the v5 API instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5.</p>

    <p>If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4<u>*</u></code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead:<u> </u><code><u>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</u></code>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>This will be a gradual rollout.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrN132" name="upChromeBrsrN132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Blob URL Partitioning: Fetching or Navigation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As a continuation of Storage Partitioning, Chromium will implement partitioning of Blob URL access by Storage Key (top-level site, frame origin, and the has-cross-site-ancestor boolean), with the exception of navigations which will remain partitioned only by frame origin. This behavior is similar to what’s currently implemented by both Firefox and Safari, and aligns Blob URL usage with the partitioning scheme used by other storage APIs as part of Storage Partitioning. In addition, Chromium will enforce noopener on renderer-initiated navigations to Blob URLs where the corresponding site is cross-site to the top-level site performing the navigation. This aligns Chromium with similar behavior in Safari, and we will pursue spec updates to reflect both of these changes.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This change can be temporarily reverted by setting the <strong>PartitionedBlobURLUsage</strong> policy, which will be available in Chrome 134. The policy will be deprecated when the other storage partitioning related enterprise policies are deprecated.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrO132" name="upChromeBrsrO132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SharedWorker script inherit controller for blob script URL&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p><a href="https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#control-and-use-worker-client" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Service Workers</a>&nbsp;should inherit controllers for the blob URL. However, existing code allows only dedicated workers to inherit the controller, and shared workers do not inherit the controller.</p>

    <p>This is the fix to make Chromium behavior adjust to the specification.</p>

    <p>An enterprise policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SharedWorkerBlobURLFixEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SharedWorkerBlobURLFixEnabled</u></a> is available to control this feature.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrP132" name="upChromeBrsrP132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate mutation events&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Synchronous mutation events, including DOMSubtreeModified, DOMNodeInserted, DOMNodeRemoved, DOMNodeRemovedFromDocument, DOMNodeInsertedIntoDocument, and DOMCharacterDataModified, negatively affect page performance, and also significantly increase the complexity of adding new features to the Web. These APIs were deprecated from the spec in 2011, and were replaced (in 2012) by the much better-behaved Mutation Observer API. Usage of the obsolete mutation events must be removed or migrated to Mutation Observer. Starting in Chrome 124, a temporary enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a>, will be available to re-enable deprecated or removed mutation events. If you encounter any issues, file a bug <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Mutation event support will be disabled by default starting in Chrome 127, around July 30, 2024. Code should be migrated before that date to avoid site breakage. If more time is needed, there are a few options:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/origintrials/#/view_trial/919297273937002497" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Mutation Events Deprecation Trial</u></a> can be used to re-enable the feature for a limited time on a given site. This can be used through Chrome 134, ending March 25, 2025.</li>
      <li>A <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy can also be used for the same purpose, also through Chrome 134.</li>
    </ul>

    <p>To read more, see <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/mutation-events-deprecation" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>this</u></a> blog post. Report any issues <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy will be deprecated.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrQ132" name="upChromeBrsrQ132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome started directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Admins might use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, available from Chrome 125, to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 136, and will be removed in Chrome 137. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that admins can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise admins may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt out through Chrome 136.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrR132" name="upChromeBrsrR132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Customizing managed profiles with custom logo and label&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>New toolbar and profile menu customizations that help users easily identify if their Chrome profile is managed, whether they're on a work or personal device. This is especially useful for scenarios where employees use their own devices with managed accounts.</p>

    <p>To help tailor this experience, we're adding three new policies:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseCustomLabel" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseCustomLabel:</u></a> Customize the text displayed on the toolbar element to match your organization's branding.</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseLogoUrl" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseLogoUrl</u></a>: Add your company logo to the profile menu.</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings</u></a>: This policy can disable the default label for a managed profile in the Chrome toolbar.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>In Chrome Chrome 133, these policies will be available to customize the logo and label shown on a managed profile.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Starting Chrome 134, there will be updates to the default behavior of the profile label and icon overlaid on the account avatar. Managed profiles will show a <em>work</em> or <em>school</em> label in addition to the profile disk. In the profile menu, there will be a building icon overlaid on the account avatar. The expanded profile disk can be disabled via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings.</u></a></p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on macOS, Windows</strong>

        <p>Policies to customize the toolbar label and icon (in profile menu)&nbsp;</p>
      </li>
      <li>Chrome 134: Starting rollout of defaults including:&nbsp;
        <ul>
          <li>1) <em>work</em> or <em>school</em> label shown in toolbar, next to user avatar&nbsp;</li>
          <li>2) A building icon overlayed on the user's account photo in the profile menu. The label can be turned off via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseProfileBadgeToolbarSettings</u></a>. Starting with 1% and gradual slow rollout thereafter.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>ChromeOS updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeOSA132" name="chromeOSA132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Customized Chrome Web Store for enterprises&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Admins can now use new settings to customize the Chrome Web Store for their managed users, which includes the ability to:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Add company logos</li>
      <li>Add hero banners and custom announcements</li>
      <li>Curate extension collections</li>
      <li>Implement category-based controls</li>
    </ul>

    <p>These settings are configurable using the Admin console and are available to all signed-in managed users (users signed-in to the Chrome Web Store with a managed Google Account). For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15469659" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Customized Chrome Web Store for enterprises</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Additionally, all managed users who sign in to the Chrome Web Store will see the following changes:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>New tags for items <strong>Blocked by their admin</strong> when searching for an item</li>
      <li>Private domain item search and advanced filtering capabilities</li>
      <li>Private items and recommended items are relocated to the <strong>Extensions</strong> tab&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>Enrolled browsers (without the need to sign in) will be supported later in 2025.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="479" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfE1U3DOs4wa2zhG1Vguzy46hY-n5NWjHUfoaKZECYRZ7qySx5ue1g5sMYv7UezfyJEhBvzLB3fERrgRydONDM_IYUEkXhBG77u3hiCcvFjGcpQydUZGG3K7R3P0WAr5KAtQgT80oE?key=4pG9fAXgc_DJnFz3w-3V7kn4" width="737"></p>
    <br>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB132" name="chromeOSB132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Native Client (NaCl) support ending on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 132 is the last release with NaCl support for unmanaged or consumer devices, followed by ChromeOS 138 in <strong>July 2025</strong> for managed devices. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1289314?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>About ChromeOS device management</u></a>.</p>

    <p>In 2017, we announced the end of support of <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Native Client (NaCl)</u></a> in favor of <a href="https://webassembly.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly</u></a>. With most developers and users having migrated away from NaCl, we confirm the following NaCl discontinuation dates:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>January 2025:</strong> Native Client (NaCl) will be disabled from ChromeOS 132 onwards.

        <ul>
          <li>For unmanaged and consumer users, ChromeOS 132 will be the last ChromeOS release with support for NaCl.</li>
          <li>For managed environments (including Kiosk sessions), administrators who manage ChromeOS devices for a business or school will have the option of extending the ability to use NaCl with a <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DeviceNativeClientForceAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DeviceNativeClientForceAllowed</u></a> NaCl allow policy through the ChromeOS 138 release. To enable device policies, please refer to <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1375678#zippy=%2Cnative-client-nacl" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Set ChromeOS device policies</u></a> in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li><strong>July 2025:</strong> ChromeOS 138 will be the last version with NaCl support.
        <ul>
          <li>For managed environments, ChromeOS 138 is a <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11333726?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Long-term Support (LTS)</u></a> ChromeOS release available to administrators who manage ChromeOS devices for a business or school.&nbsp;</li>
          <li>For devices that have been <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/3168106?hl=en#zippy=%2Cpin-chromeos-updates-to-a-specific-version" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>switched to the LTS channel</u></a> and have the NaCl allow policy enabled, NaCl will be available until LTS Last Refresh in <strong>April 2026</strong>.</li>
          <li><strong>No exceptions will be granted.</strong></li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>For Chrome Apps that use NaCl, migrate to <a href="https://webassembly.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly</u></a> (WASM). To help you with the transition, we've published the <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client/migration" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly Migration Guide</u></a>.</p>

    <p>For more information about this change or if you need assistance, you can refer to any of the following:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client/migration" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly Migration Guide</u></a>.</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/join-us-in-the-chromeos-developer-community-on-discord" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS developer community on Discord</u></a>.</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS release schedule</u></a> for release dates and updates.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>To find out more, see&nbsp;<a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/topic/6274424?hl=en&amp;ref_topic=4386913&amp;sjid=10808321024100605256-NC" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Manage policies for ChromeOS devices</u></a> in the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center.</p>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSC132" name="chromeOSC132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Onboarding refresh&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>There are many different setup items that users might look to change once they've started using their devices, including setting up a printer, connecting Bluetooth devices, changing touchpad direction, and so on. This feature consolidates many of these common setup items into a simple task list, with deep linking to where a user can change a particular setting, to simplify the process of completing many of these steps.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="448" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdtCI7qmrDVHYOPXqpj2cAOxJqgsDx7vNRVi7hJJClTDt-3wGw9UUoXaHHaMrOQWFntbVtXTH_ga5ABaXe2UOj6CnsOrFuFLhOn7o-G6eefzhCc2X_6y0wU26G7lFK2bY3ak7QOxME?key=4pG9fAXgc_DJnFz3w-3V7kn4" width="635"></p>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSD132" name="chromeOSD132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Migrate data for graduating students&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 132, a new Content transfer tool will guide graduating students or other EDU-managed users who want to migrate their data through the updated Google Takeout Transfer process. This allows them to take their Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Gmail content to a Gmail account of their choice.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This new application allows school administrators to pin an icon to the shelf, notify students and faculty on their Chromebooks, and set dates to trigger these nudges to encourage them to use Content transfer.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSE132" name="chromeOSE132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Rounded corners for Apps&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>As part of a new UI design, ChromeOS now features rounded corners on all app windows on Chromebook Plus devices.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSF132" name="chromeOSF132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS passwordless authentication&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>The passwordless ChromeOS feature allows users to access their device with PIN or a local password as their primary authentication factor. This means that you will be able to log in to your ChromeOS device with a password you set explicitly for your device, as well as with a PIN no longer tying your gmail password with your device password.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>It is not possible to enable the PIN feature on managed devices.&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSG132" name="chromeOSG132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Face control on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS now features AI-powered face control; you can now use face and gesture tracking to navigate your Chromebook, open apps, and even compose emails – all without a keyboard or mouse. This built-in technology, inspired by <a href="https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-project-gameface/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Project Gameface</u></a>, provides greater accessibility for users with motor disabilities and offers a more efficient way for everyone to interact with their devices. To read more about this feature, see this Google <a href="https://blog.google/outreach-initiatives/accessibility/face-control-chromeos/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>blog post</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSH132" name="chromeOSH132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Turn off the touchpad&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Chromebook users can now disable their touchpads. This accessibility improvement helps those who rely on screen readers or may experience accidental clicks. To turn it off, go to <strong>Settings &gt; Accessibility &gt; Cursor and Touchpad</strong>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSI132" name="chromeOSI132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Password Manager biometric authentication&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 132 enables biometrics in Password Manager and autofill on Chrome for ChromeOS devices.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="269" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfXaPE9TdViIaXm3wgPoFjuWN4ooaWBNX9jJzKXZuGfZwimC09fq4HI3nsP8QrFCy8HXpSq3PW1TdjD5NZ40o8-JNR3cZ1oyXkpQhDAKXZZEPEZ_n_ixZZ9FebXOTXMwOk_2_mA8A?key=4pG9fAXgc_DJnFz3w-3V7kn4" width="271"></p>
    <br>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSJ132" name="chromeOSJ132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Apps discovery removed from Explore&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 132 removes the Apps &amp; Games module in the Explore app. To discover new apps for your ChromeOS device, navigate to <a href="https://discover.apps.chrome" rel="noopener" target="_blank">https://discover.apps.chrome</a>.</p>

    <p><img height="446" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeLDLBO-B2o31UOfLC6ygJpl3awY6f1EgprkY4cyJL_ZDjKYWf2q_VEtHacK9YK_Q7W84Y2CtK8Pg-QrgN7Z70_LYBlW7R5ZqBSeFYUD6Kk7iBxlz6INc5r7DOww1fBIH_-Gl4MRz0?key=4pG9fAXgc_DJnFz3w-3V7kn4" width="784">.</p>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSK132" name="chromeOSK132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Remote management for idle devices&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Chrome Remote Desktop (CRD) is a feature that allows for remote control of ChromeOS devices, primarily for troubleshooting purposes, where a device is idle and unused. Admins can now initiate a CRD connection to a ChromeOS device sitting on the login screen. This enables an admin to sign-in to a managed device with their own set of credentials for troubleshooting or testing.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="375" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXex5ypzVyXlTdaHaz2EIWhSBuwRUnBBB3m__-297uxFWnGOBHpPuQNgxhGVSouXhWcUAgeKYu3_JSX729I9l-0Zkg_mg5t5XO_uLZ6gXddXl1vrejrQHP8Aeu2CeNyyWstL2esIsA?key=4pG9fAXgc_DJnFz3w-3V7kn4" width="523"></p>
    &nbsp; &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSL132" name="chromeOSL132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS device Bedtime Hours policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a> &nbsp;</p>

    <p>The new <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DeviceRestrictionSchedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DeviceRestrictionSchedule</u></a><strong> </strong>policy allows ChromeOS administrators to disallow users from logging in to specified Chromebooks during certain hours on specified days of the week. During these hours, kiosk apps are also unavailable.&nbsp;</p>

    <p><img height="349" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe8MI-nR0hbVTiARv7WLsEFi1oA-Tsio2ksFanf2hMY1cEfciFZ8qGVjDZPwPu_w-UH4xeQvOMq-QuUZTwVOh7y5Dzej8IaL7a9ffwU1KiI4BVHpcs4ncKck4w2xRjAfdg9b2fMzZc?key=4pG9fAXgc_DJnFz3w-3V7kn4" width="624"></p>
    <br>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSM132" name="chromeOSM132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Improved management disclosure on locked device&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>This feature improves the management disclosure on the device's lock screen. To enhance user understanding before using their device for personal tasks or work, we provide a clear explanation of what managed devices entail. This way, users can make informed decisions regarding their device usage. By providing necessary information, users gain the knowledge needed to make choices that align with their privacy and security concerns and preferences.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA132" name="upChromeOSA132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>AI wallpapers and backgrounds&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 134, we plan to introduce high-resolution, generative AI wallpapers and video call backgrounds on ChromeOS. With this feature, you can unleash your creativity and turn your Chromebook into a canvas of personal expression. Choose from a diverse collection of templates and, in just a few clicks, infuse your Chromebook with your unique personality, mood, or interest.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Two new policies will be available to control these features; <strong>GenAIVcBackgroundSettings</strong> and <strong>GenAIWallpaperSettings</strong>. This feature will be available on <a href="https://www.google.com/chromebook/discover/chromebookplus/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromebook Plus devices</u></a> only.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB132" name="upChromeOSB132"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Deprecating Chrome Apps support&nbsp;on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In 2016, we announced the deprecation of Chrome Apps in favor of web apps, and in 2021, we <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2021/10/extending-chrome-app-support-on-chrome.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>announced on the Chromium Blog</u></a> that support for Chrome Apps for ChromeOS Enterprise and Education customers and developers on ChromeOS would be extended until at least January 2025. With the majority of our customers having migrated off of Chrome Apps (including <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#packaged-app-legacy" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Legacy (v1) packaged apps</u></a> and <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#hosted-app" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Hosted apps</u></a>), we can confirm the following updates about Chrome Apps discontinuation dates.</p>

    <p>&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>July 2025: End of support for user-installed Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M138).</strong>

        <ul>
          <li>Chrome Apps that are force-installed through the admin console will continue to be supported.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>July 2026: Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode (scheduled for ChromeOS M150).
        <ul>
          <li>Devices on the LTS channel with Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode will receive support until April 2027.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>February 2028: Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M168), marking the end of life for all Chrome Apps.
        <ul>
          <li>Devices on the LTS channel can continue to use Chrome Apps until October 2028.</li>
          <li>No exceptions will be granted.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <p>These deprecation timelines also apply to self-hosted Chrome Apps.</p>

    <p>While no new Chrome Apps can be added to the Chrome Web Store, existing Chrome Apps can continue to be updated through October 2028 when they will reach end of life on ChromeOS. After this date, Chrome Apps will be removed from the Chrome Web Store.</p>

    <p>If your organization has developed in-house Chrome Apps and you need assistance, please refer to <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/apps/migration/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Transition from Chrome Apps</u></a> guide. You can also join us in the <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/join-us-in-the-chromeos-developer-community-on-discord" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS developer community on Discord</u></a>, or reach out to us through the form at <a href="https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us" rel="noopener" target="_blank">https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us</a>. Refer to the <a href="https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS release schedule</u></a> for release dates and updates.</p>

    <p>In the coming weeks, additional detailed information will be sent to all remaining Chrome App developers and all ChromeOS Administrators.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes</h2>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA131" name="chromeBrsrA131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Search with Google Lens on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Since Chrome 126, users can search any images or text they see on their screen with Google Lens. To use this feature, go to a website and click <strong>Search with Google Lens</strong> on the on-focus omnibox chip and on the right-click menus on desktop, or on the 3-dot menu on both desktop and mobile. Users can click, highlight, or drag anywhere on the screen to search its contents, and refine their search by adding keywords or questions to the search box. Admins can control the feature through a policy called <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LensOverlaySettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LensOverlaySettings</u></a>. To perform the search, a screenshot of the screen is sent to Google servers but it is not linked to any IDs or accounts, it is not viewed by any human, and data about its contents is not logged. We are starting the rollout of this feature gradually on iOS in Chrome 131 and we plan to launch fully in Chrome 132.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 126 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout of the feature at 1% Stable</li>
      <li>Chrome 127 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Rollout to 100% Stable</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on iOS:</strong> Rollout of the feature starts</li>
      <li>Chrome 132 on iOS: Rollout to 100% Stable</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB131" name="chromeBrsrB131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Asynchronous real-time Safe Browsing check on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Today Safe Browsing checks are on the blocking path of page loads, meaning that the user cannot see the page until the checks are completed. To improve Chrome's loading speed, real-time Safe Browsing checks will no longer block page loads after Chrome 122, and after Chrome 131 on iOS.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>We have evaluated the risk and put mitigations in place:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>For malware and 0-day attacks, local-blocklist checks will still be conducted in synchronous manner so that malicious payloads are still blocked by Safe Browsing.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>For phishing attacks, we've looked at data and it is unlikely the user would have interacted with the page (for example, typed a password) by the time we show the warning.</li>
    </ol>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 122 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on iOS</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC131" name="chromeBrsrC131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Ad-hoc code signatures for PWA shims on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Code signatures for the application shims that are created when installing a Progressive Web App (PWA) on macOS are changing to use ad-hoc code signatures that are created when the application is installed. The code signature is used by macOS as part of the application's identity. These ad-hoc signatures result in each PWA app shim having a unique identity to macOS; currently every PWA looks like the same application to macOS.</p>

    <p>This addresses problems when attempting to include multiple PWAs in the macOS <strong>Open at Login</strong> preference pane, and permits future improvements to handling of user notifications within PWAs on macOS.</p>

    <p>Administrators should test for compatibility with any endpoint security or binary authorization tools they use (such as <a href="https://santa.dev/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Santa</u></a>). The feature can be switched on for testing using the <code>chrome://flags/#use-adhoc-signing-for-web-app-shims</code> flag. Admins can then install a PWA and ensure that it launches as expected.</p>

    <p>If there is an incompatibility between the feature and their current security policies, the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AdHocCodeSigningForPWAsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank">AdHocCodeSigningForPWAsEnabled</a>&nbsp;policy can be used to disable the feature while they deploy an updated endpoint security policy. The enterprise policy is intended to be used to disable the feature only until endpoint security policies have been updated, at which point it should be unset.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 129 on macOS<br>
        This feature is turned on with a flag (<code>chrome://flags/#use-adhoc-signing-for-web-app-shims</code>) so that enterprises can test for compatibility with their endpoint security tools, such as <a href="https://santa.dev/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Santa</u></a>. If it is not currently compatible, they can control the feature using the enterprise policy while they update their endpoint security configurations. The enterprise policy is intended to be used to disable the feature only until endpoint security policies have been updated.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on macOS</strong>: Feature begins to roll out to stable, starting at 1% rollout.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD131" name="chromeBrsrD131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Choose from Google Drive&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>From Chrome 131 onwards, Chrome on iOS users can upload a file from Google Drive directly to a web page, without the need to download it on the device first.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on iOS</strong>: Includes core functionality for uploading a single file.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE131" name="chromeBrsrE131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome PDF Viewer OCR&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Chrome Desktop now makes scanned PDFs more accessible. Using on-device Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to maintain privacy (no content is sent to Google), Chrome automatically converts scanned PDFs, allowing you to select text, Ctrl+F, copy, and paste. The feature does not bypass secure PDFs. It only uses OCR on PDFs the user has access to. The solution unlocks PDF accessibility to Chrome users without any extra steps, making PDFs as accessible as the rest of the web.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrF131" name="chromeBrsrF131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome on iOS promo on Desktop NTP&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>A Chrome on iOS promo on the Desktop new tab page. This promo aims to increase awareness of Chrome on iOS and present a simple way to install.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>You can control this feature using the existing policies <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PromotionsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank">PromotionsEnabled</a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#NTPMiddleSlotAnnouncementVisible" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>NTPMiddleSlotAnnouncementVisible</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrG131" name="chromeBrsrG131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Cross profile password-reuse detection&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Previously, password-reuse detection of corporate credentials was only detectable in the corporate profile. Now, password-reuse detection detects corporate credential reuse across all non-Incognito profiles on the managed browser.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>We've updated the cross profile password-reuse detection criteria to more accurately reflect managed enterprise accounts. We’ve also updated the on-screen message to make it clearer to users that their organization is monitoring their corporate password reuse.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 123 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong><br>
        We've updated the cross profile password-reuse detection criteria to more accurately reflect managed enterprise accounts, and updated the UX message to make it clearer to users that their organization is monitoring their corporate password reuse.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
&nbsp;

<p><a id="chromandroid131" name="chromandroid131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome on Android now supports 3P autofill and password providers</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Until now, third-party autofill and password providers could be used in Chrome on Android via accessibility APIs.</p>

    <p>In Chrome M131, we're adding direct support for Android Autofill, which means these providers will work with Chrome on Android without the need for accessibility APIs. This should improve the performance of Chrome on Android and third-party autofill providers.</p>

    <p>To take advantage of this, users will need to configure their third-party provider&nbsp;in Android settings. Then, in Chrome,&nbsp;users select&nbsp;<strong>Settings &gt; Autofill services</strong> and choose <strong>Autofill using another service</strong>.</p>

    <p>If users do not change both settings, they will continue to use Google to autofill their passwords, payment and address information. Whether users can use a third-party autofill service or not can be controlled by a new policy called <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyPasswordManagersAllowed" rel="noopener" target="_blank">ThirdPartyPasswordManagersAllowed</a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Android&nbsp;</strong>

        <p>The new setting will be available from Chrome 131. If users use the new setting, it will take immediate effect. If the new setting is not used, users will continue to use either Google or a third party via accessibility (if installed).&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

        <p>The support for accessibility APIs will be deprecated in early 2025, at which point the new policy settings will apply to all users.</p>
        &nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrH131" name="chromeBrsrH131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate Safe Browsing Extended reporting&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>We are deprecating the Safe Browsing Extended reporting feature, which previously&nbsp; enhanced the security of all users by collecting telemetry information from participating users that is used for Google Safe Browsing protections. The data collected includes URLs of visited web pages, limited system information, and some page content.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This feature is now superseded by <strong>Enhanced protection mode</strong>. We suggest users switch to Enhanced protection to continue providing security for all users in addition to enabling the strongest security available in Chrome. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/9890866?visit_id=638471471514766310-2859664582&amp;p=safe_browsing_preferences&amp;rd=1" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Safe Browsing protection levels</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 129 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows<br>
        Deprecation of Safe Browsing Extended Reporting. Excluding real-time Client Safe Browsing Report Request</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        Deprecating <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SafeBrowsingExtendedReportingEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsingExtendedReportingEnabled</u></a> for real-time Client Safe Browsing Report Request</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img height="468" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcZUm-6QtoUVLPX2vd5OvjcixI6VcEOn185Yv2Vym2PwpRu5-WuSnh6R4myoMF71aeg6Ge4FTDcWjDD12KaO5I84lAs7jLnFejhTvPvWAkck3eXwJVAfGHkuFamnakkFOHOc9mKTt_UJ4GWVdox4locrt8FTWnv3lzW8Ns0uvGWoZUh65RtylIPw-9fpjN2Sw?key=kmYteZEE33m7yyUOicMnwA" width="359"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrI131" name="chromeBrsrI131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Entrust certificate distrust&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>In response to sustained compliance failures, Chrome is changing how publicly-trusted TLS server authentication (website) certificates issued by Entrust will be trusted by default in Chrome 131 and greater on Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, and Linux. iOS policies do not allow use of the Chrome Root Store in Chrome for iOS.</p>

    <p>Specifically, TLS certificates validating to the Entrust root CA certificates included in the Chrome Root Store and issued:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>after November 11, 2024, will no longer be trusted by default.</li>
      <li>on or before November 11, 2024, will be unaffected by this change.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>Should a Chrome user or enterprise explicitly trust any of the affected Entrust certificates on a platform and version of Chrome relying on the Chrome Root Store, for example, explicit trust is conveyed through a Windows Group Policy Object, the SCT-based constraints described above will be overridden and certificates will function as they do today.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Additional information and testing resources are <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2024/06/sustaining-digital-certificate-security.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>the Google Security blog</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>To learn more, see this FAQ about the <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/net/data/ssl/chrome_root_store/faq.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Root Store</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        All versions of Chrome 131 and higher that rely on the Chrome Root Store will honor the blocking action, but the blocking action will only begin for certificates issued after November 11, 2024.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrJ131" name="chromeBrsrJ131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Insecure form warnings on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Since Chrome 125, Chrome browser blocks form submissions from secure pages to insecure pages on iOS. When Chrome detects an insecure form submission, it displays a warning asking the user to confirm the submission. The goal is to prevent leaking form data over plain text without the user's explicit approval. A policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecureFormsWarningsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecureFormsWarningsEnabled</u></a> is available to control this feature.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on iOS: Feature rolls out</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on iOS</strong>: InsecureFormsWarningsEnabled policy will be removed</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrR131" name="chromeBrsrR131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>PartitionAlloc with Advanced Checks (PA/AC)&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>PartitionAlloc (PA) and its associated memory security projects have an array of advanced safeguards that are deactivated by default (or exclusively in debug builds) due to their potential impact on performance. While enabling the feature for all users might not be immediately possible, there is still an opportunity to partially enable it under specific, limited conditions.</p>

    <p>This project seeks to achieve advanced safeguards for the enterprise customers. Enterprise administrators have the option to apply enhanced security measures through enterprise policies. Security tends to be prioritized over performance in enterprise. There's a likelihood that they desire advanced checks, even if it comes at a cost to performance.</p>

    <p><em>PA with Advanced Checks</em> is advanced memory security. The feature is OFF by default due to expected performance regression. Enterprise customers have an option to enable it to achieve advanced security via enterprise policy.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrK131" name="chromeBrsrK131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Simplified sign-in and sync experience&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 131, existing users with Chrome sync turned on now experience a simplified and consolidated version of sign-in and sync in Chrome. Chrome sync is no longer shown as a separate feature in settings or elsewhere. Instead, users can sign in to Chrome to use and save information like passwords, bookmarks and more in their Google Account, subject to the relevant enterprise policies.</p>

    <p>As before, the functionality previously part of Chrome sync that saves and accesses Chrome data in the Google Account can be controlled by <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a>. Sign-in to Chrome can be switched off via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a> as before.</p>

    <p>Note that the changes do not affect users’ ability to sign in to Google services on the web (like Gmail) without signing in to Chrome, their ability to stay signed out of Chrome, or their ability to control what information is synced with their Google Account.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrLL131" name="chromeBrsrLL131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Tab freezing on Energy saver&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>When Energy saver is active, Chrome freezes a tab that has been hidden and silent for &gt;5 minutes and uses a lot of CPU, unless:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The tab provides audio- or video- conferencing functionality, detected via microphone, camera or screen, window, or tab capture, or an RTCPeerConnection with an open RTCDataChannel or a live MediaStreamTrack.</li>
      <li>The tab controls an external device, detected via usage of Web USB, Web Bluetooth, Web HID or Web Serial.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>This extends battery life and speeds up Chrome through reduced CPU usage.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 130 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows<br>
        The feature can be tested in Chrome 130 using the <code>#freezing-on-energy-saver</code> entry in <code>about:flags</code>. Alternatively, it can be tested with the <code>#freezing-on-energy-saver-testing</code> flag, which simulates that Energy saver is active and that all tabs use a lot of CPU; this allows verifying whether a tab is eligible for freezing and would be frozen if it used a lot of CPU. Energy saver availability can be controlled using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BatterySaverModeAvailability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BatterySaverModeAvailability</u></a> policy. This change has no effect when Energy save is inactive.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        The feature will start rolling out to 1% of stable in Chrome 131. It will gradually be ramped up to 100% of Stable. Energy saver availability can be controlled via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BatterySaverModeAvailability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BatterySaverModeAvailability</u></a> policy. This change has no effect when Energy saver is inactive.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrN131" name="chromeBrsrN131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Update Google Play Services to fix issues with on-device passwords&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrO131" name="chromeBrsrO131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>X25519Kyber768 key encapsulation for TLS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 124, Chrome enables by default on all desktop platforms a new post-quantum secure TLS key encapsulation mechanism X25519Kyber768, based on a NIST standard (ML-KEM). This protects network traffic from Chrome with servers that also support ML-KEM from decryption by a future quantum computer. This change should be transparent to server operators. This cipher will be used for both TLS 1.3 and QUIC connections.</p>

    <p>However, some TLS middleboxes might be unprepared for the size of a Kyber (ML-KEM) key encapsulation, or a new TLS ClientHello cipher code point, leading to dropped or hanging connections. This can be resolved by updating your middlebox, or disabling the key encapsulation mechanism via the temporary <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, which will be available through the end of 2024. However, long term, post-quantum secure ciphers will be required in TLS and the enterprise policy will be removed. Post-quantum cryptography is required for CSNA 2.0.</p>

    <p>For more detail, see this <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2023/08/protecting-chrome-traffic-with-hybrid.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium blog</u></a> post and this <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2024/08/post-quantum-cryptography-standards.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Google Security blog</u></a> post.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 124 on Windows, macOS, Linux: new post-quantum secure TLS key encapsulation mechanism X25519Kyber768 is enabled</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong>: Chrome will switch the key encapsulation mechanism to the final standard version of ML-KEM</li>
      <li>Chrome 141 on Windows, macOS, Linux: Remove enterprise policy</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrP131" name="chromeBrsrP131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecation of CSS Anchor Positioning property </strong><strong><em>inset-area</em>&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>The <a href="https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/css/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSS working group</u></a> (CSSWG) resolved to rename the inset-area property to position-area. For more details, see the CSSWG discussion on <a href="https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/10209#issuecomment-2221005001"><u>github</u></a>. The new property name, position-area, as a synonym for inset-area shipped via this feature update described on <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/6567965055778816" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Platform Status</u></a>, describing the deprecation and removal of the inset-area property.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>

  <li><strong>Support non-special scheme URLs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Chrome 130 supports <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">non-special scheme URLs</a>, for example, <a href="http://example.com/path" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>git://example.com/path</u></a>. Previously, the Chromium URL parser didn't support non-special URLs. The parser parses non-special URLs as if they had an opaque path, which is not aligned with the URL standard. Now, the Chromium URL parser parses non-special URLs correctly, following the URL standard. For more details, see <a href="http://bit.ly/url-non-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">http://bit.ly/url-non-special</a>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

      <li>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</li>

<h2>Chrome Enterprise Core changes</h2>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="chromeECA131" name="chromeECA131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>GenAI Defaults policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in 131, Chrome Enterprise Core&nbsp; introduces a policy,&nbsp; <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAiDefaultSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAiDefaultSettings</u></a>, to control the default behavior of multiple GenAI policies as part of our Trusted Tester program. You can sign up for our Trusted Tester program <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/engage/trusted-testers/sign-up/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>. This policy does not impact any manually-set policy values for generative AI features. This policy controls the default settings for the following policies:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CreateThemesSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CreateThemesSettings</u></a>&nbsp;</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DevToolsGenAiSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DevToolsGenAiSettings</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HelpMeWriteSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HelpMeWriteSettings</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HistorySearchSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HistorySearchSettings</u></a>&nbsp;</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TabOrganizerSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TabOrganizerSettings</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TabCompareSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TabCompareSettings</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAIVcBackgroundSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAIVcBackgroundSettings</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GenAIWallpaperSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GenAIWallpaperSettings</u></a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HelpMeReadSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HelpMeReadSettings</u></a></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>For more details about the default settings, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14443058?hl=en&amp;ref_topic=14443801&amp;sjid=17259358006575789407-NA" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Chrome—Generative AI features and policies</a>.</p>

    <ul>

  <li><strong>Enterprise policy to force adaptive buffering for WebAudio rendering&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Chromium's WebAudio implementation includes an adaptive buffering mechanism, which was added to resolve numerous glitching issues especially on Android with the AAudio backend. While this mechanism reduced glitches significantly, it also increased audio latency. Chrome is running an experiment that will disable the adaptive buffering mechanism and run the rendering synchronously on all platforms besides Android.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Starting Chrome 131, an enterprise policy,&nbsp;<strong>WebAudioOutputBufferingEnabled,</strong> is available that will force Chrome to default to the previous behavior of using adaptive buffering for WebAudio rendering.</p>

  <li><strong>Read aloud in Reading mode in Chrome 132&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

Reading mode will include a Read aloud feature which allows users to hear the text they are reading spoken out loud. Users can choose different natural voices and speeds, and see visual highlights.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Removal of old Headless from the Chrome binary&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Running Chrome with <code>`--headless=old`</code> no longer launches the old Headless mode, and instead prints the following log message:</p>

    <p>The old Headless mode has been removed from the Chrome binary. You can use the new <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/chromium/new-headless" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Headless mode </u></a>&nbsp;or the <code>chrome-headless-shell,</code> which is a standalone implementation of the <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-headless-shell" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>old Headless mode</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><span id="cke_bm_103915S">&nbsp;</span>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrD131" name="upChromeBrsrD131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Capture all screens&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature captures all the screens currently connected to the device using <code>getAllScreensMedia()</code>. Calling <code>getDisplayMedia()</code> multiple times requires multiple user gestures, burdens the user with choosing the next screen each time, and does not guarantee to the app that all the screens were selected. <code>getAllScreensMedia()</code> improves on all of these fronts.</p>

    <p>This feature is only exposed behind the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MultiScreenCaptureAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MultiScreenCaptureAllowedForUrls</u></a> enterprise policy, and users are warned before recording even starts, that recording <em>could</em> start at some point. The API will only work for origins that are specified in the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MultiScreenCaptureAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MultiScreenCaptureAllowedForUrls</u></a> allowlist. Any origin not specified there, will not have access to it.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH131" name="upChromeBrsrH131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove prefixed HTMLVideoElement fullscreen APIs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The prefixed HTMLVideoElement-specific fullscreen APIs have been deprecated since approximately M38. They were replaced by the <code>Element.requestFullscreen() </code>API, which first shipped un-prefixed in M71, in 2018. As of 2024, most browsers have had support for the un-prefixed APIs for a few years now.</p>

    <p>This feature tracks removing the following APIs from <code>HTMLVideoElement</code>:</p>

    <p>- readonly attribute boolean <code>webkitSupportsFullscreen</code>;</p>

    <p>- readonly attribute boolean <code>webkitDisplayingFullscreen</code>;</p>

    <p>- void <code>webkitEnterFullscreen</code>();</p>

    <p>- void <code>webkitExitFullscreen</code>();</p>

    <p>// Note the different capitalization of the "S" in FullScreen.</p>

    <p>- void <code>webkitEnterFullScreen</code>();&nbsp;</p>

    <p>- void <code>webkitExitFullScreen</code>();</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>These methods are now only aliases for the modern API. Their use has declined steadily over the years.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrI131" name="upChromeBrsrI131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

    <p>Due to unexpected issues, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled</u></a> will be removed in Chrome 135. If you have feedback about this removal, please file a bug <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/u/1/issues/377321453" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows:</strong> Deprecation of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled</u></a> policy</li>
      <li>Chrome 135 on Windows: Removal of <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ThirdPartyBlockingEnabled</u></a> policy</li>
