<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK131" name="upChromeBrsrK131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Keyboard-focusable scroll containers&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>We plan to improve accessibility by making scroll containers focusable using sequential focus navigation. Today, the tab key doesn't focus scrollers unless tabIndex is explicitly set to 0 or more.</p>

    <p>By making scrollers focusable by default, users who can't (or don't want to) use a mouse will be able to focus clipped content using their tab and arrow keys. This behavior is enabled only if the scroller does not contain any keyboard focusable children. This logic is necessary so we don't cause regressions for existing focusable elements that might exist within a scroller like a <code>&lt;textarea&gt;</code>.</p>

    <p>Note: The previous rollout of this feature (started in Chrome 127)&nbsp; was stopped due to web compatibility issues, which should be fixed in the current implementation shipping in 130.</p>

    <p><strong>Note:</strong> The previous rollout of this feature (started in 130) was stopped due to an accessibility regression, which should be fixed in the implementation shipping in 132.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL131" name="upChromeBrsrL131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Throw exception for popovers or dialogs in non-active documents&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This is a corner case change that hopefully does not impact developers. A corner case is where multiple unique conditions occur simultaneously. Previously, calling `<code>showPopover()</code>` or `<code>showModal()</code>` on a popover or dialog that resides within an inactive document would silently fail, that is, no exception would be thrown. Since the document is inactive, however, no popover or dialog would be shown. As of the <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10705" rel="noopener" target="_blank">https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10705</a> spec pull request (PR), these situations now throw the <code>InvalidStateError</code> exception.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrN131" name="upChromeBrsrN131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>User Link capturing on PWAs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Web links automatically direct users to installed web apps. To better align with users' expectations around installed web apps, Chrome makes it easier to move between the browser and installed web apps. When the user clicks a link that could be handled by an installed web app, Chrome adds a chip in the address bar to suggest switching over to the app. When the user clicks the chip, this either launches the app directly, or opens a grid of apps that can support that link. For some users, clicking a link always automatically opens the app.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 121 on Linux, macOS, Windows<br>
        When some users click a link, it always opens in an installed PWA, while some users see the link open in a new tab with a chip in the address bar, clicking on which will launch the app. A flag is available to control this feature: <code>chrome://flags/#enable-user-link-capturing-pwa</code>.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        Launch to 100% of Stable with either a default on (always launch apps on link clicks) or a default off (always open in a tab, only launch if the user clicks on chip on address bar).</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><strong><img height="340" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf-LwOs2Qi88JZIOv7RbHJegfckUnKH1a6shVA6YNQADPrM5NwTcKr6FAfoh_fB1LADOtklQpW8BgfCRXSJ-COKAzfYGv9Y50TXTjguP8wBaj3Dm5fqf3uNapgXx6vAf8_fxtyCKs7UMM561NiQFpgh7jcbvbaSaE48rdQWs8q30oSNJhin2yvkfTKFMWg5eb8?key=kmYteZEE33m7yyUOicMnwA" width="597"></strong></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrO131" name="upChromeBrsrO131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Network Service on Windows will be sandboxed&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>To improve security and reliability, the network service, already running in its own process, will be sandboxed on Windows. As part of this, third-party code that is currently able to tamper with the network service may be prevented from doing so. This might cause interoperability issues with software that injects code into Chrome's process space, such as Data Loss Prevention software. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#NetworkServiceSandboxEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>NetworkServiceSandboxEnabled</u></a> policy allows you to disable the sandbox if incompatibilities are discovered. You can test the sandbox in your environment using these <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Bk3Z8CUQucd8FP6ISKkT3Q9YYuP43574VIO_kyAISBU/view#heading=h.llygd223jffh" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>instructions</u></a>.</p>

    <p>You can report any <a href="https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/entry?template=Enterprise+Issue&amp;summary=Network+Sandbox+Issue+:&amp;comment=Chrome" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>issues you encounter</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows</strong><br>
        Network Service sandboxed on Windows</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrC131" name="upChromeBrsrC131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove SwiftShader fallback&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Allowing automatic fallback to WebGL backed by SwiftShader is deprecated and WebGL context creation will fail instead of falling back to SwiftShader. This was done for two primary reasons:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>SwiftShader is a high security risk due to JIT-ed code running in Chromium's GPU process.</li>
      <li>Users have a poor experience when falling back from a high-performance GPU-backed WebGL to a CPU-backed implementation. Users have no control over this behavior and it is difficult to describe in bug reports.</li>
    </ol>
    &nbsp;

    <p>SwiftShader is a useful tool for web developers to test their sites on systems that are headless or do not have a supported GPU. This use case will still be supported by opting in but is not intended for running untrusted content.</p>

    <p>To opt in to lower security guarantees and allow SwiftShader for WebGL, run the chrome executable with the <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader</code> command-line switch.</p>

    <p>During the deprecation period, a warning will appear in the JavaScript console when a WebGL context is created and backed with SwiftShader. Passing <code>--enable-unsafe-swiftshader </code>will remove this warning message.</p>

    <p>Chromium and other browsers do not guarantee WebGL availability. You can test and handle WebGL context creation failure and fall back to other web APIs such as Canvas2D or an appropriate message to the user.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrWW131" name="chromeBrsrWW131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Privacy &amp; security panel in Chrome DevTools&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 133, developers will be able to use the new <strong>Privacy &amp; security</strong>&nbsp;panel in Chrome DevTools to test how their site will behave when third-party cookies are limited. Developers will be able to temporarily limit third-party cookies, observe how their site behaves, and review the status of third-party cookies on their site.</p>

    <p>This feature will not make any permanent changes to existing enterprise policies, but it will let third-party cookie related enterprise policies (that is,&nbsp;<a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BlockThirdPartyCookies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BlockThirdPartyCookies</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a>) be temporarily overridden to be more restrictive. If your enterprise policy already blocks third-party cookies using <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BlockThirdPartyCookies" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BlockThirdPartyCookies</u></a>, this feature will be disabled.</p>

    <p>The new <strong>Privacy &amp; security </strong>panel will replace the existing Security&nbsp;panel. TLS connection and certificate information will continue to be available on the <strong>Security</strong> tab in the <strong>Privacy &amp; security</strong>&nbsp;panel.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeBrsrE131" name="upChromeBrsrE131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Sync to end support for Chrome versions more than four years old&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in February 2025, Chrome Sync (using and saving data in your Google Account) will no longer support Chrome versions that are more than four years old. You need to upgrade to a more recent version of Chrome if you want to continue using Chrome Sync.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong><br>
        This change affects only the old versions of Chrome and will be rolled out server-side. Chrome 133 is specified only to reflect the timeline when the change will make an effect.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrF131" name="upChromeBrsrF131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Disallow spaces in non-file:// URL hosts&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Per spec&nbsp; <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-host-code-point" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>URL hosts</u></a> [1] cannot contain the space character, but currently URL parsing in Chromium allows spaces in the host.</p>

    <p>This causes Chromium to fail several tests included in the <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/websockets?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2024-websockets" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Interop2024 'HTTPS URLs for WebSocket</u></a>' [2] and 'URL' <a href="https://wpt.fyi/results/url?label=master&amp;label=experimental&amp;aligned&amp;view=interop%20&amp;q=label%3Ainterop-2023-url" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>focus areas</u></a> [3].</p>

    <p>To bring Chromium into spec compliance, we would like to remove spaces from URL hosts altogether, but a difficulty with this is that they are used in the host part in Windows file:// URLs (<a href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/599" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>)[4].</p>

    <p>This feature will be part of the ongoing work to bring Chromium closer to spec compliance by forbidding spaces for non-file URLs only.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrG131" name="upChromeBrsrG131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 to v5 migration&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the v5 API instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5.</p>

    <p>If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4<u>*</u></code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead:<u> </u><code><u>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</u></code>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>This will be a gradual roll-out.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrP131" name="upChromeBrsrP131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Blob URL partitioning: Fetching or Navigation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>As a continuation of Storage partitioning, Chromium will implement partitioning of Blob URL access by Storage Key (top-level site, frame origin, and the <code>has-cross-site-ancestor </code>boolean), with the exception of navigations that will remain partitioned only by frame origin. This behavior is similar to what’s currently implemented by both Firefox and Safari, and aligns Blob URL usage with the partitioning scheme used by other storage APIs as part of Storage Partitioning. In addition, Chromium will enforce noopener on renderer-initiated navigations to Blob URLs where the corresponding site is cross-site to the top-level site performing the navigation. This aligns Chromium with similar behavior in Safari, and we will pursue spec updates to reflect both of these changes.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This change can be temporarily reverted by setting the <strong>PartitionedBlobURLUsage</strong> policy. The policy will be deprecated when the other storage partitioning-related enterprise policies are deprecated.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 134 on Windows, macOS, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ131" name="upChromeBrsrJ131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate mutation events&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Synchronous mutation events, including <code>DOMSubtreeModified, DOMNodeInserted, DOMNodeRemoved, DOMNodeRemovedFromDocument, DOMNodeInsertedIntoDocument, and DOMCharacterDataModified</code>, negatively affect page performance, and also significantly increase the complexity of adding new features to the Web. These APIs were deprecated from the spec in 2011, and were replaced (in 2012) by the much better-behaved Mutation Observer API. Usage of the obsolete mutation events must be removed or migrated to Mutation Observer. Starting in Chrome 124, a temporary enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a>, will be available to re-enable deprecated or removed mutation events. If you encounter any issues, file a bug <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Mutation event support will be disabled by default starting in Chrome 127, around July 30, 2024. Code should be migrated before that date to avoid site breakage. If more time is needed, there are a few options:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/origintrials/#/view_trial/919297273937002497" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Mutation Events Deprecation Trial</u></a> can be used to re-enable the feature for a limited time on a given site. This can be used through Chrome 134, ending March 25, 2025.</li>
      <li>A <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy can also be used for the same purpose, also through Chrome 134.</li>
    </ul>

    <p>To read more, see <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/mutation-events-deprecation" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>this</u></a> blog post. Report any issues <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy will be deprecated.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrM131" name="upChromeBrsrM131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome started directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Administrators might use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, available from Chrome 125, to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 136, and will be removed in Chrome 137. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that administrators can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise administrators may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt-in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt-out through Chrome 136.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

    <p>In Chrome 79, we introduced the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList</u></a> policy to revert the SameSite behavior of cookies to legacy behavior on the specified domains. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList</u></a> policy’s lifetime has been extended and will be removed on the milestone listed below.</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>ChromeOS updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeOSA131" name="chromeOSA131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS Flex auto-enrollment&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 131, ChromeOS Flex auto-enrollment now allows you to deploy ChromeOS Flex devices at scale. Similar to ChromeOS zero-touch enrollment, automatic enrollment embeds an enrollment token created by an organization's administrator into a ChromeOS Flex image. This will determine which customer organization and organizational unit a device will enroll into during initial device setup. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1360534" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Enroll ChromeOS devices</u></a> and the <a href="https://support.google.com/chromeosflex" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS Flex</u></a> help center.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB131" name="chromeOSB131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS Flex forced re-enrollment&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 131, enrolled ChromeOS Flex devices support manual forced re-enrollment. If the policy is set to enforce either automatic or manual re-enrollment, ChromeOS Flex devices will prompt users to manually re-enroll after a factory reset. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6352858" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Force wiped ChromeOS devices to re-enroll</u></a> and the <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1375678?hl=en&amp;sjid=13413969492411653424-NC#zippy=%2Cforced-re-enrollment" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Forced re-enrollment</u></a> device setting.&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSC131" name="chromeOSC131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Quick Answers styling refresh&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Quick Answers is a GenAI-powered reading assistant for ChromeOS, giving users quick insights into web pages and PDF documents. This includes summaries, interactive outlines, and document Q&amp;A. In ChromeOS 131, we introduce an updated styling for Quick Answers. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/13616580" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Quick Answers—definition</u></a>. This feature can be controlled using <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#QuickAnswers" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Quick Answers policies</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSD131" name="chromeOSD131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Split DNS for ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>You can now configure Secure DNS to be used on specified domains only. Admins can configure a list of domains to be included or excluded from using Secure DNS. You can configure this feature using these policies: <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DnsOverHttpsIncludedDomains" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DnsOverHttpsIncludedDomains</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DnsOverHttpsExcludedDomains" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DnsOverHttpsExcludedDomains</u></a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSE131" name="chromeOSE131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS Back To Safety&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>This feature gives users a way to get back to a good known state by disabling extensions and resetting settings that could hurt their experience. In past releases, in order to get your ChromeOS device to a known good state, you would have to powerwash. Thanks to this feature, there are now ways to non-destructively get your device to a state you feel comfortable with again!&nbsp;</p>

    <p>When a user selects <strong>Safety reset</strong>, this action will:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Reset Chrome settings and Chrome shortcuts&nbsp;</li>
      <li>Disable extensions</li>
      <li>Delete cookies and other temporary site data</li>
    </ul>

    <p><br>
      Bookmarks, history, and saved passwords won't be affected. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1360642" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Wipe ChromeOS device data</u></a>.</p>

    <p><img height="496.25000000000006" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd8jaqvm_YRyLDcasqsGcO80zmzFBGwV_IFtE2tXrSRAoDo23HuVzADJJB9VIE5oqXixHbI-ThAtUjLaJYpATl8841Rwo70_Hy7I5Td2beTEP-Bhm375Vm2sMg2-EkHWkdWfF_sI_8jx5Ty60D_gG0ylRELtP5BTK6Uknw3cOwQpPVP?key=uIDqQgcKFK5IYArAHl4brMBM" width="781.7931034482759"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSF131" name="chromeOSF131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Flash notifications&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Customers who frequently miss notifications that appear in the corner of the screen can now enable a setting that will flash the screen whenever a new notification arrives. This feature is particularly beneficial for customers who are hard of hearing or who use screen magnification and are often zoomed in, making it difficult to see corner notifications. This new setting can be found under <strong>Settings &gt; Accessibility &gt; Audio and captions &gt; Flash notifications</strong>.<br>
      <br>
      <strong><span> </span></strong><strong><img height="511" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcmiotS6Rn2S82D-cGcJv3RoxUOQUMqkcxJOF9AYSArh7u-m1lWP2k48X2WSPfiQNZJxBXLhmG7zGM4ZQyGdPna1I6sLqzez4a6mEddu6zzgm_ThsqQASIVOqpSM_0orwnT3_rY2okxI9MFhZb9CKkYRHQDRPP0It87eAgQfvJ5wlY?key=uIDqQgcKFK5IYArAHl4brMBM" width="631"></strong></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSG131" name="chromeOSG131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Microsoft SCEP SID update reminder&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p><strong>Only for SCEP deployments using Microsoft NPS for RADIUS. If you are not using SCEP certificates</strong> in combination with Microsoft NPS for Radius for Chromebook network connectivity, <strong>you may disregard the remainder of these instructions</strong>. We expect this to be a setup more common in enterprise rather than in education.</p>

    <p>Microsoft has announced a security update that will add a new required field, a Security Identifier (SID), to SCEP certificates in environments utilizing NPS for Radius for network authentication. This addition is due to a security vulnerability on Windows devices where usable certificates with private keys can be exported from one Windows device to be used on any other device. Addition of the SID means that the certificate becomes linked to a device or user in your Active Directory environment so that an unknown device/user cannot use it. This is not a security issue for Chromebooks, as they do not allow the exporting of certificates with private keys in them and they are protected by the TPM. However, any certificate lacking this new field will fail to authenticate against a NPS for Radius server after the hard enforcement deadline of February 11th, 2025.</p>

    <p><strong>What do you need to do?</strong></p>

    <p>As soon as possible, verify if your deployment relies on both SCEP certificates and NPS for Radius for network authentication. This can be done by going into event viewer on your <strong>Domain Controller &gt; System, </strong>and searching for event ID #39. If you see this event ID:</p>

    <p><img height="470" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfXC80gl78RCAkEsEj7d0n7wZetAMoeCbQ-RApJGhOcNkP3fY9qecrKqTt0aFAWbQuhP-7E_xqsaL5NTB7M70UpTbL4JQoQe75XSlxFJj1bAFvCE1kRzCXRQq5RvSUT-bbD9NHzNjEjTreBt8me4Emm3eRqvNgqXGmAdzYJm-HXs5xQ?key=uIDqQgcKFK5IYArAHl4brMBM" width="588"></p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>Actions to take if you see the event ID #39:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>Create a new object, or reuse an existing one, in your Active Directory environment for SCEP use</li>
      <li>Extract the SID for the AD object, for example, PS&gt; (Get-ADUser username).SID.value</li>
      <li>Create a new SCEP profile with all settings duplicated from your current setup and add in the SID of the newly created, or existing, AD object from step 1.</li>
      <li>Under the Subject Alternative name section select the <strong>Custom</strong> radio button. Add a new Subject Alternative name using the <strong>+</strong> button with the type Uniform Resource Identifier from the dropdown. Under string, the value should be similar to:&nbsp;</li>
    </ol>

    <p><code>tag:microsoft.com,2022-09-14:sid:S-1-2-3-4-5-6-8</code><br>
      <br>
      where <code>S-1-2-3-4-5-6-8</code> is the SID of the AD object</p>
    <br>
    <img height="232" src="//lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXez2ERvFiyJmGXKcM8Wbk8697mEPRcYy7uNgcYLs1cpOJle-hUgB7X-aEWmaD2R4CqtqmlNgWsqW53hQqx5z0iJG0q4gNYUDNmi3A8EDmH5-j3t8zXSVkJdfpr3gYAi_SGBzpnXX0mibK67UcR0mCQwgttRCb6YVxF-Y-ZCrWUSXWX3?key=uIDqQgcKFK5IYArAHl4brMBM" width="550">
    <ol start="5">
      <li>Deploy this new certificate to all potentially affected Chromebooks in your fleet
        <ol>
          <li>Wait, AT LEAST ONE MONTH, to reasonably guarantee that all devices have picked up the new certificate.</li>
        </ol>
      </li>
      <li>Re-link any and all policies from the old certificate to the new one from Step 2.</li>
      <li>Verify functionality using the new certificate.</li>
      <li>Delete the old profile.</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA131" name="upChromeOSA131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>AI wallpapers and backgrounds&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 132, we plan to introduce high-resolution, generative AI wallpapers and video call backgrounds on ChromeOS. With this feature, you can unleash your creativity and turn your Chromebook into a canvas of personal expression. Choose from a diverse collection of templates and, in just a few clicks, infuse your Chromebook with your unique personality, mood, or interest.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Two new policies will be available to control these features; <strong>GenAIVcBackgroundSettings</strong> and <strong>GenAIWallpaperSettings</strong>. This feature will be available on <a href="https://www.google.com/chromebook/discover/chromebookplus/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromebook Plus devices</u></a> only.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB131" name="upChromeOSB131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Graduate data migration&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 132, a new Content Transfer tool will guide graduate students or other EDU-managed users who want to migrate their data through the updated Google Takeout Transfer process. This allows them to take their Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Gmail content to a Gmail account of their choice.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This new application allows school administrators to pin an icon to the shelf, notify students and faculty on their Chromebooks, and set dates to trigger these nudges to encourage them to use the existing Takeout Transfer process.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSC131" name="upChromeOSC131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Native Client (NaCl) support ending on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>ChromeOS 132, scheduled for release in <strong>January 2025, </strong>will be the last release with NaCl support for unmanaged or consumer devices, followed by ChromeOS 138 in <strong>July 2025</strong> for <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1289314?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>managed devices</u></a>.</p>

    <p>In 2017, we announced the end of support of <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Native Client (NaCl)</u></a> in favor of <a href="https://webassembly.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly</u></a>. With most developers and users having migrated away from NaCl, we confirm the following NaCl discontinuation dates:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>January 2025:</strong> Native Client (NaCl) will be disabled from ChromeOS 132 onwards.

        <ul>
          <li>For unmanaged and consumer users, ChromeOS 132 will be the last ChromeOS release with support for NaCl.</li>
          <li>For managed environments (including Kiosk sessions), administrators who manage ChromeOS devices for a business or school, will have the option of extending the ability to use NaCl with a NaCl allow policy (<strong>DeviceNativeClientForceAllowed</strong>) through the ChromeOS 138 release. This policy will be available in the admin console from late December 2024 to early January 2025 before the release of ChromeOS 132.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li><strong>July 2025:</strong> ChromeOS 138 will be the last version with NaCl support.
        <ul>
          <li>For managed environments, ChromeOS 138 is a <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11333726?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Long-term Support (LTS)</u></a> ChromeOS release available to administrators who manage ChromeOS devices for a business or school.&nbsp;</li>
          <li>For devices that have been <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/3168106?hl=en#zippy=%2Cpin-chromeos-updates-to-a-specific-version" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>switched to the LTS channel</u></a> and have the NaCl allow policy enabled, NaCl will be available until LTS Last Refresh in <strong>April 2026</strong>.</li>
          <li><strong>No exceptions will be granted.</strong></li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <p>&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For Chrome Apps that use NaCl, migrate to <a href="https://webassembly.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly</u></a> (WASM). To help you with the transition, we've published the <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client/migration" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly Migration Guide</u></a>.</p>

    <p>For more information about this change or if you need assistance, you can refer to any of the following:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client/migration" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly Migration Guide</u></a>.</li>
      <li>
        <p>Please refer to the Chrome Enterprise and Education Help Center to learn more about <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/topic/6274424?hl=en&amp;ref_topic=4386913&amp;sjid=10808321024100605256-NC" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>managing policies for ChromeOS devices</u></a>.</p>
      </li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/join-us-in-the-chromeos-developer-community-on-discord" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS developer community on Discord</u></a>.</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS release schedule</u></a> for release dates and updates.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSD131" name="upChromeOSD131"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Chrome App support ending on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In 2016, we announced the deprecation of Chrome Apps in favor of web apps, and in 2021, we <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2021/10/extending-chrome-app-support-on-chrome.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>announced on the Chromium Blog</u></a> that Chrome App support for ChromeOS Enterprise and Education customers and developers on ChromeOS would be extended until at least January 2025. With the majority of our customers having migrated off of Chrome Apps (including <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#packaged-app-legacy" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Legacy (v1) packaged apps</u></a> and <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#hosted-app" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Hosted apps</u></a>), we can confirm the following updates about Chrome App discontinuation dates.</p>
    <strong>July 2025:</strong> End of support for user-installed Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M138).

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome Apps that are force-installed through the Admin console will continue to be supported.</li>
    </ul>
    <strong>July 2026:</strong> Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode (scheduled for ChromeOS M150).

    <ul>
      <li>Devices on the LTS channel with Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode will receive support until April 2027.</li>
    </ul>
    <strong>February 2028:</strong> Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M168), marking the end of life for all Chrome Apps.

    <ul>
      <li>Devices on the LTS channel can continue to use Chrome Apps until October 2028.</li>
      <li><strong>No exceptions will be granted.</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>These deprecation timelines also apply to self-hosted Chrome Apps.</p>

    <p>While no new Chrome Apps can be added to the Chrome Web Store, existing Chrome Apps can continue to be updated through October 2028 when they will reach end of life on ChromeOS. After this date, Chrome Apps will be removed from the Chrome Web Store.</p>

    <p>If your organization has developed in-house Chrome Apps and you need assistance, please refer to <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/apps/migration/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Transition from Chrome Apps</u></a> guide. You can also join us in the <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/join-us-in-the-chromeos-developer-community-on-discord" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS developer community on Discord</u></a>, or reach out to us through the form at <a href="https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us" rel="noopener" target="_blank">https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us</a>. Refer to the <a href="https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS release schedule</u></a> for release dates and updates.</p>

    <p>In the coming weeks, additional detailed information will be sent to all remaining Chrome App developers and all ChromeOS Administrators.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser changes</h2>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA130" name="chromeBrsrA130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Desktop toasts&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 130 introduces a new Toast pattern that will allow features to provide visual confirmation of user actions or a quick way to take a follow up action. For example, when adding something to a reading list, a Toast confirms that the item was added and offers a quick link to the reading list side panel. Toasts appear as a small chip that partially overlaps with the web contents and partially with the top toolbar of the browser.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>This will be enabled for an initial set of features in Chrome 130. Subsequent toasts will be rolled out independently by other teams utilizing the pattern.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/tQBHiSS0fDyMOkZ93VTc0P9SCcIJfxUvk_E-nHrng8NbNFFon9erDDeMTbEn3JnASoA=w673" width="673" height="262" alt="desktop toasts" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/tQBHiSS0fDyMOkZ93VTc0P9SCcIJfxUvk_E-nHrng8NbNFFon9erDDeMTbEn3JnASoA"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB130" name="chromeBrsrB130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Platform picker for screen sharing on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>When screen sharing in Chrome on macOS X Sequoia, users can now select a window or screen to share using the updated platform picker. This new platform picker removes the need for assigning screen recording permission to Chrome and is consistent with screen sharing in other macOS applications.</p>

    <p>The new picker will not be activated before the first update of macOS Sequoia, version 15.1 expected a month after the initial version of 15.0. Before that Chrome users might see a warning dialog that Chrome is not using the new picker API yet.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>To test the new screen share picker experience:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>Update Chrome to version 129 or later.</li>
      <li>On your macOS, open the Terminal.</li>
      <li>At the prompt, type: <code>open -b com.google.Chrome --args -enable-features=UseSCContentSharingPicker</code></li>
      <li>To execute the command, on your keyboard, press <strong>Enter</strong>.</li>
    </ol>
    &nbsp;

    <p>The feature can also be enabled in <code>chrome://flags</code>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on macOS</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/lNNIzNT_05yZx1rOGBtNR-VD6mEv92fjDR3nYqeR8_Dc5xgYgp_Q61MFP2BeK7_F2cU=w668" width="668" height="325" alt="screen share" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/lNNIzNT_05yZx1rOGBtNR-VD6mEv92fjDR3nYqeR8_Dc5xgYgp_Q61MFP2BeK7_F2cU"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC130" name="chromeBrsrC130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New Account menu&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Some users can now access a new <strong>Account</strong> menu by tapping on their avatar on the <strong>New tab</strong> page. The new <strong>Account</strong> menu allows them to sign out, switch accounts easily and resolve errors related to their account in Chrome. Existing policies like <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a> and <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#RestrictAccountsToPatterns" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>RestrictAccountsToPatterns</u></a> can be used to determine which accounts a user can sign in or switch to.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on iOS</strong></li>
    </ul>

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/bkW-tMa-A8zsbCloQYggmPuymwAag8Eyc8n2Ok-Rs3bG_7yRpvnK3OCcBolkcbqYvAuE=w352" width="352" height="773" alt="new account menu" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/bkW-tMa-A8zsbCloQYggmPuymwAag8Eyc8n2Ok-Rs3bG_7yRpvnK3OCcBolkcbqYvAuE"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD130" name="chromeBrsrD130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>PDF Viewer on Android&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature provides the ability to view PDFs within Chrome browser UI. Prior to this change, users have to complete many steps to view a PDF document. These steps force them out of Chrome to view the PDF document. With this feature, PDFs will render seamlessly in Chrome. Users will still be able to download PDFs and open with other first- or third-party apps of choice.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Android</strong><span>&nbsp;</span></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrE130" name="chromeBrsrE130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Tab freezing on Energy saver&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>When Energy saver is active, Chrome now freezes a tab that has been hidden and silent for &gt;5 minutes and uses a lot of CPU, unless:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>the tab provides audio- or video- conferencing functionality (detected via microphone, camera or screen, window, or tab capture, or an RTCPeerConnection with an open RTCDataChannel or a live MediaStreamTrack).</li>
      <li>the tab controls an external device (detected using Web USB, Web Bluetooth, Web HID or Web Serial).</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>This will extend battery life and speed up Chrome through reduced CPU usage.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The feature can be tested in Chrome 130 via the <code>#freezing-on-energy-saver </code>entry in about:flags. Alternatively, it can be tested with the <code>#freezing-on-energy-saver-testing</code> which simulates that Energy saver is active and that all tabs use a lot of CPU (this allows verifying whether a tab is eligible for freezing and would be frozen if it used a lot of CPU). Energy saver availability can be controlled via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BatterySaverModeAvailability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BatterySaverModeAvailability</u></a> policy (this change has no effect when Energy saver is inactive).</li>
      <li>Chrome 131 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: The feature will start rolling out to 1% of Stable in Chrome 131. It will gradually be ramped up to 100% of Stable. Energy saver availability can be controlled via the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BatterySaverModeAvailability" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BatterySaverModeAvailability</u></a> policy (this change has no effect when Energy saver is inactive).</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrF130" name="chromeBrsrF130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Compression dictionary transport with Shared Brotli and Shared Zstandard&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature adds support for using designated previous responses as an external dictionary for content encoding compressing responses with Brotli or Zstandard.</p>

    <p>Enterprises might experience potential compatibility issues with enterprise network infrastructure that intercepts HTTPS traffic and is sensitive to unknown content encodings. The enterprise policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CompressionDictionaryTransportEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CompressionDictionaryTransportEnabled</u></a> is available to turn off the compression dictionary transport feature.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrG130" name="chromeBrsrG130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Keyboard-focusable scroll containers&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 130 improves accessibility by making scroll containers focusable using sequential focus navigation. Today, the tab key doesn't focus scrollers unless tabIndex is explicitly set to 0 or more.</p>

    <p>By making scrollers focusable by default, users who can't (or don't want to) use a mouse can now focus clipped content using tab and arrow keys. This behavior is enabled only if the scroller does not contain any keyboard-focusable children. This logic is necessary so we don't cause regressions for existing focusable elements that might exist within a scroller like a <code>&lt;textarea&gt;</code>.</p>

    <p><strong>Note:</strong> The previous rollout of this feature (started in Chrome 127) was stopped due to web compatibility issues, which should be fixed in the implementation shipping in Chrome 130.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrH130" name="chromeBrsrH130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support non-special scheme URLs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 130 supports <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">non-special scheme URLs</a>, for example, <code>git://example.com/path</code>. Previously, the Chromium URL parser didn't support non-special URLs. The parser parses non-special URLs as if they had an opaque path, which is not aligned with the URL standard. Now, the Chromium URL parser parses non-special URLs correctly, following the URL standard. For more details, see <a href="http://bit.ly/url-non-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">http://bit.ly/url-non-special</a>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrI130" name="chromeBrsrI130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome on Android now supports third-party autofill and password providers&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Until now, third-party autofill and password providers could be used in Chrome on Android via accessibility APIs. In Chrome 130, we're adding direct support for Android Autofill which means these providers now work with Chrome on Android without the need for accessibility APIs. This should improve the performance of Chrome on Android. To take advantage of this, users need to ensure they have their third party provider configured in Android settings. Then, in Chrome they'll need to open <strong>Settings &gt; Autofill services</strong> and choose <strong>Autofill using another service</strong>. If users do not change <strong>both</strong> settings, they will continue to use Google to autofill their passwords, payment and address information.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Android: </strong>The new setting will be available from Chrome 130. If users use the new setting it will take immediate effect. If the new setting is not used, users will continue to use either Google and a third party via accessibility (if installed). The support for accessibility APIs will be deprecated in early 2025, at which point the new settings will be honored for all users.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrJ130" name="chromeBrsrJ130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>&lt;meter&gt; element fallback styles&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>In Chrome 130, <code>&lt;meter&gt; </code>elements with appearance: none now have a reasonable fallback style that matches Safari and Firefox, instead of just disappearing from the page. Additionally, developers can now custom style the <code>&lt;meter&gt;</code> elements.</p>

    <p>A feature flag <code>MeterAppearanceNoneFallbackStyle</code> is available in <code>chrome://flags</code> until Chrome 133 to control this feature.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2>Chrome Enterprise Core changes</h2>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeECD130" name="upChromeECD130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Default change for GenAI policies&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting with 130, we are changing&nbsp;the default setting for GenAI policies from switched off to <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14443058" rel="noopener" target="_blank">allowed, without improving AI models</a>,&nbsp;for Workspace for Education users.&nbsp;If you have devices enrolled in Chrome Enterprise Core, this policy is automatically applied to those devices to prevent sending data for AI model training. The existing policies that&nbsp;have the updated default setting are:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CreateThemesSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CreateThemesSettings</u></a> (available in the US-only for now)</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DevToolsGenAiSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DevToolsGenAiSettings</u></a> (available in most countries)</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HelpMeWriteSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HelpMeWriteSettings</u></a> (available in the US-only for now)</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HistorySearchSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HistorySearchSettings</u></a> (available in the US-only for now)</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TabOrganizerSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TabOrganizerSettings</u></a> (available in the US-only for now)</li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TabCompareSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TabCompareSettings</u></a> (available in the US-only for now)</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>For more details about the default settings, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14443058?hl=en&amp;ref_topic=14443801&amp;sjid=17259358006575789407-NA" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Chrome—Generative AI features and policies</a>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeECB130" name="chromeECB130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support for user-level settings on Custom configurations&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p><strong>Custom configurations</strong> recently launched in Chrome 127 and this feature allows IT admins to configure Chrome policies that are not yet in the Admin console, using JSON scripts. <strong>As early as October 15</strong>, <strong>Custom configurations</strong> will support applying settings at the user-level, in addition to device-level support. In order words, you will be able to enforce policies when users sign in to a managed Google account using <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14749672?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Custom configurations</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>As early as October 15 2024, on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Feature rolls out</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>To get started, you can navigate to <strong>Chrome browser &gt; Custom configurations</strong> in the Admin console; the Chrome Enterprise Core SKU is required to access this feature.</p>

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/B_sakAv22sPdTlvdff9AptGmTTEF5Kg4Bub_UsiNYfumPRt94FKewoMflaw-i6O_cSo=w804" width="804" height="445" alt="custom configurations" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/B_sakAv22sPdTlvdff9AptGmTTEF5Kg4Bub_UsiNYfumPRt94FKewoMflaw-i6O_cSo"></p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeECC130" name="chromeECC130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Audit-only URL navigation rules&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature lets customers create Chrome URL navigation rules with the Audit action. These rules allow admins to dry-run URL navigation rules before starting to show user warnings. They also allow admins to silently audit users’ navigation to restricted or sensitive URLs.</p>

    <p>URL auditing is part of the existing real-time URL check connector policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#EnterpriseRealTimeUrlCheckMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>EnterpriseRealTimeUrlCheckMode</u></a>, which can be turned on by Organizational Unit or by Group.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>

<p><a id="chromeECD130" name="chromeECD130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Security Insights&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>You can now enable Chrome Security Insights to monitor insider risk and data loss with enhanced monitoring for Chrome activity. This feature is available for the following licenses:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome Enterprise Core</li>
      <li>Workspace Enterprise Standard</li>
      <li>Workspace Enterprise Plus.&nbsp;</li>
    </ul>

    <p>For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/13761175" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Monitoring for insider risk and data loss</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Feature enabled for Chrome Enterprise Core&nbsp;</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows:</strong> Feature enabled for EDU customers (except K-12)</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>

<p><a id="chromeECE130" name="chromeECE130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Risk score on the Chrome Apps and extensions usage report&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>This feature adds a new column in the Admin console for browser management that displays the risk assessment for installed extensions in the admin's environment. This new addition allows IT admins to quickly identify extensions with a high, medium or low risk score using the sorting and filtering functionality of the report.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome browser changes</h4>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrA130" name="upChromeBrsrA130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Search and receive answers in your Chrome history with AI&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 131, users will be able to search their browsing history and receive generated answers based on page contents. Initially, this feature will only be available to users in English in the US. Admins can control this feature by using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HistorySearchSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HistorySearchSettings</u></a> policy. You have the following options for your organization:&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>0 = Enable the feature for users, and send relevant data to Google to help train or improve AI models. Relevant data may include prompts, inputs, outputs, and source materials, depending on the feature. It may be reviewed by humans for the sole purpose of improving AI models.</li>
      <li>1 = Enable the feature for users, but do not send data to Google to train or improve AI models.</li>
      <li>2 = Fully disable feature</li>
    </ul>

    <p>For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15248971" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Search your history in Chrome with AI</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <p><strong>● Chrome 131 on Linux, Mac, Windows:</strong> the feature generates answers to your search queries.</p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrB130" name="upChromeBrsrB130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Ad-hoc code signatures for Progressive Web App shims on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Code signatures for application shims that are created when installing a Progressive Web App (PWA) on macOS are changing to use ad-hoc code signatures, which are created when the application is installed. The code signature is used by macOS as part of the application's identity. These ad-hoc signatures will result in each PWA shim having a unique identity to macOS; currently every PWA looks like the same application to macOS.</p>

    <p>This will address problems when attempting to include multiple PWAs in the macOS <em>Open at Login</em> preference pane, and will permit future improvements for handling user notifications within PWAs on macOS.</p>

    <p>Administrators should test for compatibility with any endpoint security or binary authorization tools they use (such as Santa). The feature can be enabled for this testing via <code>chrome://flags/#use-adhoc-signing-for-web-app-shims</code>. They can then install a Progressive Web Apps and ensure that it launches as expected.</p>

    <p>If there is an incompatibility between the feature and their current security policies, the enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#AdHocCodeSigningForPWAsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>AdHocCodeSigningForPWAsEnabled</u></a>, can be used to disable the feature while they deploy an updated endpoint security policy. The enterprise policy is intended to be used to disable the feature only until endpoint security policies have been updated, at which point it should be unset.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on macOS:</strong> Feature disabled behind a flag (<code>chrome://flags/#use-adhoc-signing-for-web-app-shims</code>) so that enterprises can test for compatibility with their endpoint security tools, such as Santa (<code>https://santa.dev/</code>). If it is not currently compatible they can disable the feature via the enterprise policy while they update their endpoint security configurations. The enterprise policy is intended to be used to disable the feature only until endpoint security policies have been updated.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on macOS:</strong> Feature will begin to roll out to Stable, starting at 1% rollout.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrC130" name="upChromeBrsrC130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Asynchronous real-time Safe Browsing check&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Today, Safe Browsing checks are on the blocking path of page loads, meaning that the user cannot see the page until the checks are completed. In Chrome 122 and later on Android, ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, to improve Chrome's loading speed, real-time Safe Browsing checks no longer block page loads. We have evaluated the risk and put mitigations in place:&nbsp;</p>

    <ol>
      <li>For malware and 0-day attacks, local-blocklist checks will still be conducted in a synchronous manner so that malicious payloads are still blocked by Safe Browsing.&nbsp;</li>
      <li>For phishing attacks, we've looked at data and it is unlikely the user would have interacted with the page (for example, type a password) by the time we show the warning.</li>
    </ol>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 122 on Android, ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on iOS</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove non-standard GPUAdapter requestAdapterInfo() method&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>The <a href="https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/gpu/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebGPU</u></a> working group decided it was impractical for <code>requestAdapterInfo() </code>to trigger a permission prompt so they’ve removed that option and replaced it with the GPUAdapter info attribute.&nbsp;This means that web developers can get the same <code>GPUAdapterInfo</code> value synchronously. For more information, see the previous <a href="https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/eZqMmX7q_bA/m/euMLVMpxAgAJ" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Intent to Ship: WebGPU: GPUAdapter</u></a> info attribute.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate Safe Browsing Extended reporting&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p><strong>Safe Browsing Extended</strong> reporting is a feature that enhances the security of all users by collecting telemetry information from participating users that is used for Google Safe Browsing protections. The data collected includes URLs of visited web pages, limited system information, and some page content. However, this feature is now superseded by <strong>Enhanced protection </strong>mode. <ul>
  <li><strong>Entrust certificate distrust&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>In response to sustained compliance failures, Chrome 127 changes how publicly-trusted TLS server authentication, that is, websites or certificates issued by Entrust, are trusted by default. This applies to Chrome 127 and later on Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, and Linux; iOS policies do not allow use of the Chrome Root Store in Chrome for iOS.</p>

    <p>Specifically, TLS certificates validating to the Entrust root CA certificates included in the Chrome Root Store and issued:</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- after October 31, 2024, will no longer be trusted by default.</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- on or before October 31, 2024, will be unaffected by this change.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>If a Chrome user or an enterprise explicitly trusts any of the affected Entrust certificates on a platform and version of Chrome relying on the Chrome Root Store, for example, when explicit trust is conveyed through a Windows Group Policy Object, the Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT) constraints described above will be overridden and certificates will function as they do today.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For additional information and testing resources, see <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2024/06/sustaining-digital-certificate-security.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Sustaining Digital Certificate Security - Entrust Certificate Distrust.</u></a></p>

    <p>To learn more about the Chrome Root Store, see this <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/net/data/ssl/chrome_root_store/faq.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>FAQ</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>All versions of Chrome 131 and higher that rely on the Chrome Root Store will honor the blocking action, but the blocking action will only begin for certificates issued after November 11, 2024.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH130" name="upChromeBrsrH130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Simplified sign-in and sync experience&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 131, existing users with Chrome sync turned on will experience a simplified and consolidated version of sign-in and sync in Chrome. Chrome sync will no longer be shown as a separate feature in settings or elsewhere. Instead, users can sign in to Chrome to use and save information like passwords, bookmarks and more in their Google Account, subject to the relevant enterprise policies.</p>

    <p>As before, the functionality previously part of Chrome sync that saves and accesses Chrome data in the Google Account can be controlled by <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a>. Sign-in to Chrome can be disabled via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a> as before.</p>

    <p>Note that the changes do not affect users’ ability to sign in to Google services on the web (like Gmail) without signing in to Chrome, their ability to stay signed out of Chrome, or their ability to control what information is synced with their Google Account.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>User Link capturing on PWAs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Web links automatically direct users to installed web apps. To better align with users' expectations around installed web apps, Chrome makes it easier to move between the browser and installed web apps. When the user clicks a link that could be handled by an installed web app, Chrome adds a chip in the address bar to suggest switching over to the app. When the user clicks the chip, this either launches the app directly, or opens a grid of apps that can support that link. For some users, clicking a link always automatically opens the app.</p>

      <li>Chrome 121 on Linux, macOS, Windows: When some users click a link, it always opens in an installed PWA, while some users see the link open in a new tab with a chip in the address bar, clicking on which will launch the app. A flag is available to control this feature: <code>chrome://flags/#enable-user-link-capturing-pwa</code>.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Linux, macOS, Windows:</strong> Launch to 100% of Stable with either a default on (always launch apps on link clicks) or a default off (always open in a tab, only launch if the user clicks on chip on address bar).<br>

  <li><strong>Deprecation of CSS Anchor Positioning property </strong><strong><em>inset-area</em>&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>The <a href="https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/css/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSS working group</u></a> (CSSWG) resolved to rename the inset-area property to position-area. For more details, see the CSSWG discussion on <a href="https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/10209#issuecomment-2221005001" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>github</u></a>. The new property name, position-area, as a synonym for inset-area shipped via this feature update described on <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/6567965055778816" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chrome Platform Status</u></a>, describing the deprecation and removal of the inset-area property.</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK130" name="upChromeBrsrK130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>X25519Kyber768 key encapsulation for TLS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 124, Chrome enables by default on all desktop platforms a new post-quantum secure TLS key encapsulation mechanism X25519Kyber768, based on a NIST standard (ML-KEM). This protects network traffic from Chrome with servers that also support ML-KEM from decryption by a future quantum computer. This change should be transparent to server operators. This cipher will be used for both TLS 1.3 and QUIC connections.</p>

    <p>However, some TLS middleboxes might be unprepared for the size of a Kyber (ML-KEM) key encapsulation, or a new TLS ClientHello cipher code point, leading to dropped or hanging connections. This can be resolved by updating your middlebox, or disabling the key encapsulation mechanism via the temporary <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, which will be available through the end of 2024. However, long term, post-quantum secure ciphers will be required in TLS and the enterprise policy will be removed. Post-quantum cryptography is required for CSNA 2.0.</p>

    <p>For more detail, see this <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2023/08/protecting-chrome-traffic-with-hybrid.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium blog</u></a> post and this <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2024/08/post-quantum-cryptography-standards.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Google Security blog</u></a> post.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 124 on Windows, Mac, Linux: new post-quantum secure TLS key encapsulation mechanism X25519Kyber768 is enabled</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Windows, Mac, Linux: </strong>Switch to standard version of ML-KEM</li>
      <li>Chrome 141 on Windows, Mac, Linux: Remove enterprise policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled</u></a></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL130" name="upChromeBrsrL130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

    <p>Chrome Desktop now makes scanned PDFs more accessible. Using on-device OCR to maintain privacy (no content is sent to Google), Chrome automatically converts scanned PDFs, allowing you to select text, Ctrl+F, copy, and paste. The feature does not bypass secure PDFs. It will only OCR PDFs the user has access to. The solution unlocks PDF accessibility to Chrome users without any extra steps, making PDFs as accessible as the rest of the web.</p>

<ul>

    <p>To improve security and reliability, the network service, already running in its own process, will be sandboxed on Windows. As part of this, third-party code that is currently able to tamper with the network service may be prevented from doing so. This might cause interoperability issues with software that injects code into Chrome's process space, such as Data Loss Prevention software. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#NetworkServiceSandboxEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>NetworkServiceSandboxEnabled</u></a> policy allows you to disable the sandbox if incompatibilities are discovered. You can test the sandbox in your environment using <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Bk3Z8CUQucd8FP6ISKkT3Q9YYuP43574VIO_kyAISBU/view#heading=h.llygd223jffh" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>these</u></a> instructions. You can use the <a href="https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/entry?template=Enterprise+Issue&amp;summary=Network+Sandbox+Issue+:&amp;comment=Chrome" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium bug tracker</u></a> to report any issues you encounter.</p>
    &nbsp;

      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Windows: </strong>Network Service sandboxed on Windows</li>
