<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrP130" name="upChromeBrsrP130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Capture all screens&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>This feature captures all the screens currently connected to the device using <code>getAllScreensMedia()</code>. Calling <code>getDisplayMedia()</code> multiple times requires multiple user gestures, burdens the user with choosing the next screen each time, and does not guarantee to the app that all the screens were selected. <code>getAllScreensMedia()</code> improves on all of these fronts.</p>

    <p>This feature is only exposed behind the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MultiScreenCaptureAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MultiScreenCaptureAllowedForUrls</u></a> enterprise policy, and users are warned before recording even starts, that recording <em>could</em> start at some point. The API will only work for origins that are specified in the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MultiScreenCaptureAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MultiScreenCaptureAllowedForUrls</u></a> allowlist. Any origin not specified there, will not have access to it.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on ChromeOS</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrQ130" name="upChromeBrsrQ130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>SafeBrowsing API v4 to v5 migration&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Chrome calls into the <a href="https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing/v4" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SafeBrowsing v4 API</u></a> will be migrated to call into the v5 API instead. The method names are also different between v4 and v5.</p>

    <p>If admins have any v4-specific URL allowlisting to allow network requests to <code>https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4*</code>, these should be modified to allow network requests to the whole domain instead: <code>safebrowsing.googleapis.com</code>. Otherwise, rejected network requests to the v5 API will cause security regressions for users.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>This will be a gradual roll-out.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrR130" name="upChromeBrsrR130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Private network access checks for navigation requests: warning-only mode&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Before a website A navigates to another site B in the user's private network, this feature does the following:</p>

    <p>1. Checks whether the request has been initiated from a secure context.</p>

    <p>2. Sends a preflight request, and checks whether B responds with a header that allows private network access.</p>

    <p>There are already features for subresources and workers, but this one is for navigation requests specifically. These checks protect the user's private network.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Since this feature is the warning-only mode, we do not fail the requests if any of the checks fail. Instead, a warning will be shown in the DevTools console, to help developers prepare for the coming enforcement.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 133 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrS130" name="upChromeBrsrS130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate mutation events&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Synchronous mutation events, including <code>DOMSubtreeModified</code>, <code>DOMNodeInserted</code>, <code>DOMNodeRemoved</code>, <code>DOMNodeRemovedFromDocument</code>, <code>DOMNodeInsertedIntoDocument</code>, and <code>DOMCharacterDataModified</code>, negatively affect page performance, and also significantly increase the complexity of adding new features to the Web. These APIs were deprecated from the spec in 2011, and were replaced (in 2012) by the much better-behaved Mutation Observer API. Usage of the obsolete mutation events must be removed or migrated to Mutation Observer. Starting in Chrome 124, a temporary enterprise policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank">MutationEventsEnabled</a>, will be available to re-enable deprecated or removed mutation events. If you encounter any issues, file a bug <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>

    <p>Mutation event support will be disabled by default starting in Chrome 127, around July 30, 2024. Code should be migrated before that date to avoid site breakage. If more time is needed, there are a few options:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>The <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/origintrials/#/view_trial/919297273937002497" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Mutation Events Deprecation Trial</u></a> can be used to re-enable the feature for a limited time on a given site. This can be used through Chrome 134, ending March 25, 2025.</li>
      <li>A <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy can also be used for the same purpose, also through Chrome 134.</li>
    </ul>

    <p>Please see <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/mutation-events-deprecation" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>this</u></a> blog post for more detail. Report any issues <a href="https://issues.chromium.org/new?component=1456718&amp;template=1948649" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#MutationEventsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>MutationEventsEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy will be deprecated.</li>
    </ul>
    <br>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrT130" name="upChromeBrsrT130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome will start directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Administrators might use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, available from Chrome 125, to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 136, and will be removed in Chrome 137. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that administrators can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise administrators may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt-in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt-out through Chrome 136.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

Google SecOps will analyze the data to provide instant analysis and context on risky activity; this data is further enriched to provide additional context and is searchable for a year.</p>

<div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Chrome Enterprise Premium changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeEPA130" name="upChromeEPA130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Enterprise Data Controls: Clipboard&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Admins can set data control rules in the Google Admin console to protect end users from data leakage on Chrome browser. Data Controls are lightweight rules set in the Google Admin console that allow admins to set a Chrome policy to control sensitive user actions such as copying and pasting sensitive data and taking screenshots or screen sharing.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>This feature can be controlled via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DataControlsRules" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DataControlsRules</u></a> policy. This feature is available to test for the members of the Chrome Enterprise Trusted Tester program. You can sign up for our Trusted Tester program <a href="https://inthecloud.withgoogle.com/trusted-testers/sign-up.html?_ga=2.146701236.-163299450.1697557917&amp;_gl=1*96nbfd*_ga*MTYzMjk5NDUwLjE2OTc1NTc5MTc.*_ga_WH2QY8WWF5*MTY5NzU1NzkxNi4xLjEuMTY5NzU1ODIyMy4wLjAuMA.." rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>here</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

      <li>Chrome 128 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: Trusted Tester program</li>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Screenshot protections&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    &nbsp; <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/9SVRWY4EJ6xp3wkTi_N3HVdLBk6JsfPMJUDkEjW2YSC2x2VI1VjpigBVXF6fzyyUI8c=w512" width="512" height="233" alt="Access point names" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/9SVRWY4EJ6xp3wkTi_N3HVdLBk6JsfPMJUDkEjW2YSC2x2VI1VjpigBVXF6fzyyUI8c"><br>
    &nbsp;</li>

<p><a id="chromeOST130" name="chromeOST130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Microsoft SCEP SID update&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><strong>Only for SCEP deployments using Microsoft NPS for RADIUS. If you are not using SCEP certificates</strong> in combination with Microsoft NPS for Radius for Chromebook network connectivity, <strong>you may disregard the remainder of these instructions</strong>. We expect this to be a setup more common in enterprise rather than in education.</p>

    <p>Microsoft has announced a security update that will add a new required field, a Security Identifier (SID), to SCEP certificates in environments utilizing NPS for Radius for network authentication. This addition is due to a security vulnerability on Windows devices where usable certificates with private keys can be exported from one Windows device to be used on any other device. Addition of the SID means that the certificate becomes linked to a device or user in your Active Directory environment so that an unknown device/user cannot use it. This is not a security issue for Chromebooks, as they do not allow the exporting of certificates with private keys in them and they are protected by the TPM. However, any certificate lacking this new field will fail to authenticate against a NPS for Radius server after the hard enforcement deadline of February 11th, 2025.</p>

    <p><strong>What do you need to do?</strong></p>

    <p>As soon as possible, verify if your deployment relies on both SCEP certificates and NPS for Radius for network authentication. This can be done by going into event viewer on your <strong>Domain Controller -&gt; System, </strong>and searching for event ID #39. If you see this event ID:</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/lW60Ni8qf8odBCObhOtpP1et87ivHJpeRWRgq5RKBG_TuBJndcC5BjtBMP4SKwg4Cg=w512" width="512" height="409" alt="Microsoft SCEP" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/lW60Ni8qf8odBCObhOtpP1et87ivHJpeRWRgq5RKBG_TuBJndcC5BjtBMP4SKwg4Cg"> &nbsp;

    <p>Actions to take if you see the event ID #39:</p>

    <ol>
      <li>Create a new object, or reuse an existing one, in your Active Directory environment for SCEP use</li>
      <li>Extract the SID for the AD object, for example, PS&gt; (Get-ADUser username).SID.value</li>
      <li>Create a new SCEP profile with all settings duplicated from your current setup and add in the SID of the newly created, or existing, AD object from step 1.</li>
      <li>Under the Subject Alternative name section select the <strong>Custom</strong> radio button. Add a new Subject Alternative name using the <strong>+</strong> button with the type Uniform Resource Identifier from the dropdown. Under string, the value should be similar to:&nbsp;</li>
    </ol>

    <p>&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;<code>tag:microsoft.com,2022-09-14:sid:S-1-2-3-4-5-6-8</code><br>
      <br>
      &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;where <code>S-1-2-3-4-5-6-8</code> is the SID of the AD object&nbsp;</p>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/ETsDnWecQ7n9JzWK-JKIgz_4lCJgsJ9hyHDbQOlIjQ7N2-P5PHIKHN61aypRCxgRIw=w512" width="512" height="216" alt="Microsoft SCEP" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/ETsDnWecQ7n9JzWK-JKIgz_4lCJgsJ9hyHDbQOlIjQ7N2-P5PHIKHN61aypRCxgRIw">

    <ol start="5">
      <li>Deploy this new certificate to all potentially affected Chromebooks in your fleet:
        <ol>
          <li>Wait, AT LEAST ONE MONTH, to reasonably guarantee that all devices have picked up the new certificate.</li>
        </ol>
      </li>
      <li>Relink any and all policies from the old certificate to the new one from Step 2.</li>
      <li>Verify functionality using the new certificate.</li>
      <li>Delete the old profile.</li>
    </ol>

    <p>&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>AI wallpapers and backgrounds&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 131, we plan to introduce high-resolution, generative AI wallpapers and video call backgrounds on ChromeOS. With this feature, you can unleash your creativity and turn your Chromebook into a canvas of personal expression. Choose from a diverse collection of templates and, in just a few clicks, infuse your Chromebook with your unique personality, mood, or interest.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Two new policies will be available to control these features; <strong>GenAIVcBackgroundSettings</strong> and <strong>GenAIWallpaperSettings</strong>. This feature will be available on <a href="https://www.google.com/chromebook/discover/chromebookplus/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromebook Plus devices</u></a> only.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB130" name="upChromeOSB130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS Flex auto-enrollment&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 131, ChromeOS Flex auto-enrollment will allow you to deploy ChromeOS Flex devices at scale. Similar to ChromeOS zero-touch enrollment, automatic enrollment embeds an enrollment token created by an organization's administrator into a ChromeOS Flex image. This will determine which customer organization and organizational unit a device will enroll into during initial device setup.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSC130" name="upChromeOSC130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Graduate data migration&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 132, a new Content Transfer tool will guide graduate students or other EDU-managed users who want to migrate their data through the updated Google Takeout Transfer process. This allows them to take their Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Gmail content to a Gmail account of their choice.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This new application allows school administrators to pin an icon to the shelf, notify students and faculty on their Chromebooks, and set dates to trigger these nudges to encourage them to use the existing Takeout Transfer process.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSD130" name="upChromeOSD130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Chrome App support ending on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In 2016, we announced the deprecation of Chrome Apps in favor of web apps, and in 2021, we <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2021/10/extending-chrome-app-support-on-chrome.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>announced on the Chromium Blog</u></a> that Chrome App support for ChromeOS Enterprise and Education customers and developers on ChromeOS would be extended until at least January 2025. With the majority of our customers having migrated off of Chrome Apps (including <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#packaged-app-legacy" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Legacy (v1) packaged apps</u></a> and <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/extensions/docs/extension_and_app_types.md#hosted-app" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Hosted apps</u></a>), we can confirm the following updates about Chrome App discontinuation dates.</p>
    <strong>July 2025:</strong> End of support for user-installed Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M138).

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome Apps that are force-installed through the Admin console will continue to be supported.</li>
    </ul>
    <strong>July 2026:</strong> Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode (scheduled for ChromeOS M150).

    <ul>
      <li>Devices on the LTS channel with Chrome Apps in Kiosk Mode will receive support until April 2027.</li>
    </ul>
    <strong>February 2028:</strong> Last ChromeOS release with support for Chrome Apps (scheduled for ChromeOS M168), marking the end of life for all Chrome Apps.

    <ul>
      <li>Devices on the LTS channel can continue to use Chrome Apps until October 2028.</li>
      <li>No exceptions will be granted.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>These deprecation timelines also apply to self-hosted Chrome Apps.</p>

    <p>While no new Chrome Apps can be added to the Chrome Web Store, existing Chrome Apps can continue to be updated through October 2028 when they will reach end of life on ChromeOS. After this date, Chrome Apps will be removed from the Chrome Web Store.</p>

    <p>If your organization has developed in-house Chrome Apps and you need assistance, please refer to <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/apps/migration/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Transition from Chrome Apps</u></a> guide. You can also join us in the <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/join-us-in-the-chromeos-developer-community-on-discord" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS developer community on Discord</u></a>, or reach out to us through the form at <a href="https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us" rel="noopener" target="_blank">https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us</a>. Refer to the <a href="https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS release schedule</u></a> for release dates and updates.</p>

    <p>In the coming weeks, additional detailed information will be sent to all remaining Chrome App developers and all ChromeOS Administrators.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSE130" name="upChromeOSE130"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Native Client (NaCl) support ending on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In 2017, we announced the deprecation of Native Client (NaCl) in favor of <a href="https://webassembly.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly</u></a>. With the majority of our customers having migrated off of NaCl, we can confirm some important changes coming to ChromeOS.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>January 2025: </strong>Native Client (NaCl) will be disabled by default from ChromeOS M132 onwards.

        <ul>
          <li>For unmanaged and consumer users, M131 will be the last ChromeOS release with support for NaCl.</li>
          <li>For managed user environments, administrators who manage ChromeOS devices for a business or school already will have the option of extending the ability to use NaCl with a NaCl allow policy through the M138 release. Starting with M132, the policy will also be available for Kiosk sessions.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li><strong>July 2025: </strong>ChromeOS M138 will mark the end of life for NaCl technology on ChromeOS.
        <ul>
          <li>For managed environments, M138 is a <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11333726?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Long-term Support (LTS)</u></a> ChromeOS release available to administrators who manage ChromeOS devices for a business or school. Devices that have been <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/3168106?hl=en#zippy=%2Cpin-chromeos-updates-to-a-specific-version" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>switched to the LTS channel</u></a> and have the NaCl allow policy enabled can continue to use NaCl until LTS Last Refresh in April 2026.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p>If your organization has developed in-house Chrome Apps with NaCl and you need assistance, please refer to <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/apps/migration/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Transition from Chrome Apps</u></a> and <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/native-client/migration" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>WebAssembly Migration</u></a> guides. You can also join us in the <a href="https://chromeos.dev/en/posts/join-us-in-the-chromeos-developer-community-on-discord" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS developer community on Discord</u></a>, or reach out to us through the form at <a href="https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us" rel="noopener" target="_blank">https://chromeos.dev/work-with-us</a>. Refer to the <a href="https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeOS release schedule</u></a> for release dates and updates.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>In the coming weeks, additional detailed information will be sent to NaCl developers and impacted ChromeOS Administrators.</p>

    <p>&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

  <div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA129" name="chromeBrsrA129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Tab compare&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 129 (US-only), we introduce <strong>Tab compare</strong>, a new feature that presents an AI-generated overview of products from across multiple tabs, all in one place. This feature is controlled through the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TabCompareSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>TabCompareSettings</u></a> policy. For more details, see our <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15425104" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Tab compare</a> article in the Chrome Enterprise and Education help center.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Linux, macOS, Windows&nbsp;</strong></li>
    </ul>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/EOGmOTgHhdORaWZ6Aw7BrNbrv12hlC_cmvTYLK9jrbuxKDMS7TDrKsiTWz61OB3MuEtP=w620" width="620" height="547" alt="Tab compare" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/EOGmOTgHhdORaWZ6Aw7BrNbrv12hlC_cmvTYLK9jrbuxKDMS7TDrKsiTWz61OB3MuEtP"> &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB129" name="chromeBrsrB129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome no longer supports macOS 10.15&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome 129 no longer supports macOS 10.15, which is already outside of its support window with Apple. Users have to update their operating systems in order to continue running Chrome browser. Running on a supported operating system is essential to maintaining security. If run on macOS 10.15, Chrome continues to show an infobar that reminds users that Chrome 129 no longer supports macOS 10.15.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on macOS: </strong>Chrome no longer supports macOS 10.15</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC129" name="chromeBrsrC129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Ad-hoc code signatures for PWA shims on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Code signatures for application shims that are created when installing a Progressive Web App (PWA) on macOS are changing to use ad-hoc code signatures, which are created when the application is installed. The code signature is used by macOS as part of the application's identity. These ad-hoc signatures will result in each PWA shim having a unique identity to macOS; currently every PWA looks like the same application to macOS.</p>

    <p>This addresses problems when attempting to include multiple PWAs in the macOS <strong>Open at Login</strong> preference pane, and permits future improvements for handling user notifications within PWAs on macOS.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on macOS</strong></li>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrH129" name="chromeBrsrH129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New option in HttpsOnlyMode policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Ask Before HTTP (ABH), formerly named HTTPS Only/First Modes, is a setting that tells Chrome to ask for user consent before sending insecure HTTP content over the wire. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HttpsOnlyMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HttpsOnlyMode</u></a> policy allows force-enabling, or force-disabling, ABH.</p>

    <p>In Chrome 129, we are adding a new middle-ground variant of ABH called <em>balanced mode</em>. This variant aims to reduce user inconvenience by working like (strict) ABH most of the time, but not asking when Chrome knows that an HTTPS connection isn't possible, such as when connecting to a single-label hostname like internal/.</p>

    <p>We are adding a <em>force_balanced_enabled</em> policy option to allow force-enabling this new variant. Setting <em>force_balanced_enabled</em> on browsers before Chrome 129 will result in the default behavior, which places no enterprise restrictions on the ABH setting.</p>

    <p>To avoid unexpected impact, if you have previously set <em>force_enabled</em>, we recommend not setting <em>force_balanced_enabled</em> until your entire fleet has upgraded to Chrome 129 or higher. If you are not migrating from <em>force_enabled</em> to <em>force_balanced_enabled</em>, you will be unaffected by this change.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Android, ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrL129" name="chromeBrsrL129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate the includeShadowRoots argument on DOMParser&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The includeShadowRoots argument was a never-standardized argument to the DOMParser.parseFromString() function, which was there to allow imperative parsing of HTML content that contains declarative shadow DOM. This was shipped in<a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5191745052606464" rel="noopener" target="_blank"> Chrome 90</a> as part of the initial shipment of declarative shadow DOM. Since the standards discussion rematerialized in 2023, the shape of DSD APIs changed, including this feature for imperative parsing. To read more, see details of the <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5161240576393216" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>context on the related standards</u></a>, and information is also available on the related deprecations of <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5081733588582400" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>shadow DOM serialization </u></a>and <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/6239658726391808" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>shadow root attribute</u></a>.<br>
      Now that a standardized version of this API, in the form of <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/6560361081995264" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>setHTMLUnsafe() and parseHTMLUnsafe() </u></a>shipped in Chrome 124, the non-standard includeShadowRoots argument needs to be deprecated and removed. All usage should shift accordingly:<br>
      Instead of:<br>
      &nbsp; <code>(new DOMParser()).parseFromString(html,'text/html',{includeShadowRoots: true});</code><br>
      This can be used instead:<br>
      &nbsp; <code>document.parseHTMLUnsafe(html);</code></p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Linux, macOS, Windows, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrM129" name="chromeBrsrM129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecation of non-standard declarative shadow DOM serialization&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The prototype implementation, which was shipped in 2020 and then updated in 2023, contained a method called `getInnerHTML()` that could be used to serialize DOM trees containing shadow roots. That part of the prototype was not standardized with the rest of the declarative shadow DOM, and has only recently reached spec consensus (for details, see <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8867" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>). As part of that consensus, the shape of the getInnerHTML API changed.</p>

    <p>This feature represents the deprecation of the previously shipped `getInnerHTML()` method. The replacement is called `getHTML()`, which shipped in Chrome 125. For details, see this <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5102952270528512" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeStatus feature description</u></a>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrN129" name="chromeBrsrN129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Rename inset-area to position-area&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>The CSS working group (<a href="https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/css/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSSWG</u></a>) resolved to rename this property from `inset-area` to `position-area`. For more details, see the CSSWG discussion in <a href="https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/10209#issuecomment-2221005001" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>. Chrome will support both the old and new property names for a few milestones, to help developers migrate to the new position-area name. We are shipping the new property name, `position-area`, as a synonym for `inset-area` in Chrome 129 along with the deprecation DevTrial for `inset-area`.</p>

    <p>The `inset-area` property is currently planned for removal in Chrome 131.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

Meanwhile, if the Chromebook supports RGB, the <a href="https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/12313257" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Keyboard Settings page</u></a> will have a direct link to the Personalization Hub's RGB color selection options.</p>
  </li>

<p><a id="chromeOSK129" name="chromeOSK129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

  <li>
    <p><strong>Automatic reload of sign-in screen&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Starting from version 129, ChromeOS optimizes the support of 3P identity provider based logins. In the most common scenario, administrators show a permanent 3P identity provider login on the sign in screen. Many identity providers time out after a specific cadence, for example, 15 mins, leading to errors for the user. The new <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DeviceAuthenticationFlowAutoReloadInterval" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DeviceAuthenticationFlowAutoReloadInterval</u></a> policy allows for a repeated refresh of 3P identity providers on the login screen, avoids timeouts, and therefore significantly increases the reliability of 3P identity provider logins.</p>
  </li>

    <p><strong>CSE Workspace file types now supported in Google Drive&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Client side encryption (CSE) is a Google Workspace and Drive feature that allows customers and users to encrypt files with customer provided keys so that data is encrypted and never stored on our servers in the clear. This launch provides basic CSE support in the Files app on ChromeOS. This includes making CSE files visible, opening CSE files in the browser and flagging non Google Workspace CSE files as unsupported.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

    <p>We are launching an update to the battery icon to ensure that the battery state no longer covers the battery level. Now you can easily see how much battery you have left.</p>

  <div class="no-margin"><h2>Coming soon</h2>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> The items listed below are experimental or planned updates. They might change, be delayed, or canceled before launching to the Stable channel.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<h4>Upcoming Chrome browser updates</h4>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrB129" name="upChromeBrsrB129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Entrust certificate distrust&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>In response to sustained compliance failures, Chrome 127 changes how publicly-trusted TLS server authentication, that is, website or certificates issued by Entrust, are trusted by default. This applies to Chrome 127 and later on Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, and Linux; iOS policies do not allow use of the Chrome Root Store in Chrome for iOS.</p>

    <p>Specifically, TLS certificates validating to the Entrust root CA certificates included in the Chrome Root Store and issued:</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- after October 31, 2024, will no longer be trusted by default.</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- on or before October 31, 2024, will be unaffected by this change.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>If a Chrome user or an enterprise explicitly trusts any of the affected Entrust certificates on a platform and version of Chrome relying on the Chrome Root Store, for example, when explicit trust is conveyed through a Windows Group Policy Object, the Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT) constraints described above will be overridden and certificates will function as they do today.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For additional information and testing resources, see <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2024/06/sustaining-digital-certificate-security.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Sustaining Digital Certificate Security - Entrust Certificate Distrust.</u></a></p>

    <p>To learn more about the Chrome Root Store, see this <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/net/data/ssl/chrome_root_store/faq.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>FAQ</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 127 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: All versions of Chrome 127 and higher that rely on the Chrome Root Store will honor the blocking action, but the blocking action will only begin for certificates issued after October 31, 2024.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>The blocking action will begin for certificates issued after October 31, 2024. This will also affect Chrome 127, 128 and 129.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrC129" name="upChromeBrsrC129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Fallback styles for &lt;meter&gt; elements&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>As early as Chrome 130, <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/2011/WD-html5-author-20110809/the-meter-element.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HTML5 </u><u>&lt;meter&gt;</u><u> elements</u></a> with `appearance: none` will have a reasonable fallback style that matches Safari and Firefox instead of just disappearing from the page. In addition, developers will be able to custom style the &lt;meter&gt; elements.</p>

    <p>A temporary policy <strong>MeterAppearanceNoneFallbackStyle</strong> will be available until Chrome 133 to control this feature.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrD129" name="upChromeBrsrD129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Compression dictionary transport with Shared Brotli and Shared Zstandard&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>This feature adds support for using designated previous responses, as an external dictionary for <a href="https://github.com/google/brotli" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Brotli</u></a>- or Zstandard-compressing HTTP responses.</p>

    <p>Enterprises might experience potential compatibility issues with enterprise network infrastructure. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CompressionDictionaryTransportEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CompressionDictionaryTransportEnabled</u></a> policy is available to turn off the compression dictionary transport feature.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrE129" name="upChromeBrsrE129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Keyboard-focusable scroll containers&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Improves accessibility by making scroll containers focusable using sequential focus navigation. Today, the tab key doesn't focus scrollers unless tabIndex is explicitly set to 0 or more.</p>

    <p>By making scrollers focusable by default, users who can't (or don't want to) use a mouse will be able to focus clipped content using a keyboard's tab and arrow keys. This behavior is enabled only if the scroller does not contain any keyboard focusable children. This logic is necessary so we don't cause regressions for existing focusable elements that might exist within a scroller like a &lt;textarea&gt;.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrF129" name="upChromeBrsrF129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Support non-special scheme URLs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Chrome 130 will support <a href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>non-special scheme URLs</u></a>, for example, git://example.com/path, correctly. Previously, Chromium's URL parser didn't support non-special URLs. The parser parses non-special URLs as if they had an <em>opaque path</em>, which is not aligned with the URL Standard. Now, Chromium's URL parser parses non-special URLs correctly, following the URL Standard. For more details, see <a href="http://bit.ly/url-non-special" rel="noopener" target="_blank">http://bit.ly/url-non-special</a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrG129" name="upChromeBrsrG129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Simplified sign-in and sync experience&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 131, existing users with Chrome sync turned on will experience a simplified and consolidated version of sign-in and sync in Chrome. Chrome sync will no longer be shown as a separate feature in settings or elsewhere. Instead, users can sign in to Chrome to use and save information like passwords, bookmarks and more in their Google Account, subject to the relevant enterprise policies.</p>

    <p>As before, the functionality previously part of Chrome sync that saves and accesses Chrome data in the Google Account can be controlled by <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SyncTypesListDisabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SyncTypesListDisabled</u></a>. Sign-in to Chrome can be disabled via <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#BrowserSignin" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>BrowserSignin</u></a> as before.</p>

    <p>Note that the changes do not affect users’ ability to sign in to Google services on the web (like Gmail) without signing in to Chrome, their ability to stay signed out of Chrome, or their ability to control what information is synced with their Google Account.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrH129" name="upChromeBrsrH129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome extension telemetry integration with Google SecOps&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>We will begin to collect relevant <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/12325569" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chronicle extension telemetry</u></a> data from within Chrome, for managed profiles and devices, and send it to Google <a href="https://cloud.google.com/security/sec-ops?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SecOps</u></a>. Google SecOps will analyze the data to provide instant analysis and context on risky activity; this data is further enriched to provide additional context and is searchable for a year.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on ChromeOS, LaCrOS, Linux, macOS, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrI129" name="upChromeBrsrI129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>User Link capturing on PWAs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Web links automatically direct users to installed web apps. To better align with users' expectations around installed web apps, Chrome makes it easier to move between the browser and installed web apps. When the user clicks a link that could be handled by an installed web app, Chrome adds a chip in the address bar to suggest switching over to the app. When the user clicks the chip, this either launches the app directly, or opens a grid of apps that can support that link. Clicking a link always automatically opens the app.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 121 on Linux, macOS, Windows: When some users click a link, it always opens in an installed PWA, while some users see the link open in a new tab with a chip in the address bar, clicking on which will launch the app. A flag is available to control this feature: <code>chrome://flags/#enable-user-link-capturing-pwa</code>.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 131 on Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Launch to 100% of Stable with either a default on (always launch apps on link clicks) or a default off (always open in a tab, only launch if the user clicks on chip on address bar).</li>
    </ul>
    <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/IgSkHmN5UJD6lk3KE8NE56BaVnaEXlJ3DV4J8Xmpb0cvEmsyYOQF86z9IOSk-kltUQ=w838" width="838" height="473" alt="User Link on PWA" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/IgSkHmN5UJD6lk3KE8NE56BaVnaEXlJ3DV4J8Xmpb0cvEmsyYOQF86z9IOSk-kltUQ"></li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ129" name="upChromeBrsrJ129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome Third-Party Cookie Deprecation (3PCD)&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>On July 22nd, we announced a new path forward for Privacy Sandbox on the web. Instead of deprecating third-party cookies, we would introduce a new experience in Chrome that lets people make an informed choice that applies across their web browsing, and they’d be able to adjust that choice at any time. We're discussing this new path with regulators, and will engage with the industry as we roll this out.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For more details, see this <a href="https://privacysandbox.com/news/privacy-sandbox-update/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Privacy Sandbox update</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK129" name="upChromeBrsrK129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Insecure form warnings on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Chrome 125 started to block form submissions from secure pages to insecure pages on iOS. When Chrome detects an insecure form submission, it now displays a warning asking the user to confirm the submission. The goal is to prevent leaking of form data over plain text without user's explicit approval. A policy <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecureFormsWarningsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecureFormsWarningsEnabled</u></a> is available to control this feature, and will be removed in Chrome 130.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on iOS: Feature rolls out</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on iOS</strong>: <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#InsecureFormsWarningsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>InsecureFormsWarningsEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL129" name="upChromeBrsrL129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Remove enterprise policy used for legacy same site behavior&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>In Chrome 79, we introduced the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList</u></a> policy to revert the SameSite behavior of cookies to legacy behavior on the specified domains. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList</u></a> policy’s lifetime has been extended and will be removed on the milestone listed below.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 132 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, macOS, Windows: </strong>Remove <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>LegacySameSiteCookieBehaviorEnabledForDomainList</u></a> policy</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrM129" name="upChromeBrsrM129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>X25519Kyber768 key encapsulation for TLS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 124, Chrome enables by default on all desktop platforms a new post-quantum secure TLS key encapsulation mechanism X25519Kyber768, based on a NIST standard (ML-KEM). This protects network traffic from Chrome with servers that also support ML-KEM from decryption by a future quantum computer. This is exposed as a new TLS cipher suite. TLS automatically negotiates supported ciphers, so this change should be transparent to server operators. This cipher will be used for both TLS 1.3 and QUIC connections.</p>

    <p>However, some enterprise network devices such as firewalls and proxies (TLS middleboxes) might be unprepared for the size of a Kyber (ML-KEM) key encapsulation, or a new TLS ClientHello cipher code point, leading to dropped or hanging connections. This can be resolved by updating your middlebox, or disabling the key encapsulation mechanism via the temporary <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, which will be available through at least Chrome 141 in 2025. However, long term, post-quantum secure ciphers will be required in TLS and the enterprise policy will be removed. Post-quantum cryptography is required for CSNA 2.0.</p>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 131, Chrome will switch the key encapsulation mechanism from the draft version of Kyber, to the final standard version of ML-KEM. Using any form of post-quantum key exchange (Kyber or ML-KEM) will continue to be controlled by the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled</u></a> policy.</p>

    <p>For more detail, see this <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2023/08/protecting-chrome-traffic-with-hybrid.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium blog</u></a> post and this <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2024/08/post-quantum-cryptography-standards.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Google Security blog</u></a> post.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 124 on Windows, macOS, Linux</li>
      <li>Chrome 131</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrN129" name="upChromeBrsrN129"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome will start directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Administrators can use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, available from Chrome 125, to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 136, and will be removed in Chrome 137. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that administrators can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise administrators may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt-in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt-out through Chrome 136.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>
</div>

On these pages, IT administrators will be able to find reporting information on managed profiles such as profile details, browser versions, policies applied, and more.</p>

    <p>Starting with 130, we will change the default setting for GenAI policies from switched off to <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14443058?hl=en" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>allowed, without improving AI models</u></a>.     <p>The <strong>Custom configurations</strong> page was recently launched in Chrome 127 and it allows IT admins to configure Chrome policies that are not yet in the Admin console, using JSON scripts. <strong>As early as October 1st</strong>, Custom configurations will support applying settings at the user-level, in addition to machine-level support.   <div class="no-margin"><h2>Chrome browser updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrA128" name="chromeBrsrA128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Search your history in Chrome with AI&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 128, users can search their browsing history based on page contents and not just the page title and URL. Initially, this feature is only available to users in English in the US. Admins can control this feature by using the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HistorySearchSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HistorySearchSettings</u></a> policy. You have the following options for your organization:&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;0 = Enable the feature for users, and send relevant data to Google to help train or improve AI models. Relevant data may include prompts, inputs, outputs, and source materials, depending on the feature. It may be reviewed by humans for the sole purpose of improving AI models.</li>
      <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;1 = Enable the feature for users, but do not send data to Google to train or improve AI models.</li>
      <li>&nbsp;&nbsp;2 = Fully disable feature</li>
    </ul>

    <p>For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/15248971" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Search your history in Chrome with AI</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 128 on Linux, Mac, Windows&nbsp;</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrB128" name="chromeBrsrB128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Admin-configurable site search&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Site search shortcuts are a way to use the address bar (Omnibox) as a search box for a specific site without navigating directly to the site’s URL, similar to how you can use the Omnibox to perform a broad Google search of the web. You can now create site shortcuts on behalf of your managed users, to shortcut to the most critical enterprise sites. You can control this feature using the&nbsp;<a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#SiteSearchSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>SiteSearchSettings</u></a> policy.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 128 on ChromeOS, Linux, Mac, Windows: </strong>Available for <strong>Chrome Browser Core</strong> customers signed up for Trusted Tester starting Chrome 128, followed by gradual rollout for all <strong>Chrome Browser Enterprise</strong> customers a few weeks later</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3CO1ViWs6hWHyXHtJanuelLaxLSagf4QXpozZUkkaQNfnB__3cktkkaM0OZ_52qOs_0=w843" width="843" height="586" alt="Admin search" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3CO1ViWs6hWHyXHtJanuelLaxLSagf4QXpozZUkkaQNfnB__3cktkkaM0OZ_52qOs_0"><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/Mb_fPCUZ6UdrEAU28IJkFQOSjyZ99yL7_hkogG715-_huk8nhoj4WDrl_GF-nWJVyQ=w895" width="927" height="695" alt="Admin search" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/Mb_fPCUZ6UdrEAU28IJkFQOSjyZ99yL7_hkogG715-_huk8nhoj4WDrl_GF-nWJVyQ"></p>
  </li>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrC128" name="chromeBrsrC128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Handling undecryptable passwords in Password Manager&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Users sometimes end up with undecryptable passwords on their device, for example, if they've used third party software to move to a new device. We are launching a new policy called <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DeletingUndecryptablePasswordsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DeletingUndecryptablePasswordsEnabled</u></a> that helps handle such passwords. When enabled, this policy deletes undecryptable passwords from the user's device, unless the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UserDataDir" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UserDataDir</u></a> policy is specified. When <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DeletingUndecryptablePasswordsEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DeletingUndecryptablePasswordsEnabled</u></a> is off, undecryptable passwords are untouched, but this will result in broken Password Manager functionality.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 128 on iOS, Linux, Mac, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrD128" name="chromeBrsrD128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Inactive tabs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>In Chrome 128, we now hide old tabs under a new <strong>Inactive Tabs</strong> section in the tab switcher on Chrome on Android. Chrome users can access the <strong>Inactive Tabs</strong> section to view all old tabs or close them using the new bulk tab functionality. These tabs will be deleted if inactive for over 60 days.&nbsp;</p>

  <li><strong>Revamped Chrome Safety Check on Android&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Chrome 128 introduces&nbsp; a new proactive Safety Check that regularly checks the browser for safety-related issues and informs users when there's anything that needs their attention. This launch also introduces a re-designed <strong>Safety Check</strong> page, <code>chrome://settings/safetyCheck</code>, with Chrome’s proactive safety-related actions and information tailored to each user, designed to make it easier for users to stay safe online. <p><a id="chromeBrsrG128" name="chromeBrsrG128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Rust JSON Parser&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>As early as Chrome 128, Chrome will parse JSON using Rust, rather than C++. This will remove the risk of memory safety vulnerabilities in the JSON parser, improving security. This change should be transparent to users. There is a small risk of certain invalid JSON, which Chrome currently accepts, no longer being accepted, although the Rust parser remains extremely lenient.</p>

    <p>In the event that Chrome doesn't accept the invalid JSON, this will lead to 500s or other application-level errors, not crashes. If Chrome no longer accepts some invalid JSON, the JSON should be aimed to be fixed.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 128</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrI128" name="chromeBrsrI128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Updates for CookiePartitionKey of partitioned cookies&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Chrome 128 adds a cross-site ancestor bit to the keying of the partitioned cookie's CookiePartitionKey. This change unifies the partition key with the partition key values used in storage partitioning and adds protection against clickjacking attacks by preventing cross-site embedded frames from having access to the top-level-site's partitioned cookies.</p>

    <p>If an enterprise experiences any breakage with embedded iframes, they can use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CookiesAllowedForUrls" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CookiesAllowedForUrls</u></a> policy or use SameSite=None cookies without the Partitioned attribute and then invoke the Storage Access API (SAA) to ensure that embedded iframes have access to the same cookies as the top level domain.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 128 on Windows, Mac, Linux</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrJ128" name="chromeBrsrJ128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate CHIPS and relaunch in WebView&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>The WebViewClient supports a method, <code>shouldInterceptRequest</code>, which allows developers to intercept network activity and modify HTTP headers, etc. This API does not have access to the Cookie header and relies on the Android CookieManager API in order to query what cookies are available for a particular request URL. However, partitioned cookies are double-keyed on the top-level site and the site of the URL using the cookies.</p>

    <p>Currently, the CookieManager API provides no way for developers to query partitioned cookies correctly, and this will cause a mismatch between what the Java API returns and what frames in WebView will actually be in their Cookie header. After discussing this with the WebView team, we believe that the option that will minimize potential app breakage is to disable Cookies Having Independent Partitioned State (<a href="https://developers.google.com/privacy-sandbox/cookies/chips" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CHIPS</u></a>) on WebView until we are able to ship support for the Cookie header to <code>shouldInterceptRequest</code>. We will release the changes to <code>shouldInterceptRequest</code> in the next target SDK version (API level 36).</p>

    <p>Enterprise workflows that use WebView to load web content that relies on partitioned cookies will have their state cleared. WebView apps still have access to unpartitioned 3P cookies and cookies set with Partitioned after the change will revert to their legacy pre-CHIPS behavior until we relaunch the feature.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 128 on Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrK128" name="chromeBrsrK128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Isolated Web Apps&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Isolated Web Apps (IWAs) are an extension of existing work on PWA installation and Web Packaging that provides stronger protections against server compromise and other tampering, which is necessary for developers of security-sensitive applications.</p>

    <p>Rather than being hosted on live web servers and fetched over HTTPS, these IWAs are packaged into Web Bundles, signed by their developer, and distributed to end-users through one or more of the potential methods described in the Chromium project <a href="https://www.chromium.org/blink/launching-features/isolated-web-apps/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>explainer</u></a>.</p>

    <p>In this initial release, IWAs are only installable using a new policy, <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#IsolatedWebAppInstallForceList" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>IsolatedWebAppInstallForceList</u></a>, on enterprise-managed ChromeOS devices.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 128 on ChromeOS</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrL128" name="chromeBrsrL128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Rename position-try-options to position-try-fallbacks&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>The CSS working group (<a href="https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/css/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSSWG</u></a>) resolved to rename this property, because fallbacks more accurately describe what this property controls. The word <em>options</em> is a bit unclear, since the styles outside of `position-try` blocks will be tested first, and if they result in a layout that fits within the containing block, none of the options will get used. So <em>fallbacks</em> is a better word to describe this behavior. For more details, see <a href="https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/10395#issuecomment-2192127524" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 128 on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeBrsrM128" name="chromeBrsrM128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>

    <p>Enterprise users can now access their upcoming meetings directly from the <strong>New tab</strong> page with the new calendar card.
