  <div class="no-margin"><h2>ChromeOS updates</h2>

<p><a id="chromeOSA128" name="chromeOSA128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Snap groups on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 128, <strong>Snap groups</strong> allow you to group windows on ChromeOS. A snap group is formed when you pair two windows for a split-screen. You can bring the windows&nbsp;back together, resize them simultaneously, or move them both as a group.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/gG9C_J7feNzYtmaDj1mP8IyQAdDkl1SCAT1tiXbJEfM6MMmK2FL-1cBqKtXv_GrAhAjC=w512" width="512" height="341" alt="snap groups" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/gif" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/gG9C_J7feNzYtmaDj1mP8IyQAdDkl1SCAT1tiXbJEfM6MMmK2FL-1cBqKtXv_GrAhAjC"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSB128" name="chromeOSB128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Data processor mode: EU-wide rollout&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>New data processor mode features and ChromeOS terms are available to the entire EU through the Google Admin console. For more details, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14316192" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Overview of ChromeOS data processor mode</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>As a ChromeOS administrator, you can now activate <strong>Data processor mode</strong>, which covers&nbsp; a set of ChromeOS features and services referred to as <strong>Essential Services</strong>.&nbsp;</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSC128" name="chromeOSC128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Privacy controls: Geolocation&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Privacy on ChromeOS devices is now easier to manage by adding the ability to control geolocation access to the <strong>Settings &gt; Privacy and security &gt; Privacy controls</strong> page. Users can now set geolocation access to <strong>Allowed</strong>, <strong>Only allowed for system services</strong>, or <strong>Off</strong>, depending on their preference.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>We allow users to block all apps or websites, or entire systems access to geolocation regardless of previously granted permissions, and provide users easy to use controls to re-enable them whenever it would be helpful.</p>

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3auDEYfZ6zlqRP7ViKYR280fu_y-_iTrgCXks8T6Gkrr2oxFNlmhJwfmuoeRDaRTZw=w782" width="782" height="678" alt="geolocation" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3auDEYfZ6zlqRP7ViKYR280fu_y-_iTrgCXks8T6Gkrr2oxFNlmhJwfmuoeRDaRTZw"></p>
    &nbsp;

    <p>We’ve added a new policy,&nbsp; <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GoogleLocationServicesEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GoogleLocationServicesEnabled</u></a>. This controls the availability of geolocation on the device inside of user sessions. Unlike the now deprecated policy below, it affects the entire system, not just the Android VM (Arc).</p>

    <p>Deprecation notice (6 months): <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ArcGoogleLocationServicesEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ArcGoogleLocationServicesEnabled</u></a>&nbsp;</p>

    <p>This is being deprecated in favor of the added <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#GoogleLocationServicesEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>GoogleLocationServicesEnabled</u></a> policy, as it covers the entire system and not just Android VM (Arc). Additionally, we are modifying the effect of the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DefaultGeolocationSetting" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>DefaultGeolocationSetting</u></a> to no longer affect the system geolocation setting.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSD128" name="chromeOSD128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS privacy control reminders on Apps settings page&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>To use the cameras and microphones on ChromeOS, you need to turn on both privacy controls and app permissions in two separate places.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>We are making it easier for users to be aware of the states of the privacy controls and provide actionable reminders on the ChromeOS <strong>Apps</strong> settings page so that users have a smoother experience. To view the ChromeOS <strong>Apps</strong> settings page, click <strong>Settings &gt;Apps &gt; Manage your Apps</strong>, and select the desired app.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/EGf6mjHNV90v6JtGr_m0-owKva93KF-RaPXDXYDC1wWVGju103dPqTulLeN_LqXvwgY=w895" width="1532" height="862" alt="App settings" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/gif" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/EGf6mjHNV90v6JtGr_m0-owKva93KF-RaPXDXYDC1wWVGju103dPqTulLeN_LqXvwgY"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSE128" name="chromeOSE128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Store aggregated vitals data with one-year retention&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>From ChromeOS 128 onwards, we store aggregated vitals data for one-year retention to better track the progress over time. Vitals data includes Android app performance metrics, such as crash rate, and these metrics will help us improve Android app performance on ChromeOS devices.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSF128" name="chromeOSF128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>OCR in ChromeOS Camera App&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Optical Character Recognition (OCR) enables text extraction from images captured in the ChromeOS Camera App by integrating an ML-powered text extraction service. ChromeOS 128 supports 77 languages; it also supports both horizontal and vertical detection. This allows copying and searching text from images, speaking text from images by screen reader, and creating searchable PDFs from images. By default, text detection in Photo mode is disabled and can be enabled from <strong>Settings &gt; Text detection in preview</strong>.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/I-oVDHUNlXa7IAWByH0h-WBEQrdneaZUpy4TrvbZ9sAFWMPqz4HY2-0YipQBN3kh3XJM=w876" width="876" height="550" alt="OCR camera app" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/I-oVDHUNlXa7IAWByH0h-WBEQrdneaZUpy4TrvbZ9sAFWMPqz4HY2-0YipQBN3kh3XJM"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSG128" name="chromeOSG128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Magnifier follows ChromeVox&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Magnifier following ChromeVox is designed for people who are blind or have low vision. When you read text aloud using ChromeVox, the screen magnifier now automatically follows the words, so you never lose your place. To try this out, you can enable both Magnifier and ChromeVox in your settings. Zoom in to your preferred zoom level using <strong>Ctrl + Alt + Brightness up</strong> and <strong>Ctrl + Alt + Brightness down</strong>. A setting is available under the Magnifier settings to adjust this behavior.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSH128" name="chromeOSH128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Auto Gain Control enabled by default&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>Auto Gain Control (AGC) allows apps, such as video calling apps, to automatically optimize microphone volume for best audio quality. When auto gain control is enabled and in-use, a message appears in the quick settings panel to inform the user that the microphone gain slider is being overridden. AGC is enabled by default in ChromeOS 128. If you want to manually control the microphone volume even for apps that support AGC, you can go to <strong>Settings &gt; Device &gt; Audio</strong> and deselect <strong>Allow apps to automatically adjust mic volume</strong>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/11Qvs33PqUo0lRx4Q9YFA0HrrzCwMbK6hI4D7ZSQj3nxxp_e0pvMW3QqLX-6cxrak_g=w708" width="708" height="822" alt="AGC audio" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/11Qvs33PqUo0lRx4Q9YFA0HrrzCwMbK6hI4D7ZSQj3nxxp_e0pvMW3QqLX-6cxrak_g"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>

<p><a id="chromeOSI128" name="chromeOSI128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>

    <p>For ChromeOS cellular-enabled devices, we have made it easier to view, manage, and add Access Point Names (APNs). We’ve also improved registration failure handling and messaging.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="chromeOSJ128" name="chromeOSJ128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Pinned notifications on ChromeOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a></p>

    <p>ChromeOS notifications help to visually separate pinned notifications from other notifications. ChromeOS 128 significantly differentiates the visual look of pinned notifications from typical notifications to reflect their significant difference - we notify the user of an ongoing process rather than an instantaneous event.</p>

<h4>Upcoming Chrome browser updates</h4>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrA128" name="upChromeBrsrA128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Tab compare&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 129 (US-only), we will introduce <strong>Tab compare</strong>, a new feature that presents an AI-generated overview of products from across multiple tabs, all in one place. This feature will be controlled through the <strong>TabCompareSettings</strong> policy.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Linux, Mac, Windows&nbsp;</strong></li>
    </ul>

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/N_kQVFWH2xu_SCHft4NHFPNjWHyRpA6Z359xQHK0Q6Euq_NLvFJ8nPYwqFCNjNLzxA=w812" width="812" height="725" alt="tab compare" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/N_kQVFWH2xu_SCHft4NHFPNjWHyRpA6Z359xQHK0Q6Euq_NLvFJ8nPYwqFCNjNLzxA"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrB128" name="upChromeBrsrB128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Ad-hoc code signatures for PWA shims on macOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Code signatures for application shims that are created when installing a Progressive Web App (PWA) on macOS are changing to use ad-hoc code signatures, which are created when the application is installed. The code signature is used by macOS as part of the application's identity. These ad-hoc signatures will result in each PWA shim having a unique identity to macOS; currently every PWA looks like the same application to macOS.</p>

    <p>This will address problems when attempting to include multiple PWAs in the macOS <strong>Open at Login</strong> preference pane, and will permit future improvements for handling user notifications within PWAs on macOS.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Mac</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrC128" name="upChromeBrsrC128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Clear device data on sign out on iOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 129, signing out from a managed account in an unmanaged browser will delete browsing data that is saved on the device. Managed users will be presented a confirmation dialog on sign-out explaining that the data will be cleared. Data will be cleared only from the time of sign-in, otherwise all data will be cleared; time of sign-in is only known if the user signed in on Chrome 122 or later.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>The data that will be deleted includes:&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li>browsing history</li>
      <li>cookies and site data</li>
      <li>passwords</li>
      <li>site settings</li>
      <li>autofill</li>
      <li>cached images and files</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on iOS</strong></li>
    </ul>

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/b0rIw-ALOH6bMWwnK7_RwuodsfR6RGnxfz5tBpHOHLuDz1dyFunrGqhfACzb7tHq1Sw=w345" width="345" height="756" alt="delete user data" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/b0rIw-ALOH6bMWwnK7_RwuodsfR6RGnxfz5tBpHOHLuDz1dyFunrGqhfACzb7tHq1Sw"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrD128" name="upChromeBrsrD128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Fallback styles for HTML5 &lt;meter&gt; elements&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>As early as Chrome 129, <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/2011/WD-html5-author-20110809/the-meter-element.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HTML5 </u><u>&lt;meter&gt;</u><u> elements</u></a> with `appearance: none` will have a reasonable fallback style that matches Safari and Firefox instead of just disappearing from the page. In addition,&nbsp; developers will be able to custom style the &lt;meter&gt; elements.</p>

    <p>A temporary policy <strong>MeterAppearanceNoneFallbackStyle</strong> will be available until Chrome 133 to control this feature.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>

    <p>Chrome will no longer support macOS 10.15, which is already outside of its support window with Apple. Users have to update their operating systems in order to continue running Chrome browser. Running on a supported operating system is essential to maintaining security. If run on macOS 10.15, Chrome continues to show an infobar that reminds users that Chrome 129 will no longer support macOS 10.15.</p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrF128" name="upChromeBrsrF128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate Safe Browsing Extended reporting&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p><strong>Safe Browsing Extended</strong> reporting is a feature that enhances the security of all users by collecting telemetry information from participating users that is used for Google Safe Browsing protections. The data collected includes URLs of visited web pages, limited system information, and some page content. However, this feature is now superseded by <strong>Enhanced protection </strong>mode. We suggest users switch to <strong>Enhanced protection</strong> to continue providing security for all users in addition to enabling the strongest security available in Chrome. For more information, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/9890866?visit_id=638471471514766310-2859664582&amp;p=safe_browsing_preferences&amp;rd=1" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Safe Browsing protection levels</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/Xo02o6G_lLHuiWAqLOL9Pc3ckaqJmIS9UVfOGwcXTQE31urCMwLZhvaEYvmcrJMLZ3oL=w576" width="576" height="792" alt="safe browsing" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/Xo02o6G_lLHuiWAqLOL9Pc3ckaqJmIS9UVfOGwcXTQE31urCMwLZhvaEYvmcrJMLZ3oL"></p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Android, iOS, ChromeOS, Linux, Mac, Windows: </strong>Deprecation of Safe Browsing Extended Reporting</li>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrGG128" name="upChromeBrsrGG128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Certificate Manager on Windows and MacOS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>As early as Chrome 129, there is a new certificate management settings screen accessible from security settings on Windows and MacOS. This replaces the link to Windows cert manager and MacOS keychain, respectively, although these operating system surfaces are still accessible from the certificate management settings page.</p>

    <p>The certificate manager displays certificates that are trusted or distrusted by Chrome, including the contents of the Chrome Root Store, and any certificates that have been imported from the underlying operating system. Users can access the page directly by navigating to <code>chrome://certificate-manager</code>.</p>

    <p>A future release will introduce user and enterprise management of certificates added directly to Chrome.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Mac, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrG128" name="upChromeBrsrG128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>New option in HttpsOnlyMode policy&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Ask Before HTTP (ABH) , formerly named HTTPS Only/First Modes, is a setting that tells Chrome to ask for user consent before sending insecure HTTP content over the wire. The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HttpsOnlyMode" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>HttpsOnlyMode</u></a> policy allows force-enabling, or force-disabling, ABH.</p>

    <p>In Chrome 129, we are adding a new middle-ground variant of ABH called <em>balanced mode</em>. This variant aims to reduce user inconvenience by working like (strict) ABH most of the time, but not asking when Chrome knows that an HTTPS connection isn't possible, such as when connecting to a single-label hostname like internal/.</p>

    <p>We are adding a <em>force_balanced_enabled</em> policy option to allow force-enabling this new variant. Setting <em>force_balanced_enabled</em> on browsers before Chrome 129 will result in the default behavior, which places no enterprise restrictions on the ABH setting.</p>

    <p>To avoid unexpected impact, if you have previously set <em>force_enabled</em>, we recommend not setting <em>force_balanced_enabled</em> until your entire fleet has upgraded to Chrome 129 or higher. If you are not migrating from <em>force_enabled</em> to <em>force_balanced_enabled</em>, you will be unaffected by this change.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, Mac, Windows, Fuchsia</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrJ128" name="upChromeBrsrJ128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate of non-standard declarative shadow DOM serialization&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>The prototype implementation, which was shipped in 2020 and then updated in 2023, contained a method called `<code>getInnerHTML()</code>` that could be used to serialize DOM trees containing shadow roots. That part of the prototype was not standardized with the rest of the declarative shadow DOM, and has only recently reached spec consensus (for details, see <a href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8867" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>). As part of that consensus, the shape of the <code>getInnerHTML</code> API changed.</p>

    <p>This feature represents the deprecation of the previously shipped `<code>getInnerHTML()</code>` method. The replacement is called `<code>getHTML()</code>`, which shipped in Chrome 125. For details, see this <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5102952270528512" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>ChromeStatus feature description</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrK128" name="upChromeBrsrK128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Deprecate the includeShadowRoots argument on DOMParser&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>The <code>includeShadowRoots</code> argument was a never-standardized argument to the <code>DOMParser.parseFromString()</code> function, which was there to allow imperative parsing of HTML content that contains declarative shadow DOM. This was shipped in<a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5191745052606464" rel="noopener" target="_blank"> Chrome 90</a> as part of the initial shipment of declarative shadow DOM. Since the standards discussion rematerialized in 2023, the shape of DSD APIs changed, including this feature for imperative parsing. To read more, see details of the <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5161240576393216" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>context on the related standards</u></a>, and information is also available on the related deprecations of <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5081733588582400" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>shadow DOM serialization </u></a>and <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/6239658726391808" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>shadow root attribute</u></a>.<br>
      Now that a standardized version of this API, in the form of <a href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/6560361081995264" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>setHTMLUnsafe() and parseHTMLUnsafe() </u></a>shipped in Chrome 124, the non-standard <code>includeShadowRoots</code> argument needs to be deprecated and removed. All usage should shift accordingly:<br>
      Instead of:<br>
      &nbsp; <code>(new DOMParser()).parseFromString(html,'text/html',{includeShadowRoots: true});</code><br>
      This can be used instead:<br>
      &nbsp; <code>document.parseHTMLUnsafe(html);</code></p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Linux, Mac, Windows, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrL128" name="upChromeBrsrL128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Rename inset-area to position-area&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>The CSS working group (<a href="https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/css/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>CSSWG</u></a>) resolved to rename this property from `<code>inset-area</code>` to `<code>position-area</code>`. See the CSSWG discussion in <a href="https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/10209#issuecomment-2221005001" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Github</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Chrome has decided to release an interoperable solution, by supporting both property names. We will ship the new property name, `<code>position-area</code>`, as a synonym for `<code>inset-area</code>` first. Then after a suitable amount of time, we will remove `<code>inset-area</code>`. The latter removal will be done under a separate Intent.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 129 on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Entrust certificate distrust&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>In response to sustained compliance failures, Chrome 127 changes how publicly-trusted TLS server authentication, that is, websites or certificates issued by Entrust, are trusted by default. This applies to Chrome 127 and later on Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, and Linux; iOS policies do not allow use of the Chrome Root Store in Chrome for iOS.</p>

    <p>Specifically, TLS certificates validating to the Entrust root CA certificates included in the Chrome Root Store and issued:</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- after October 31, 2024, will no longer be trusted by default.</p>

    <p>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- on or before October 31, 2024, will be unaffected by this change.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>If a Chrome user or an enterprise explicitly trusts any of the affected Entrust certificates on a platform and version of Chrome relying on the Chrome Root Store, for example, when explicit trust is conveyed through a Windows Group Policy Object, the Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT) constraints described above will be overridden and certificates will function as they do today.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For additional information and testing resources, see <a href="https://security.googleblog.com/2024/06/sustaining-digital-certificate-security.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Sustaining Digital Certificate Security - Entrust Certificate Distrust.</u></a></p>

    <p>To learn more about the Chrome Root Store, see this <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/net/data/ssl/chrome_root_store/faq.md" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>FAQ</u></a>.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 127 on Android, ChromeOS, Linux, Mac, Windows: All versions of Chrome 127 and higher that rely on the Chrome Root Store will honor the blocking action, but the blocking action will only begin for certificates issued after October 31, 2024.</li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on ChromeOS, Linux, Mac, Windows: </strong>The blocking action will begin for certificates issued after October 31, 2024. This will also affect Chrome 127, 128 and 129.</li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

  <li><strong>User Link capturing on PWAs&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Web links automatically direct users to installed web apps. To better align with users' expectations around installed web apps, Chrome makes it easier to move between the browser and installed web apps. When the user clicks a link that could be handled by an installed web app, Chrome adds a chip in the address bar to suggest switching over to the app. When the user clicks the chip, this either launches the app directly, or opens a grid of apps that can support that link. For some users, clicking a link always automatically opens the app.</p>

      <li>Chrome 121 on Linux, Mac, Windows: When some users click a link, it always opens in an installed PWA, while some users see the link open in a new tab with a chip in the address bar, clicking on which will launch the app. A flag is available to control this feature: chrome://flags/#enable-user-link-capturing-pwa.</li>
    </ul>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Linux, Mac, Windows: </strong>Launch to 100% of Stable with either a default on (always launch apps on link clicks) or a default off (always open in a tab, only launch if the user clicks on chip on address bar).</li>
    </ul>

    <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong><strong><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/YGeRa7eoXluiQkV0lBBe1BF6n5R_lR6ZqWpS2CE_IdFjRa-A-A6e7WujpZu4rfOgdgz2=w895" width="1477" height="837" alt="PWA links" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/YGeRa7eoXluiQkV0lBBe1BF6n5R_lR6ZqWpS2CE_IdFjRa-A-A6e7WujpZu4rfOgdgz2"></strong></p>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrR128" name="upChromeBrsrR128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Private network access checks for navigation requests: warning-only mode&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Before a website A navigates to another site B in the user's private network, this feature does the following:</p>

    <p>1. Checks whether the request has been initiated from a secure context.</p>

    <p>2. Sends a preflight request, and checks whether B responds with a header that allows private network access.</p>

    <p>There are already features for subresources and workers, but this one is for navigation requests specifically. These checks protect the user's private network.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Since this feature is the <em>warning-only</em> mode, we do not fail the requests if any of the checks fail. Instead, a warning will be shown in the DevTools console, to help developers prepare for the coming enforcement.</p>

      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android</strong></li>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrV128" name="upChromeBrsrV128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>X25519Kyber768 key encapsulation for TLS&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 124, Chrome enables by default on all desktop platforms a new post-quantum secure TLS key encapsulation mechanism X25519Kyber768, based on a NIST standard (ML-KEM). This protects network traffic from Chrome with servers that also support ML-KEM from decryption by a future quantum computer. This is exposed as a new TLS cipher suite. TLS automatically negotiates supported ciphers, so this change should be transparent to server operators. This cipher will be used for both TLS 1.3 and QUIC connections.</p>

    <p>However, some TLS middleboxes might be unprepared for the size of a Kyber (ML-KEM) key encapsulation, or a new TLS ClientHello cipher code point, leading to dropped or hanging connections. This can be resolved by updating your middlebox, or disabling the key encapsulation mechanism via the temporary <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, which will be available through the end of 2024. However, long term, post-quantum secure ciphers will be required in TLS and the enterprise policy will be removed. Post-quantum cryptography is required for CSNA 2.0.</p>

    <p>For more detail, see this <a href="https://blog.chromium.org/2023/08/protecting-chrome-traffic-with-hybrid.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>Chromium blog</u></a> post.</p>

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 124 on Windows, Mac, Linux</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 135 on Android</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;<a id="upChromeBrsrW128" name="upChromeBrsrW128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>UI Automation accessibility framework provider on Windows&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong>

    <p>Starting in Chrome 126, Chrome will start directly supporting accessibility client software that uses Microsoft Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Prior to this change, such software interoperated with Chrome by way of a compatibility shim in Microsoft Windows. This change is being made to improve the accessible user experience for many users. It provides complete support for Narrator, Magnifier, and Voice Access; and will improve third-party apps that use Windows's UI Automation accessibility framework. Users of Chrome will find reduced memory usage and processing overhead when used with accessibility tools. It will also ease development of software using assistive technologies.</p>

    <p>Administrators might use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> enterprise policy, available from Chrome 125, to either force-enable the new provider (so that all users receive the new functionality), or disable the new provider. This policy will be supported through Chrome 136, and will be removed in Chrome 137. This one-year period is intended to give enterprises sufficient time to work with third-party vendors so that they may fix any incompatibilities resulting from the switch from Microsoft's compatibility shim to Chrome's UI Automation provider.</p>
    &nbsp;

    <ul>
      <li>Chrome 125 on Windows:The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy is introduced so that administrators can enable Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider and validate that third-party accessibility tools continue to work.</li>
      <li>Chrome 126 on Windows: The Chrome variations framework will be used to begin enabling Chrome's UI Automation accessibility framework provider for users. It will be progressively enabled to the full stable population, with pauses as needed to address compatibility issues that can be resolved in Chrome. Enterprise administrators may continue to use the <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy to either opt-in early to the new behavior, or to temporarily opt-out through Chrome 136.</li>
      <li><strong>Chrome 137 on Windows: </strong>The <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#UiAutomationProviderEnabled" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u>UiAutomationProviderEnabled</u></a> policy will be removed from Chrome. All clients will use the browser's UI Automation accessibility framework provider.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>
</div>

  <div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming ChromeOS changes</h4>

<p><a id="upChromeOSA128" name="upChromeOSA128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Update to keyboard shortcut for Select-to-speak&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>On Chromebooks, the Select-to-speak keyboard shortcut (Search + s) now works when it is first pressed. As early as ChromeOS 129, you will no longer need to enable it first in <strong>Settings &gt; Accessibility &gt; Text-to-Speech &gt; Select-to-speak</strong>. A dialog appears confirming that you want to turn on Select-to-speak the first time you press the keyboard shortcut.&nbsp;</p>
    &nbsp;

    <p><img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/gKyEQPQDFpQ5tINGpjhJRbakmPYiWBxeaHsY-bDLwNDVdMJxpMcyxISe0gNoWVxEw9Y=w895" width="1207" height="808" alt="text to speak" class="screenshot" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/gKyEQPQDFpQ5tINGpjhJRbakmPYiWBxeaHsY-bDLwNDVdMJxpMcyxISe0gNoWVxEw9Y"></p>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSB128" name="upChromeOSB128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Chrome Enterprise Premium for file transfers on Managed Guest Sessions&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 129, organizations will be able to extend Chrome Enterprise Premium’s powerful scanning and content and context-based protection to local files on ChromeOS on Managed Guest Sessions.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>For example, a misplaced file containing Social Security numbers is instantly blocked when a user attempts to copy it to an external drive, safeguarding this confidential information.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSC128" name="upChromeOSC128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ChromeOS XDR Window Events&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>In ChromeOS 130, window focus events will be available as part of Extended Threat Detection and Response (XDR) on ChromeOS. You will be able to bring windows into focus activities of devices in your managed fleet by simply updating XDR events in the Admin console!</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upChromeOSD128" name="upChromeOSD128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Generative AI wallpapers and video conference backgrounds&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>

    <p>As early as ChromeOS 130, we plan to introduce high-resolution, generative AI wallpapers and video-conference meeting backgrounds on ChromeOS. With this feature, you can unleash your creativity and turn your Chromebook into a canvas of personal expression. Choose from a diverse collection of templates and, in just a few clicks, infuse your Chromebook with your unique personality, mood, or interest.&nbsp;</p>

    <p>Two new policies will be available to control these features; <strong>GenAIVcBackgroundSettings</strong> and <strong>GenAIWallpaperSettings</strong>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>&nbsp;</p>
</div>

  <div class="no-margin"><h4>Upcoming Admin console changes</h4>

<p><a id="upAdminConA128" name="upAdminConA128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Chrome browser managed profile reporting&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Chrome Enterprise Core will introduce new Chrome browser managed profile reporting in the Admin console. This feature will provide a new Managed profile listing and detail pages. On these pages, IT administrators will be able to find reporting information on managed profiles such as profile details, browser versions, policies applied, and more.</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome 130 on Android, Linux, Mac, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upAdminConB128" name="upAdminConB128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Admin console widget for data controls&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>A new settings widget in the Admin console allows users to configure data controls policies for specific URLs.&nbsp;</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Chrome</strong><strong> 128 on ChromeOS, Linux, Mac, Windows</strong></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>

<p><a id="upAdminConC128" name="upAdminConC128"></a>&nbsp; &nbsp;</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Default change for GenAI policies&nbsp;</strong><a href="#top"><img src="//storage.googleapis.com/support-kms-prod/875e9907-0d60-4f4e-a960-862bc24a29f4" height="18" alt="back to top" data-mime-type="image/svg+xml"></a>

    <p>Starting with 130, we will change the default setting for GenAI policies from switched off to allowed, without improving AI models. This doesn't impact age restrictions on access to any relevant GenAI features. The existing policies that will have the updated default setting are:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#CreateThemesSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank">CreateThemesSettings</a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DevToolsGenAiSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank">DevToolsGenAiSettings</a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HelpMeWriteSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank">HelpMeWriteSettings</a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#HistorySearchSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank">HistorySearchSettings</a></li>
      <li><a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TabOrganizerSettings" rel="noopener" target="_blank">TabOrganizerSettings</a></li>
    </ul>
    &nbsp;</li>
</ul>
</div>

  <p class="align-right"><a href="#top">↑ back to top</a> &nbsp;</p>
